name: Board setup
job: Board rules for every component on this board. Send first; draws nothing.
attach: none. Nothing here has shipped. Tokens, type scale and base icons come from the published Pantopus design system.
text:
SETUP 00a-00. Foundations board 00a: Marks, captions and chips. Draw nothing yet.

Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is the Foundations board 00a.
TYPE: NEW (a component specimen board).
ATTACH: none. Nothing here has shipped. Tokens, type scale and base icons come from the published Pantopus design system.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
The first design work for Pantopus, before any screen. It draws nine components once, precisely, with every variant and state: ProvenanceMark · SourceCaption · ScopeChip · FreshnessLine · OfflineNotice · StatusChip · KindGlyph · AddressChip · ChoiceChip. Every later screen is designed in a separate project with no memory of this one and uses these exact names, so label everything with its name, keys (B12) and tokens.

HOW THIS PROJECT RUNS
- The board rules (B1–B17) and the Notes rules below apply to every artboard in this project.
- Next, I send one component message per turn, in order. Each one opens with "Component 00a-NN: <Name>." and carries that component's specification, its ARTBOARDS list and its BATCH PLAN.
- A long component arrives in parts (for example 00a-NNa, then 00a-NNb). A part message takes the place of "continue" and carries the specification for the next batch. Specifications from earlier parts of the same component still apply.
- Draw only the current batch (at most 6 artboards), in the listed order. Then stop and wait for "continue", the next part or the next component message. If a batch will not fit, finish the artboards in order and say which ones moved to the next turn.
- Everything you need is in this message and the current component message (with its earlier parts). Components already drawn here are final; reuse them exactly when embedded. Never rely on any other project, file or link.
- Where a component message differs from a board rule, it wins for that component only, and the difference goes on Notes.

PUBLISH (a founder step; you only prepare the index)
When the founder accepts a component, the founder adds it to the published Pantopus design system under its exact name, so it comes out identical on all 59 later surfaces. Make this mechanical: list every specimen name on 00a · Notes, section E. Give one name per drawn grid cell, plus one for each anatomy size or platform form the component message lists under PUBLISH KEYS. "Does not apply" cells get no name.
  <Component> / <variant> / <state> / <size|platform> / <light|dark>
<variant> and <state> are exactly the printed keys (B12), never the labels. The <size|platform> slot takes exactly one of these strings: size codes in uppercase (XS, S, M, L, OG); platform codes in lowercase (ios, android, web); otherwise "any". It is "any" unless the component message says otherwise. Example: "StatusChip / overdue / default / any / light".

======================================================================
BOARD RULES
======================================================================

B1. Artboards. Every artboard is 1440 px wide and as tall as its content needs, on surface.app (light) or dark surface.app (dark). A component message may set a wider artboard for a grid (for example 2000 or 2400 px); that message gives the margins, label column and gutters, and records the width on Notes, section A. Name each artboard "00a · <Component> · <NN-state> · <light|dark>". The component name takes the house style's platform slot, because one specimen artboard shows all three platforms. The only other artboard is "00a · Notes". Print each exact name above its frame in label 13/18/600 text.strong. The standard kinds are:
  01-anatomy: callouts, TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF.
  02-variants-states (light and dark): the variant × state grid.
  03-scaling-greyscale: AX5, 200% and web zoom frames, GREYSCALE and INCREASE CONTRAST.
  04-in-context: crops of real surfaces. Label each crop with its surface id, platform, width and fixture (Home A, Place B or Friend C).
The component message lists its exact artboards and any extra dark twins.

B2. Top block. Inside each component artboard, print the component name in h1 30/36/700 text.primary, its one-line purpose in body 16/24 text.secondary, then "Used in:" plus the line the message gives, in caption 12/16 text.secondary, exactly. Each section below gets an overline 11/16/600 caps heading (ANATOMY, GREYSCALE and so on).

B3. Specimen cells. Draw each specimen on a surface.base card (radius lg 12, shadow sm, 16 px padding) unless the cell names another surface. Under the card, print its cell label in caption 12/16 text.secondary: its keys, size and surface, joined by " · ". Example: "official · default · S 16pt · on surface.base".

B4. Callouts. Draw 1 px text.secondary leader lines that end in a numbered SQUARE badge (16×16, radius xs 4, surface.sunken fill, label 13/18/600 text.strong numeral). Beside each number, give the measurement and token in caption 12/16 text.strong, for example "[1] 12pt disc · ink text.secondary". Badges are square because circles are reserved (B8). Callout numbers written [1]–[7] or ①–⑦ in a component message are these square badges; never draw them as circles. Dimension lines are 1 px text.secondary with 4 px end ticks and the number centred.

B5. Units and sizes. The first time a size appears in a section, give it three ways: "16pt / 16dp / 16px" (iOS / Android / web; the values are equal). Spacing uses only 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64. Type uses only the type scale, the large-text sizes in B9, and any deviation a message records on Notes. Any other dimension is allowed only where this setup or a component message states it.

B6. Tokens by name, and dark mode. Label every colour by its token name. Hex values appear only in each TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE; the values below are for you. Dark artboards use:
  surface.base #FFFFFF → dark surface.base #0F172A
  surface.raised #F9FAFB → dark surface.raised #1E293B
  surface.sunken #F3F4F6 → dark surface.sunken #0F172A (same as dark base)
  surface.app #F6F7F9 → dark surface.app #020617
  surface.muted #F8FAFC → dark surface.muted #111827
  text.primary #111827 → dark text.primary #E5E7EB
  text.strong #374151 → dark text.strong #F1F5F9
  text.secondary #6B7280 → dark text.secondary #94A3B8
  text.muted #9CA3AF → dark text.muted #64748B (disabled controls and placeholders only)
  border.default #E5E7EB → dark border.default #1F2937 (decoration only)
  border.strong #D1D5DB → dark border.strong #374151 (decoration only)
  border.focus #0284c7 → dark border.focus #38BDF8
  primary.700 #0369a1 (links, selected text, selected edges) → "primary.400 (dark link)" #38BDF8, the same value as dark border.focus. Use that exact name on the board.
  primary.50 #f0f9ff (selected fill) → primary.900 #0c4a6e with dark text.primary on it. primary.400 (dark link) on primary.900 is for glyphs and edges only.
  primary.500 #0ea5e9 appears only where a component message names it.
  semantic.success #059669, semantic.warning #D97706 and semantic.error #DC2626 keep their hue in dark mode and go on glyphs only. primary.700 stands in for semantic.info where a message says so.
  Sunken fills: dark surface.sunken equals dark surface.base, so a sunken fill vanishes on a dark base card. Use dark surface.sunken on dark surface.raised, and dark surface.raised on dark surface.base or dark surface.app. These fills need no border.

B7. Contrast numbers. Ratios are WCAG 2 ratios computed from the real tokens. A colour at an opacity is alpha-blended over its surface in sRGB with unrounded channels, and every ratio is rounded to 2 decimals at the end. Each component message's TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE gives the figures that component needs. Print them exactly as given, and do not recompute them.

B8. Circles are reserved. Only ProvenanceMark may draw a solid disc, a ring, or a disc with a knocked-out tick. This covers any glyph silhouette and any drawn dot, bullet or badge. The typographic middle dot (·) in text is allowed. Round sub-parts inside a larger glyph are fine (a head, cart wheels, a pin's hole). Draw dot groups inside a glyph as short dashes or small rounded squares. The only other exceptions are the platform radio indicators that a component message names and flags on Notes. No iOS or web frame draws an unselected radio ring; the only ring in those frames is ProvenanceMark's unconfirmed mark.

B9. Large text. AX5 frames (iOS, 393 wide): caption 40pt, label 44pt, bodySmall 46pt, body 53pt. Android 200% frames (412 wide): caption 24sp, label 26sp, bodySmall 28sp, body 32sp. Crop both frames to the component and its row. Pairs stack, text wraps and never ends in an ellipsis, pills that must wrap become rounded rectangles (radius lg 12), and hit areas grow. Glyphs and marks scale with their text, capped at 2× their default size; a component message states any size that does not scale. Web 200% zoom frames are 390 px wide, a 195 px effective viewport, so they show the narrowest layout. A message that needs the wide zoomed form asks for a 1440 frame at 200% (720 px effective).

B10. Greyscale. Each light 03 artboard repeats the light grid at 50% scale, fully desaturated, unless the message sets a different scope. Next to each cell, print "Reads without colour: yes — <cue>", or the failure and its fix where the message names one.

B11. Increase Contrast. Each light 03 artboard shows what changes, or prints "Increase Contrast: nothing changes — <why>". By default, text.secondary becomes text.strong (dark: dark text.strong). Disabled text.muted stays, because the reason caption carries the meaning. Each message states its result.

B12. Grids, keys and cell labels. Rows are the message's variants and columns are its states, in the given order. Draw every cell. Under each row and column label, print "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary. Keys are lowercase and hyphenated, with no "/", spaces, fixture strings or dates. Labels may be longer and may quote fixtures. Each message lists its keys, and cell labels and publish names use only those keys. A cell that "does not apply" is an empty surface.base card reading "Does not apply — <reason>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary; a shared reason is printed in each cell. Never leave a cell blank or skip a row or column.

B13. Targets. The minimum hit area is 44pt on iOS, 48dp with 8dp gaps on Android, and 44px on web: "target (B13)". Draw it as a 1 px dashed text.secondary outline labelled "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px". Point a small "not a target" label at any mark or glyph inside a row.

B14. Focus vs selection. Focus is a 2 px border.focus ring (dark: dark border.focus) with a 2 px gap outside the shape. Selection is a fill plus a glyph, plus the edge or ink change the message states. Never show selection with a ring alone, or focus with a fill.

B15. Motion. Nothing animates unless a message says so. Where motion exists, draw its Reduce Motion pose and its end pose beside it. Any exemption from the house style's 300ms limit is stated in the message and recorded on Notes.

B16. Fixtures and dates. Use only the house-style FIXTURES and the strings quoted in the messages. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific. Compute every relative time from it: "observed 7:00 AM" is "11 hours ago", Mon 26 Oct is "in 7 days", and Sat 10 Oct is "9 days ago". Date rows put the relative count first ("in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct"). "Tonight", "Today" and "Tomorrow" stand alone, with no date. A time today shows no weekday ("As of 7:40 AM"). Any other string goes on Notes, section B.

B17. Air readings. The AQI track belongs to AqiBand, which is not on this board. Air rows show the value line and caption only. No EPA ColorVision Assist hue appears, and no text sits on an AQI fill.

======================================================================
00a · NOTES (one artboard, built up across the project)
======================================================================
ProvenanceMark's last part creates 00a · Notes, and each later component's last batch updates it. On each update, redraw the whole artboard, keep every earlier entry word for word, and add the new entries under the component's subheading. Print numbered lists in body 16/24 text.primary on surface.base, in five sections:
  A. Deviations and decisions (each needs a founder yes or no).
  B. Invented strings.
  C. Omitted or merged states ("none" if every cell was drawn).
  D. Open questions (only where two readings would give materially different components).
  E. Publish index (every PUBLISH name, one per line, grouped by component).
Entry numbers start with the component number: 00 for board-wide entries, then 01 ProvenanceMark through 09 ChoiceChip (for example "01.A3"). Print these entries first, under "Board":
  00.A1 Artboard names put the component in the platform slot, because each artboard covers all three platforms.
  00.A2 Marks and glyphs at AX5 / 200% are capped at 2× their default size.
  00.A3 No dark primary.50 exists, so the dark selected fill is primary.900. The dark link colour is named "primary.400 (dark link)" (= dark border.focus).
  00.A4 Dark surface.sunken equals dark surface.base, so sunken fills on a dark base or app surface use dark surface.raised.
  00.A5 Dated rows follow DateRow's format (B16). DateRow owns the format, and later surfaces copy it from there.
  00.A6 Web 200% zoom frames are 390 px (195 px effective), so they show the narrowest layout.
  00.A7 Every grid row and column carries a key, and publish names use only keys.
  00.A8 Contrast figures use the B7 method (sRGB alpha blend, unrounded channels, rounded at the end). Each component's figures are printed in its own TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE.
  00.A9 No AQI track or EPA hue appears on this board.
  00.A10 The dark text.strong, text.muted, border.strong and surface.muted values come from the published design system, not the house style. Dark text.strong is intentionally brighter than dark text.primary, for Increase Contrast.
  00.A11 Artboards are 1440 px wide unless a component message sets a wider grid artboard; each such width is recorded under that component.
  00.A12 Publish-name size and platform slot casing: size codes uppercase (XS, S, M, L, OG), platform codes lowercase (ios, android, web), otherwise "any".
  00.B1 Board annotations: "Does not apply — …" reasons, "not a target", "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px", "Reads without colour: yes — …", "Increase Contrast: nothing changes — …".

Reply 'ready' and wait for the first component.

name: ProvenanceMark
job: The only way the product says how sure it is about a fact. Three shapes, one meaning each, used everywhere. Design it first on the Foundations board, before any other prompt.
text:
Component 00a-01: ProvenanceMark. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

It comes first because every other component embeds its marks, and it gets a full light and dark set.

ARTBOARDS (8, exact names; the batch plan gives the order)
00a · ProvenanceMark · 01-anatomy · light
00a · ProvenanceMark · 01-anatomy · dark
00a · ProvenanceMark · 02-variants-states · light
00a · ProvenanceMark · 02-variants-states · dark
00a · ProvenanceMark · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
00a · ProvenanceMark · 03-scaling-greyscale · dark
00a · ProvenanceMark · 04-in-context · light
00a · ProvenanceMark · 04-in-context · dark
Plus 00a · Notes, created in batch 2.

BATCH PLAN
Batch 1 (this turn):
 1. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 01-anatomy · light
 2. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 02-variants-states · light
 3. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 04-in-context · light
 4. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 5. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 01-anatomy · dark
 6. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 02-variants-states · dark
Then stop and wait for "continue".
Batch 2:
 1. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 04-in-context · dark
 2. 00a · ProvenanceMark · 03-scaling-greyscale · dark
 3. 00a · Notes (create it with the "Board" entries from the setup message and the 01 entries below)
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

PURPOSE (print): The only way the product says how sure it is about a fact: three shapes, one meaning each, used everywhere.
USED IN (print): x-provenance-sheet, x-date-sheet, x-place-file, f5-today-calendar-strip, f4-today-pickup-card, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, f1-today-tab, f3-household-calendar, f3-household-notifications, f8-scale-strips, f8-compare-arrival-header, f8-compare-reveal, f8-compare-sheet, f8-og-compare-card, f8-seasonal-aha, f6-place-section-details, f10-extraction-confirm, f10-bill-provenance, f10-bill-trend, f10-mail-day-triage, f11-keeper-strip, f1-claim-receipt.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy: each silhouette at L 56pt with callouts, then all sizes in a row)
- OFFICIAL: a solid disc. The diameter equals the size.
- UNCONFIRMED: a ring with the same outer diameter and a transparent centre. Stroke width: XS 12 → 1.5px, S 16 → 2px, M 24 → 3px, L 56 → 7px. Never thinner than 1.5px.
- YOU ADDED: a solid disc with a tick KNOCKED OUT of it. The tick is a true cut-out that shows the surface behind, not a second colour painted on top. The tick spans the middle 56% of the diameter. Its stroke width equals the ring stroke for that size (XS 1.5, S 2, M 3, L 7), with round caps and joins. This drawing survives one-colour tinting.
- Ink: text.secondary (4.83:1 on base) or darker in light mode; dark text.secondary in dark mode. Add a crossed-out swatch row labelled "never border.* · never text.muted" (border.default is 1.24:1, text.muted is 2.54:1).
- Sizes, each with its use printed:
  XS 12pt / 12dp / 12px: the smallest size at which the three shapes can still be told apart (strip cells, widget, tray previews).
  S 16pt: list rows and captions.
  M 24pt: the sheet legend.
  L 56pt: the provenance sheet header.
  OG 28px at 1200 wide: the share-card minimum.
- Below 12pt, no mark is drawn. Show a row labelled "10pt → no mark" that prints the words instead: "Pickup day · Thursday · On record, not confirmed".
- Spacing: 8pt (spacing.2) between the mark and its text, shown with a dimension line.
- LEGEND specimen (at M 24pt, stacked): [drawn official mark] "Official" · [drawn unconfirmed mark] "On record, not confirmed" · [drawn you-added mark] "You added this". Where a legend is written "● Official · ○ … · ✓ …", those characters stand for the drawn marks: always render the vector mark, never a font character.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE (01-anatomy, light and dark)
text.secondary #6B7280 4.83:1 on base · dark text.secondary #94A3B8 6.96:1 on dark base, 5.71:1 on dark raised · stale: text.primary #111827 at 50% (the B7 50% figures) · dark stale: dark text.primary #E5E7EB at 50% (B7) · tinted widget: primary.700 #0369a1 on surface.base 5.93:1 (light) and primary.500 #0ea5e9 on dark surface.raised 5.28:1 (dark), never dimmed (at 50% they drop to 2.24:1 and 2.36:1) · never: primary.500 on surface.base 2.77:1, border.default 1.24:1, text.muted 2.54:1, text.secondary at 50% 1.98:1.
01-anatomy · dark carries the three silhouettes, the size row, the legend and this table in dark tokens only. It has no text blocks.

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 6 rows × 5 columns; each cell is a 358-wide row at S 16pt on surface.base unless a column rule says otherwise)
Columns (label → key): default → default · stale (dimmed + age words) → stale · inside tap target → in-target · tinted/accented widget rendering (silhouette only) → tinted-widget · greyscale → greyscale.
Rows (label → key), used in every column unless a column rule says otherwise:
 R1 official (filled) → official: "Flood zone" / "Zone X — minimal flood hazard", caption "FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021".
 R2 unconfirmed (hollow) → unconfirmed: "Pickup day" / "Thursday", caption "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct" (Place B).
 R3 you-added (filled + knocked-out tick) → you-added: "Warranty ends" / "Water heater · in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec", caption "You added this" (Home A).
 R4 read-from-your-photo → read-from-photo: a machine read before the user commits it, drawn with the UNCONFIRMED ring. Row "Clark Public Utilities" / "$142.18 · due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct". Under the uncertain value only (the due date), add the flag line "We weren't sure — check this" in caption 12/16 text.strong with a 12pt text.strong pencil glyph (not a circle). Beside the cell, draw a small arrow to a copy of the row after commit, where the mark becomes YOU ADDED, labelled "on commit → you-added".
 R5 stale → stale: the fact's own provenance shape (the official disc for air) in text.primary at 50% (3.39:1). Row "Air quality" / "AQI 42 · Good" (value line only, B17), with the words "Observed 7:00 AM · AirNow — 11 hours ago" in caption text.secondary.
 R6 reported → reported: shape unchanged (the unconfirmed ring for the Place B pickup row), plus a status line under the row, "You reported this · checking", in caption 12/16 text.secondary with no glyph.
Column rules:
 - default: as above.
 - stale: dim the mark to text.primary at 50% and replace the caption with that row's own stale caption. The dimming is never the only cue: the age words always appear. Per row:
   R1: Does not apply — an effective date does not age.
   R2: dimmed ring, caption "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct — 9 days ago".
   R3: Does not apply — your own entry does not age.
   R4: Does not apply — a pre-commit read is not refreshed.
   R5: print "same as stale variant" (R5 is already stale) and draw the R5 row.
   R6: dimmed ring, the R2 stale caption, and the "You reported this · checking" line under it.
 - in-target: draw the whole row at a 44pt minimum height (iOS), with the dashed target (B13) around the row and a "not a target" label on the mark. Add "48dp on Android · 44px on web".
 - tinted-widget: draw the row at XS 12pt inside a 158×158 widget crop rendered in one accent hue. Light cell: widget background surface.base, tint primary.700, labelled "system tint stand-in · 5.93:1" (never primary.500: 2.77:1). All silhouettes are one colour; the YOU ADDED tick stays a cut-out showing the widget background. Print the word next to every mark (a widget is a standalone surface).
   R5 tinted-widget: no dimming under tinted rendering. Draw the full-strength tint (5.93:1 light, 5.28:1 dark) and let the age words "— 11 hours ago" carry the stale state. Label it "tint is never dimmed; the words carry stale".
 - greyscale: the default cell at 0% saturation, labelled "shape carries the meaning".
Dark twin: the same 30 cells in dark tokens. The tinted column uses widget background dark surface.raised with tint primary.500, labelled "system tint stand-in · 5.28:1". Its R5 cell follows the same no-dimming rule.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R1, R2 and R3 stacked. The mark scales with Dynamic Type relative to the caption style, capped at 32pt. The row text wraps, and the mark top-aligns to the first line. The legend becomes one entry per line.
- 200% (Android 412): the same three rows with sp scaling, mark capped at 32dp.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same, with the SVG sized in em.
- XS legibility strip: the three marks at XS 12pt on surface.base, surface.sunken, dark surface.base and dark surface.raised, plus both tinted-widget backgrounds from the grid, labelled "must be told apart at 12pt".
- GREYSCALE (this component overrides B10): do not redraw the grid. Print "Greyscale: see the greyscale column on 02-variants-states — every cell reads yes — shape". Draw one deliberate FAIL example labelled "WRONG": two discs that differ only in hue, with the fix label "fix: shape, not colour".
- INCREASE CONTRAST: the three marks in text.strong, labelled "Increase Contrast ink".
Dark twin (03 · dark): the AX5 and 200% frames in dark tokens, the XS strip, and the three marks in dark text.strong labelled "Increase Contrast ink". It leaves out the web zoom frame and the greyscale pointer, because greyscale does not depend on theme.

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy · light)
- Spoken names are fixed: "official", "on record, not confirmed", "you added this". The name is appended to the row's merged label:
  "Flood zone, Zone X, minimal flood hazard, FEMA, official"
  "Pickup day Thursday, City of Camas, on record, not confirmed"
  "Warranty ends, water heater, in 54 days, Saturday 12 December, you added this"
- Non-colour encoding: the shape; colour never tells the marks apart.
- Target rule: the mark is never a tap target on its own. The enclosing row or cell is the target (B13).
- Contrast: at least 3:1 in both themes, including the tinted widget. Scales with Dynamic Type or sp up to AX5 / 200%.
- Each surface shows a legend or a first-occurrence word once.

COPY (print on 01-anatomy · light)
- Legend strings, exactly: "Official" · "On record, not confirmed" · "You added this".
- Print the word next to the mark once per surface. On standalone surfaces (widget, OG card, push landing), print it next to every mark.
- In a push, the caveat goes at the front of the title: "Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow".
- Glossary: never "verified", "confirmed" or "trusted" for official data; never "unverified", "estimated", "guessed", "pending" or "probable" for the hollow mark; never "user-entered", "self-reported" or "manual" for the tick.

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy · light)
- iOS widgets: the mark is widgetAccentable, and the tick stays knocked out under accented rendering.
- Android widgets: fixed ink (text.secondary / dark text.secondary), not a Material dynamic colour role.
- Web: inline SVG with role="img" and an aria-label holding the spoken name.
- OG card: at least 28px at 1200 wide.

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three 390-wide crops; the dark twin has the same three crops)
 a) x-place-file, Place B. A legend strip at the top ("Official · On record, not confirmed · You added this" with drawn M-size marks), then these rows: "Flood zone · Zone X — minimal flood hazard" (official); "Radon zone · Zone 1 — highest potential" (official, caption "EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home"); "Pickup day · Thursday" (unconfirmed); "Pickup frequency · Not set" (no mark, because nothing is on record).
 b) f5-today-calendar-strip, Home A. At the top of the crop, above the strip, a legend line: [drawn official mark] "Official" · [drawn unconfirmed mark] "On record, not confirmed" · [drawn you-added mark] "You added this", with the marks at S 16pt, labelled "legend once per surface". Then a 14-cell FourteenDayStrip from Mon 19 Oct to Sun 1 Nov, with marks at XS 12pt in one ink colour. Draw every fixture date in the window:
   Tue 20 Oct: unconfirmed ring (recycling and garbage, city schedule).
   Fri 23 Oct: you-added mark (Clark Public Utilities bill).
   Mon 26 Oct: voter registration, a statewide rule, drawn as a full-height bar spanning the cell with no mark. Label it "civic bar (FourteenDayStrip)".
   Tue 27 Oct: unconfirmed ring (garbage only).
   Wed 28 Oct: you-added mark (City of Vancouver water bill).
   Sun 1 Nov: you-added mark (HOA dues).
   All other cells are empty. Beside the strip print "at most 3 marks per cell, then +N".
  Under the strip, draw the matching rows at S 16pt, each with its mark:
   "Recycling and garbage" / "Tomorrow" (unconfirmed)
   "Clark Public Utilities · $142.18" / "in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct" (you added)
   "Online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct" / "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct" (official)
   "Garbage only" / "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct" (unconfirmed)
   "City of Vancouver water · $84.00" / "in 9 days · Wed 28 Oct" (you added)
   "HOA dues · $285" / "in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov" (you added)
  Label: "the strip is one element; rows are the targets".
 c) f7-today-widget, 338×158pt, "Larkspur Loop". Marks at XS 12pt, each with its word printed beside it, for example "On record, not confirmed" next to "Recycling and garbage · Tomorrow".

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy · light)
- Instead of filled vs hollow for any other meaning (sender vs you in compare, taken vs open founding slots, density), draw labelled pointers, or solid vs hatched segments plus a numeral — because filled vs hollow means provenance and nothing else.
- Instead of a confidence percentage, bar or star, draw one of the three marks plus its word — because the product never grades certainty.
- Instead of a hollow mark on an official public dataset (EPA radon zone, USFS wildfire hazard), draw the filled mark and put the limit in the caption's scope word ("county-wide estimate") — because hollow means "not confirmed", not "coarse".
- Instead of a tick painted in a second colour on top of the disc, knock the tick out — because a second colour disappears under one-colour widget tinting.
- Instead of a light tinted widget in primary.500, use primary.700 on surface.base — because primary.500 is 2.77:1 on white and marks need 3:1.
- Instead of dimming a tinted widget mark for stale, keep the full tint and add the age words — because a dimmed tint drops below 3:1.
- Instead of making an 8px dot the tap target, make the enclosing row or cell the target — because a small mark cannot be hit reliably.
- Instead of a bare "Unverified" suffix on every row, show the word once per surface in a legend — because repetition is noise and "unverified" is forbidden.
- Instead of text.secondary at 50% for stale, use text.primary at 50% — because the first drops to 1.98:1.
- Instead of one age suffix on every row, give each fact its own stale caption — because an effective date or your own entry does not age.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: official · unconfirmed · you-added · read-from-photo · stale · reported. States: default · stale · in-target · tinted-widget · greyscale.
<size|platform> is the size the cell is drawn at (XS, S, M, L, OG); tinted-widget cells are XS. Examples: "ProvenanceMark / official / default / S / light" · "ProvenanceMark / you-added / tinted-widget / XS / dark".

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "01 ProvenanceMark")
 01.A1 Stale ink is text.primary at 50% (3.39:1 on base), not a plain "50% opacity", because text.secondary at 50% is 1.98:1 and marks need 3:1.
 01.A2 Stale captions are per row, not one shared suffix. The pickup schedule reads "as of Sat 10 Oct — 9 days ago". The official effective-date row, your own entry and a pre-commit photo read "does not apply", because they do not age.
 01.A3 The tinted widget is never dimmed for stale. The full tint stays (5.93:1 light, 5.28:1 dark) and the age words carry the state, because a 50% tint drops to 2.24:1 (light) and 2.36:1 (dark).
 01.A4 Tinted-widget stand-in: primary.700 on surface.base in light (5.93:1) and primary.500 on dark surface.raised in dark (5.28:1). primary.500 on white is 2.77:1, so it is not used in light mode.
 01.A5 The ring and tick stroke widths per size (1.5 / 2 / 3 / 7) and the 56% tick span are this board's geometry. The source spec sets only the 1.5px minimum.
 01.A6 The spoken example "Trash day Tuesday, City of Camas, …" became "Pickup day Thursday, City of Camas, on record, not confirmed", following the glossary ("Pickup day") and the Place B fixture.
 01.A7 In the calendar-strip crop, Mon 26 Oct voter registration is FourteenDayStrip's full-height civic bar (a civic, state or county rule is a full-height bar spanning the cell), not a mark. Its row uses the "must arrive by" wording.
 01.A8 The calendar-strip crop prints the legend once above the strip, so that surface shows each mark's word once (invariant 1).
 01.B1 "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct" · "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct — 9 days ago" · "Water heater · in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec" · "$142.18 · due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct" · "Pickup frequency · Not set" · "Pickup day · Thursday · On record, not confirmed" · "Recycling and garbage · Tomorrow".
 01.B2 The six calendar-strip rows under crop b, each quoted exactly as written there.
 01.B3 Annotations: "civic bar (FourteenDayStrip)" · "legend once per surface" · "tint is never dimmed; the words carry stale" · "on commit → you-added".
 01.B4 The flood-zone and warranty spoken labels from ACCESSIBILITY.
 01.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 01.E Every ProvenanceMark name, by the grammar and keys above.

DONE WHEN
- All 8 artboards and 00a · Notes (Board and 01 entries) exist with exact names.
- Both 02 grids have 6 × 5 cells with printed keys; "Does not apply" cells print their reasons; the stale column uses each row's own caption; both R5 tinted cells are at full tint.
- No mark is under 12pt, no ring stroke under 1.5px, and the tick is a cut-out everywhere, including both tinted cells (each printing its background, tint and ratio).
- Crops a and b print the legend once; the widget crop prints the word beside every mark.
- The strip is named "FourteenDayStrip" and nothing else. No mark is a target on its own.

name: SourceCaption
job: Puts the minimum provenance on the value itself: who says it, what it covers, and when. Almost nobody opens the provenance sheet, so the caption has to carry the caveat.
text:
Component 00a-02: SourceCaption. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

SourceCaption embeds the ProvenanceMark you drew in 00a-01. Reuse those marks exactly, including the stale ink and stroke rule.

ARTBOARDS (5, exact names)
1. 00a · SourceCaption · 01-anatomy · light: the caption pattern with callouts, base vs sunken ink, the wrap example, link vs no link, the OG strip, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF
2. 00a · SourceCaption · 02-variants-states · light: the 7 × 3 grid
3. 00a · SourceCaption · 04-in-context · light: f8-scale-strips, f1-today-air-band (default and alert, no track), and the f8-compare-arrival-header frozen row
4. 00a · SourceCaption · 03-scaling-greyscale · light: AX5, 200%, web zoom, the greyscale grid, Increase Contrast
5. 00a · SourceCaption · 02-variants-states · dark: the same 21 cells in dark tokens
Also: update 00a · Notes.
WIDTH: both 02-variants-states artboards are 1600 px wide (an exception to B1; Notes 02.A4). All other artboards are 1440.

BATCH PLAN
Batch 1 (this turn):
 1. 00a · SourceCaption · 01-anatomy · light
 2. 00a · SourceCaption · 02-variants-states · light
 3. 00a · SourceCaption · 04-in-context · light
 4. 00a · SourceCaption · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 5. 00a · SourceCaption · 02-variants-states · dark
 6. 00a · Notes (update it with the 02 entries below)
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

PURPOSE (print): Puts the minimum provenance on the value itself: who says it, what it covers, and when.
Under the purpose, print this rationale line in body 16/24 text.secondary (a top-block addition, Notes 02.A3): "Almost nobody opens the provenance sheet, so the caption carries the caveat."
USED IN (print): f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f1-today-air-band, f8-seasonal-aha, f8-compare-arrival-header, f8-compare-reveal, f8-og-compare-card, f8-compare-sheet, x-provenance-sheet, x-place-file, f4-today-pickup-card, f5-today-calendar-strip, f3-household-calendar, f10-bill-trend.

LINK RULE (applies to every cell, crop and frame)
A caption is a link only when its source has a URL. A link caption shows all three of these: the authority word in primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)) with an underline; the trailing external-link glyph in the same colour; and the dashed target (B13) around the caption line. A caption with no URL is all text.secondary (text.strong on sunken), with no underline, no glyph and no target.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy: callouts on a 358-wide specimen, "FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021", with a URL, so it shows the link form. Callout numbers are the square badges from B4.)
- [1] ProvenanceMark at S 16pt, leading, top-aligned to the first line, with an 8pt gap.
- [2] Authority, [3] " · " separator, [4] scope word, [5] " · ", [6] as-of. All in caption 12/16/400.
- Ink: text.secondary on base, raised or app surfaces; text.strong on sunken. Draw two copies side by side, one on base and one on sunken, each labelled with its tokens and ratios.
- The caption wraps to two lines at default size and never cuts the authority short with an ellipsis. Draw a 240-wide wrap example: "EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home".
- [7] The optional trailing external-link glyph (12pt, an arrow out of a square, not a circle), shown only when a source URL exists (LINK RULE).
- Beside the specimen, draw the same caption without a URL, labelled "no URL: flat, not a target", so link and no-link sit side by side.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE (01-anatomy)
text.secondary #6B7280: 4.83 on base / 4.63 raised / 4.51 app / 4.39 sunken (below 4.5, so text on sunken is text.strong) · text.strong #374151: 9.37 on sunken, 10.31 on base · primary.700 #0369a1: 5.93 on base / 5.68 raised / 5.54 app / 5.39 sunken · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8: 8.33 on dark base / 6.83 dark raised · dark text.secondary #94A3B8: 6.96 on dark base / 5.71 dark raised · dark text.strong #F1F5F9: 16.30 on dark base · mark ink: as in the ProvenanceMark table (at least 3:1; stale text.primary at 50%: 3.39 on base, dark 4.45 on dark base).

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 7 rows × 3 columns)
Layout: 48 px side margins, a 238 px row-label column, 32 px gutters, and three 390-wide columns (48 + 238 + 3 × (32 + 390) + 48 = 1600). Each cell is a 390-wide surface.base card (358 content + 16 px padding each side) showing the value line in bodySmall 14/20 text.primary above the caption. R5 content is 320 wide (a 352-wide card), left-aligned in its column.
Columns (label → key): default → default · stale (the as-of age appended) → stale · offline ("as of" date) → offline.
Each row states its mark and whether it has a URL. Apply the LINK RULE in every cell of the row. Offline rule (Notes 02.A7): captions with an effective date, a frozen date or a stated as-of do not change offline; only live captions switch to "as of <time>".
 R1 dated static → dated-static. Mark: official. URL: none. Value "Zone X — minimal flood hazard".
   default: "FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021".
   stale: Does not apply — an effective date does not age.
   offline: unchanged. Draw the default caption and label it "static captions do not change offline".
 R2 live → live. Mark: official. URL: yes (AirNow). Value "AQI 42 · Good" (value line only, B17).
   default: "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM today".
   stale: dimmed mark, "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM today — 11 hours ago" (the same string as ProvenanceMark R5).
   offline: "AirNow · nearest monitors · as of 7:00 AM". The link form stays, because the URL still exists.
 R3 frozen token (a compare card's saved reading) → frozen. Mark: official. URL: none. Value "AQI 42 · Good".
   default: "AirNow · on Sat 12 Sep 2026".
   stale: Does not apply — a frozen reading is dated, never "ago".
   offline: unchanged; label it as in R1.
 R4 county scope → county. Mark: official (the limit goes in the scope word, never a hollow mark). URL: yes (EPA). Value "Zone 1 — highest potential". This caption has no as-of (Notes 02.A9).
   default: "EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home".
   stale: Does not apply — a county zone does not age.
   offline: unchanged; label it as in R1.
 R5 collapsed sources line, only at 320–360 wide → collapsed. URL: none on the sources line. Draw it in the 320-wide content under these four value rows, each with the official mark at S 16pt:
   "Flood · Zone X — minimal flood hazard"
   "Wildfire · Moderate · 3 of 5"
   "Air · AQI 42 · Good" (with its own time on the row: "observed 7:00 AM today")
   "Radon · Zone 1 — highest potential"
  The sources line itself has no mark.
   default: "Sources: FEMA, USFS, AirNow, EPA".
   stale: the sources line is unchanged; only the air row dims its mark and appends "— 11 hours ago".
   offline: the sources line is unchanged; the air row reads "as of 7:00 AM".
 R6 no URL, a flat caption that is not tappable → no-url. Mark: unconfirmed (the Place B pickup schedule, as in ProvenanceMark R2). URL: none. Value "Thursday".
   default: "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct", with no glyph and no underline, labelled "not a target".
   stale: the dimmed ring (text.primary at 50%, as in ProvenanceMark) and "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct — 9 days ago", flat, no link, labelled "not a target". This matches ProvenanceMark R2 stale.
   offline: unchanged; label it as in R1.
 R7 dated static, with URL → dated-static-link. Mark: official. URL: yes (FEMA). Value "Zone X — minimal flood hazard". It exists so the difference between R1 and R6 is visible.
   default: "FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021" in the link form.
   stale: Does not apply — an effective date does not age.
   offline: unchanged; label it as in R1.
That leaves 4 "Does not apply" cells per grid (R1, R3, R4 and R7 stale) and 17 drawn cells.
Dark twin: all 21 cells in dark tokens, same 1600 px layout. Stale ink is dark text.primary at 50%.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R2 and R4 at caption 40pt with the mark at 32pt (stroke 4px), wrapping to as many lines as needed and never ending in an ellipsis. Both are links, so both keep the underline, the glyph (scaled to 24pt) and a target that grows with the text.
- 200% (Android 412): the same at 24sp.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10): all 21 cells; the 4 "Does not apply" cells repeat their reasons. Drawn link cells (R2 and R4 default and offline, R7 default and offline, R2 stale): "Reads without colour: yes — underline + glyph". All other drawn cells, including R6 stale: "Reads without colour: yes — words; the mark's shape".
- INCREASE CONTRAST: R2 default with the non-link caption text in text.strong. The authority link stays primary.700 with its underline and glyph.

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Contrast is at least 4.5:1 (see the table).
- The caption is read after the value in the row's merged label: "Air quality, AQI 42, Good, AirNow, nearest monitors, observed 7:00 AM today, official".
- When a URL exists, the row exposes the link as a custom action named "Open <authority>" (for example "Open AirNow"). On web, the link is a separate focusable link after the row.
- The non-colour cue for a link is the underline plus the external-link glyph.
- Target rule: a caption is a target (B13) only when a URL exists. A caption with no URL is never a target.
- There is no hover-only content.

COPY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Always authority · scope · as-of (as-of where the source has one).
- Use the authority's own word, "hazard" or "potential"; never "risk" unless the source says risk.
- Deadlines received by a date say "must arrive by" ("Online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct").
- Never write "Sources:" at widths above 360 (except the OG image).
- Never write "provider", "feed" or "partner" for the source.
- Never label a frozen reading "today".

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy)
- Same on iOS, Android and web.
- On the OG image, the caption is at least 28px and may be merged into one sources line; the full captions go in og:description. Draw a 1200-wide strip crop showing "Sources: FEMA, USFS, AirNow, EPA" at 28px on surface.base in text.secondary, with no mark and no link, labelled "OG sources strip · 28px". This strip is a published specimen.

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three 390-wide crops)
 a) f8-scale-strips, Place B: the flood row. Draw the value line "Zone X — minimal flood hazard" and the R1 caption (official mark, no URL) only. Where the strip would sit, between the value and the caption, draw a 1 px text.secondary placeholder box labelled "track omitted: ScaleStrip".
 b) f1-today-air-band, Place B: "AQI 42 · Good" with the R2 caption (official, link form). Beside it, draw an alert-variant copy: "AQI 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups" with "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 4:00 PM today" (official, link form). Both show the value line and caption only; label them "track omitted: AqiBand" (B17).
 c) f8-compare-arrival-header, Friend C: a "Dana · Camas, WA" card with the row "Air on Sat 12 Sep · AQI 42 · Good" and the R3 caption "AirNow · on Sat 12 Sep 2026" (official, no URL).

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of hiding the source behind a tooltip or "learn more", print authority · scope · as-of on the value — because almost nobody opens the sheet.
- Instead of labelling a frozen reading "today", write "on Sat 12 Sep 2026" — because a shared card is read days later.
- Instead of making a caption with no URL tappable, draw it flat — because a target that goes nowhere breaks trust.
- Instead of "Sources:" on wide layouts, give every row its own caption — because the collapsed line exists only for 320–360 widths (except the OG image).
- Instead of cutting a long authority short with an ellipsis, wrap to a second line — because the authority is the caveat.
- Instead of a hollow mark on a county-wide official estimate, use the filled mark and the scope word — because hollow means "not confirmed".

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: dated-static · dated-static-link · live · frozen · county · collapsed · no-url. States: default · stale · offline. <size|platform> is "any" for grid cells. Example: "SourceCaption / live / stale / any / light".
Also publish the OG strip: "SourceCaption / collapsed / default / OG / light".
Total: 35 names (17 drawn cells per theme, plus the OG strip).

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "02 SourceCaption")
 02.A1 Source example strings were re-dated to the house-style fixtures (TODAY Mon 19 Oct 2026) and the weekday date format: "effective Sep 24, 2021" → "effective Sep 2021"; "observed 3:10 PM today" → "observed 7:00 AM today"; "on Sep 12, 2026" → "on Sat 12 Sep 2026"; "— 9 hours ago" → "— 11 hours ago"; "as of Sep 15" → "as of 7:00 AM".
 02.A2 SourceCaption adds a dated-static-link key (row R7) for the with-URL form, so the link form can be published separately from the no-URL form.
 02.A3 The top block carries a second line, a rationale, under the purpose.
 02.A4 Both 02-variants-states artboards are 1600 px wide (an exception to B1): 48 px side margins, a 238 px row-label column, 32 px gutters and three 390-wide cards (358 content + 16 px padding). R5 content is 320 wide (a 352-wide card), left-aligned in its column.
 02.A5 URL and mark per row: R2 live (AirNow), R4 county (EPA) and R7 dated-static-link (FEMA) have URLs; R1, R3, R5 and R6 do not. R1–R5 and R7 carry the official mark; R6 carries the unconfirmed mark. R5's marks sit on its four value rows, and the sources line has none.
 02.A6 The OG sources strip is published as "SourceCaption / collapsed / default / OG / light", using the board's uppercase size code.
 02.A7 Captions with an effective date, a frozen date or a stated as-of do not change offline; only live captions switch to "as of <time>". The contract's offline state ("as of <date>") therefore applies to live captions only.
 02.A8 When a URL exists, the row exposes the link to assistive tech as a custom action "Open <authority>"; on web it is a separate focusable link after the row.
 02.A9 The county caption has no as-of: a county zone map is undated, so the contract string is used as-is. The printed copy rule reads "as-of where the source has one".
 02.A10 The Place B pickup caption has a stale form ("— 9 days ago"), matching ProvenanceMark R2 and 01.A2, so later surfaces get one answer.
 02.B1 "AirNow · nearest monitors · as of 7:00 AM" · "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 4:00 PM today" · "AQI 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups" · "Air on Sat 12 Sep · AQI 42 · Good" · "Flood · Zone X — minimal flood hazard" · "Wildfire · Moderate · 3 of 5" · "Air · AQI 42 · Good" · "Radon · Zone 1 — highest potential" · "Sources: FEMA, USFS, AirNow, EPA" · "Open AirNow" · "track omitted: AqiBand" · "track omitted: ScaleStrip" · "static captions do not change offline" · "dated static, with URL" · "no URL: flat, not a target" · "OG sources strip · 28px" · "Reads without colour: yes — underline + glyph" · "Reads without colour: yes — words; the mark's shape". "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct", its "— 9 days ago" form and "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM today — 11 hours ago" are already listed under 01; "not a target" is listed under 00.
 02.B2 Spoken label: "Air quality, AQI 42, Good, AirNow, nearest monitors, observed 7:00 AM today, official".
 02.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 02.E All 35 SourceCaption names: one per drawn grid cell (17 light, 17 dark), plus the OG strip.

DONE WHEN
- All 5 artboards exist with their exact names, and both 02 artboards are 1600 px wide with the stated margins, label column and gutters. Notes has the 02 entries, with the earlier entries unchanged.
- Both grids have 7 rows × 3 columns with printed keys; exactly 4 cells per grid (R1, R3, R4, R7 stale) are "Does not apply" and print their reasons.
- Every cell carries the mark its row names. R6 uses the unconfirmed ring, and its stale cell shows the dimmed ring with "— 9 days ago", flat. No R5 sources line has a mark.
- R2, R4 and R7 cells show the underline, the glyph and the dashed target. No other cell or crop without a URL shows any of the three.
- Text on sunken is text.strong. No authority is cut short with an ellipsis. "Sources:" appears only in the 320-wide R5 cells and on the OG strip.
- No frozen reading says "today". No air or scale crop draws a track or an EPA hue; each shows its "track omitted" label instead.
- 02.E lists exactly 35 names.

name: ScopeChip
job: States who can see this address data: only you, or your household. It appears on every surface that shows address data.
text:
Component 00a-03: ScopeChip. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

ARTBOARDS (5, exact names; all 1440 wide)
1. 00a · ScopeChip · 01-anatomy · light: the pill with callouts, the glyphs, target vs label-only, the footer sentence, the retired wording, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF
2. 00a · ScopeChip · 02-variants-states · light: the 5 × 4 grid
3. 00a · ScopeChip · 04-in-context · light: the f1-today-tab location row, the x-date-sheet footer above Save, the f1-claim-receipt pairs and consent

5. 00a · ScopeChip · 02-variants-states · dark: the same 20 cells in dark tokens
Also: update 00a · Notes.

Batch 1 (this turn):
 1. 00a · ScopeChip · 01-anatomy · light
 2. 00a · ScopeChip · 02-variants-states · light
 3. 00a · ScopeChip · 04-in-context · light
 4. 00a · ScopeChip · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 5. 00a · ScopeChip · 02-variants-states · dark
 6. 00a · Notes (update it with the 03 entries below)
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

PURPOSE (print): States who can see this address data, only you or your household, on every surface that shows address data.
USED IN (print): f1-today-tab, f1-today-air-band, f1-your-places, f1-add-place-sheet, f1-save-confirmation, f1-email-verify-handoff, f1-claim-receipt, x-date-sheet, x-place-file, f4-today-pickup-card, f7-widget-tap-landing, f9-privacy-mirror, f11-keeper-naming, f11-keeper-strip, f3-household-notifications, f10-mail-day-triage, f10-snap-capture-tray, f10-mail-snap-privacy, f10-mail-piece-photo.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy: callouts on "Saved place · Only you" and "Your household")
- ① Pill, radius pill, height 24pt / 24dp / 24px.
- ② Horizontal padding 8 (spacing.2) and a 4 (spacing.1) gap between glyph and label.
- ③ A 12pt glyph: a person means Only you; a house means household. It is a line glyph with a 1.5px stroke in text.strong. The house glyph could use identity.home only if it reached 3:1, but identity.home on surface.sunken is 2.99:1, so draw it in text.strong and print "identity.home fails 3:1 on sunken (2.99) → text.strong".
- ④ Label in label 13/18/600, text.strong (9.37:1 on sunken). The " · " separator is a typographic middle dot with a space on each side.
- ⑤ Fill surface.sunken, with no border (dark: the sunken-fill rule in B6).
- ⑥ Hit area: a target (B13) only when the chip opens the control that changes scope. Draw a "label only, no target" copy and an "opens scope control" copy with the dashed target and a trailing 12pt chevron in text.strong.
- Footer sentence form (used in sheets): a 16pt glyph and a sentence in bodySmall 14/20 text.secondary on base, with no pill.
- Consent buttons (used with the pending pair): both are secondary buttons of equal weight: surface.base fill, 1px text.secondary outline, radius md 8, label 13/18/600 text.primary, 44pt / 48dp / 44px tall (dark, per B6: dark surface.base fill, 1px dark text.secondary outline, dark text.primary label). Neither is filled primary.700.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE (01-anatomy)
text.strong #374151 on sunken 9.37 · identity.home #16A34A on sunken 2.99 (not used) · text.secondary #6B7280 on base 4.83 (footer sentence; consent button outline) · dark text.strong #F1F5F9 on dark raised 13.35 · dark text.secondary #94A3B8 on dark base 6.96 (dark consent button outline).

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 5 rows × 4 columns)
Geometry: a 160-wide row-label column, then four 280-wide columns with 24 gutters (each B3 card is 280 wide, 248 inside its padding). Cells grow in height to fit; nothing is scaled.
Columns (label → key): default → default · pending share (dashed house glyph) → pending · declined share (person → person) → declined · struck (old scope on the claim receipt) → struck.
 R1 saved place → saved-place: "Saved place · Only you" with the person glyph.
   default: as specified.
   pending and declined: Does not apply — pending and declined exist only in the scope-change pair (R4).
   struck: the chip with a 1px text.strong strike line through the label, then a 4pt gap, a 12pt arrow glyph, another 4pt gap and a "Your household" chip, captioned "old scope on the claim receipt". The strike is never the only cue: the new chip is always beside it (wrap the new chip under the struck one if the cell is too narrow).
 R2 claimed home → claimed-home: "Your household" with the house glyph.
   default: as specified.
   pending, declined and struck: Does not apply — a claimed home's chip has no pending share or older scope of its own.
 R3 named home (multi-home contexts) → named-home: "Larkspur Loop · Your household" with the house glyph.
   default: as specified.
   pending, declined and struck: Does not apply — a claimed home's chip has no pending share or older scope of its own.
 R4 scope-change pair (claim receipt, trailing edge of a carried row) → scope-change-pair: glyphs only, a 12pt person glyph → 12pt arrow → 12pt house glyph, in text.strong. Show it on the row "Warranty ends · in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec".
   default: person → house, both in solid lines (shared).
   pending: person → house, with the house drawn in a DASHED 1.5px stroke (2px dash, 2px gap), shown until the user chooses. Under the row, the consent question "Share the 2 dates you entered with Sam?" in bodySmall 14/20 text.primary, then the two consent buttons from the anatomy, "Share with the household" and "Keep them private to me" (the glossary tension is flagged on Notes). Stack them vertically, both full cell width, both 44pt / 48dp / 44px tall, both in the secondary style; labels wrap rather than truncate. Under the cell, add the caption "specimen shows one of the 2 rows" (the in-context crop c shows both).
   declined: person → person, both solid.

 R5 footer sentence form (sheets) → footer-sentence:
   default: two copies, the person glyph with "Only you will see this." and the house glyph with "Everyone in this household will see this."
   pending, declined and struck: Does not apply — the sentence describes the current scope only.
Dark twin: all 20 cells in dark tokens, same geometry, using the sunken-fill rule from B6; the consent buttons use their dark style from the anatomy.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R1 and R3 at label 44pt. The chip wraps to two lines and becomes a rounded rectangle (radius lg 12), with the glyph scaled to 24pt and top-aligned. The height grows to fit. Nothing is truncated.
- 200% (Android 412): the same at 26sp.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10, scope changed): the light grid again at 100% scale, not 50% (it is 1376 wide and fits the 1440 artboard), fully desaturated. Every drawn cell reads "yes — glyph + words"; Does-not-apply cells get no verdict. The dashed house still reads as dashed: "yes — dashed stroke + consent words".
- INCREASE CONTRAST: the chip is unchanged (it is already text.strong); the R5 footer sentence becomes text.strong.

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Spoken: "Visible to only you" (R1); "Visible to your household" (R2 and R3; R3 is prefixed with "Larkspur Loop,"). Pair, default: "Visible to your household". Pair, pending: "Visible to only you; will be visible to your household if you share". Pair, declined: "Visible to only you".
- Never colour-only: the glyph plus the words.
- Target rule: a target (B13) only when it opens the scope control; otherwise it is not a target.
- It wraps at AX sizes.

COPY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Exactly these chip strings: "Saved place · Only you" and "Your household" (with an optional leading home label, as in "Larkspur Loop · Your household").
- Exactly these sentences: "Only you will see this." and "Everyone in this household will see this."
- Draw a crossed-out list headed "Retired wording": "Only you see this" · "Only you can see these" · "private to your home" · "Saved place - Only you" (a hyphen instead of a middle dot).
- A saved place never uses the words home, household or claim.
- Where finance permissions differ, name the people instead: "You and Sam can see these photos".

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy)
- Identical on iOS, Android and web.
- On push landings, it sits next to the address in the location row.

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three crops at 100%, each labelled with surface id, platform, width and fixture)
 a) f1-today-tab, Place B, web 390: the location row "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with "Saved place · Only you" beside it (wrapping under it if the row is too narrow), and the FreshnessLine words "Updated 12m ago" below it (caption 12/16 text.secondary, 4pt below the location row; FreshnessLine is specified in the next component).
 b) x-date-sheet, Home A, iOS 393: the sheet's title row at the top of the crop, with the title "Add a date" and the sheet's visible "Close" in that row; then (with the sheet body cropped out between) the footer sentence "Everyone in this household will see this." directly above the sheet's primary button "Save".
 c) f1-claim-receipt, Home A, Android 412: the header title "What moved when you claimed", under it the struck "Saved place · Only you" → "Your household" (R1 struck). Then two carried rows, each with a pending pair (R4 pending) at its trailing edge: "Warranty ends · in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec" and "Notice deadline · in 133 days · Mon 1 Mar 2027". Under the rows, the consent block from R4 (the question and the two stacked secondary buttons, 48dp tall).

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of a green "verified-looking" chip to mean membership, draw the neutral sunken chip with the house glyph — because green reads as verification, which is a different thing.
- Instead of dropping the chip from an alert landing, keep it next to the address — because an alert is when people most need to know who else sees it.
- Instead of "Everyone in this household" where finance permissions differ, name the people ("You and Sam can see these photos") — because the sentence would be false.
- Instead of an identity.home fill, use surface.sunken with text.strong — because the colour is not the message and fails contrast on sunken.
- Instead of any new wording, use the two chip strings and two sentences — because five earlier wordings drifted.
- Instead of a filled "Share" button beside an outlined decline, give both consent buttons the same secondary style — because a decline must carry equal weight.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: saved-place · claimed-home · named-home · scope-change-pair · footer-sentence. States: default · pending · declined · struck. <size|platform> is "any". Example: "ScopeChip / scope-change-pair / pending / any / light".

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "03 ScopeChip")
 03.A1 The house glyph is text.strong, because identity.home is 2.99:1 on surface.sunken.
 03.A2 Footer sentence type is bodySmall 14/20 text.secondary with a 16pt glyph; the source spec sets no type style.
 03.A3 The named-home example "Maple St · Your household" became "Larkspur Loop · Your household" (the Home A fixture label).
 03.A4 Glossary tension: the sourced consent button "Keep them private to me" is close to the glossary's forbidden "private to you" and the retired "private to your home". Proposed alternative: "Just me" (the house style's neutral decline).
 03.A5 The second carried row shows the year ("Mon 1 Mar 2027") because the date is not in the current year; the count is from TODAY Mon 19 Oct 2026.
 03.A6 Both consent buttons use one secondary style (surface.base fill, 1px text.secondary outline, radius md 8, label 13/18/600 text.primary; dark tokens per B6), because the source sets no style and a decline must carry equal weight. Later consent pairs copy this.
 03.A7 The ScopeChip greyscale grid is drawn at 100%, not the B10 50%, so the 13pt labels and glyphs stay legible for the verdicts.
 03.B1 "Warranty ends · in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec" · "Notice deadline · in 133 days · Mon 1 Mar 2027" (tile label + the Home A notice-deadline fixture) · "What moved when you claimed" (receipt header; the place-file entry name from f1-claim-receipt research) · "old scope on the claim receipt" · "specimen shows one of the 2 rows" · "label only, no target" · "opens scope control" · "Retired wording" · "Saved place - Only you" (retired example, not in the contract's list) · "identity.home fails 3:1 on sunken (2.99) → text.strong".
 03.B2 Spoken labels: "Visible to only you; will be visible to your household if you share".
 03.B3 Sourced, not invented: "Share the 2 dates you entered with Sam?" (adapted from f1-claim-receipt research: "Sam and Dana" → "Sam", to match the Home A fixture), "Share with the household" and "Keep them private to me" (f1-claim-receipt research); "Add a date" and "Save" (the DateSheet title and primary button); "Close" (the house style's visible sheet Close).
 03.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 03.D Keep "Keep them private to me", or use "Just me"? (03.A4)
 03.E Every ScopeChip name.

DONE WHEN
- All 5 artboards exist with their exact names, and Notes has the 03 entries with the earlier entries unchanged.
- Both grids have 5 rows × 4 columns with printed keys, and every "Does not apply" cell prints its reason.
- Only the two chip strings and the two sentences appear as scope wording; the retired list is crossed out.
- No chip uses a green or identity.home fill; the house glyph is text.strong.
- A strike never appears without the new chip beside it, and the pending pair is dashed with its consent block; the two consent buttons are stacked, full cell width, in the same secondary style (outlined, neither filled), and the R4 pending cell carries "specimen shows one of the 2 rows".
- Each in-context crop is labelled with its surface id, platform, width and fixture (web 390, iOS 393, Android 412).
- The x-date-sheet crop shows "Add a date" as the title with a visible "Close" in the title row, and its primary button reads "Save".
- The greyscale grid is at 100% with a verdict beside every drawn cell.
- Dark chips on dark base use dark surface.raised (B6).

text:
Component 00a-04: FreshnessLine. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

ARTBOARDS (5, exact names)
1. 00a · FreshnessLine · 01-anatomy · light (1440 wide): placement, glyphs, the system hairline (running, stopped at 5s, Reduce Motion), the Retry target, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF
2. 00a · FreshnessLine · 02-variants-states · light (2400 wide): the 6 × 5 grid, then the no-reflow strip below it
3. 00a · FreshnessLine · 04-in-context · light (1440 wide): f1-today-tab, f7-today-widget past horizon, f3-bills-list header
4. 00a · FreshnessLine · 03-scaling-greyscale · light (2400 wide): AX5, 200%, web zoom, the greyscale grid, Increase Contrast
5. 00a · FreshnessLine · 02-variants-states · dark (2400 wide): the same 30 cells in dark tokens
Also: update 00a · Notes.

BATCH PLAN
Batch 1 (this turn):
 1. 00a · FreshnessLine · 01-anatomy · light
 2. 00a · FreshnessLine · 02-variants-states · light
 3. 00a · FreshnessLine · 04-in-context · light
 4. 00a · FreshnessLine · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 5. 00a · FreshnessLine · 02-variants-states · dark
 6. 00a · Notes (update it with the 04 entries below)
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

PURPOSE (print): One persistent line that states how old the content is: refresh, stale and offline all go here instead of a toast.
USED IN (print): f1-today-tab, f7-widget-tap-landing, f7-today-widget, f1-today-air-band, x-place-file, f9-invite-rewards-card, f9-nearby-cells-map, f11-keeper-strip, f10-bill-trend, f3-bills-list, f3-members-roster, f1-your-places.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy: callouts on a 358-wide card header, "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with the "Saved place · Only you" ScopeChip, and the line under it)
- ① Placement: directly under the location row or card header, 4pt / 4dp / 4px (spacing.1) below it.
- ② Caption 12/16/400 in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken).
- ③ Optional leading 16pt / 16dp / 16px glyph, in text.secondary with an 8 gap: offline (a cloud with a slash) or retry (a circular arrow drawn as an open arc with an arrowhead, not a closed ring).
- ④ Optional 2pt / 2dp / 2px indeterminate hairline under the header, full card width, in primary.700 (5.93:1 on base; at least 3:1 on its surface). It is each platform's own system indeterminate progress indicator (iOS linear ProgressView, Android Material 3 LinearProgressIndicator, web an indeterminate progress bar), tinted primary.700, with no custom duration or easing. It runs only if the refresh takes 1s or longer. This is the only motion on the board (the B15 exemption; see 04.A1). Draw three poses side by side:
   running: a short segment partway along the track, with the note "system indeterminate progress indicator · no custom duration · exempt from the 300ms rule, stopped within 5s (see Notes)".
   after 5s (the end pose): the hairline stops and is removed. "Updating…" stays in the line until the result arrives; then the line becomes "Updated just now" or the failed line (R3). Label it "idle loops stop within 5s".
   Reduce Motion: no hairline at all; the word "Updating…" carries the state.
- ⑤ "Retry" is an inline text button in label 13/18/600 primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)), with its target (B13) drawn dashed.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE (01-anatomy)
text.secondary #6B7280 4.83 on base · text.strong #374151 9.37 on sunken · primary.700 #0369a1 5.93 on base · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8 6.83 on dark raised.

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 6 rows × 5 columns)
Geometry: a 160-wide row-label column and a 12 gutter, then five 390-wide columns with 12 gutters: 160 + 12 + 5 × 390 + 4 × 12 = 2170 wide, on the 2400-wide artboard. Each drawn cell is the full 390-wide B3 card (the 358-wide header plus line, with 16 padding) at 100% scale; nothing is scaled. Does-not-apply cells are 390 wide too. Cells grow in height to fit.
Columns (label → key): fresh → fresh · refreshing → refreshing · stale → stale · failed → failed · offline → offline.
Each variant exists in exactly one state (see 04.A6). Draw that one cell as described, and fill the row's other four cells with the reason given for that row (B12).
 R1 "Updating…" → updating → refreshing. Stack two sub-cells vertically in the one cell: "under 1s: no hairline" above "1s or longer: hairline". The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while refreshing".
 R2 "Updated just now" / "Updated 12m ago" / "Updated 2h ago" (the system relative date) → updated → fresh. Stack all three strings as specimen text in the one cell. The refreshing, failed and offline cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while fresh". The stale cell: "Does not apply — stale is stated per fact (R5)".
 R3 "Couldn't refresh · Retry" → failed → failed, with the retry glyph and the Retry target. The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only after a refresh fails".
 R4 "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" → offline → offline, with the offline glyph. The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while offline".
 R5 per-fact stale → fact-stale → stale: the card shows the header ("1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with its ScopeChip) with no freshness line under it, then the air row "AQI 42 · Good" with the R5 line "Observed 7:00 AM · AirNow — 11 hours ago" under it. Show the air row's value line only: no AQI track and no EPA hue (B17); label the cell "track omitted: AqiBand". The rest of the card stays undimmed. The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while one fact is stale".
 R6 widget past horizon → widget-horizon → stale: "As of 7:40 AM · Open to refresh", in a 338×158 widget crop (its card is 370 wide, inside the 390 column). The widget shows the label "Larkspur Loop", then two rows, "Clark Public Utilities · in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct" and "HOA dues · in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov", with no provenance marks, then the R6 line. The time is today's, so no weekday is shown. The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while the widget is past its refresh horizon".
BELOW the grid, draw a "what does not change" strip: the same 358-wide card at 100% in the fresh and refreshing states, side by side, with identical layout, labelled "no dim, no skeleton, no reflow while refreshing".
Dark twin: all 30 cells in dark tokens, same geometry, on its 2400-wide artboard.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale, 2400 wide)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R3 and R4 at caption 40pt. The line wraps, and "Retry" moves to its own line as a full-width text button with its label at 44pt and a hit area at least 44pt tall that grows with the text. The glyph scales to 32pt.
- 200% (Android 412): the same at 24sp, with the label at 26sp and a hit area at least 48dp tall that grows with the text.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10, scope changed): the light grid again at 100% scale, not 50%, fully desaturated, in the same 2170-wide geometry, so the 12/16 lines stay legible. Every drawn cell reads "yes — words state the state"; Does-not-apply cells get no verdict.
- INCREASE CONTRAST: R3 and R4 with the line and glyph in text.strong; Retry stays primary.700.

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Changes are announced in a polite live region, never an assertive one (iOS: an accessibility announcement queued behind current speech (default or low priority); Android: accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"; web: aria-live="polite").
- Non-colour: stale is stated in words.
- Target rule: Retry is a target (B13).
- Ageing text is announced once, not every minute.
- Spoken example: "You're offline, as of 7:04 AM".

COPY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Relative time for recency ("Updated 12m ago"). "As of" plus an absolute time for offline or frozen data ("as of 7:04 AM"); add the weekday only when the time is not today.
- Never "Last synced", "refreshed at" or "last seen".
- Never a disappearing toast as the only proof.

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy)
- iOS widgets use the system Text(date, style: .relative).
- Android widgets use the equivalent system relative-time text.
- The hairline is each platform's system indeterminate progress indicator.
- Web: a polite live region.
- Same wording everywhere.

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three crops at 100%, each labelled with surface id, platform, width and fixture)
 a) f1-today-tab, Place B, web 390: the location row, the ScopeChip, "Updated 12m ago", then the air row "AQI 42 · Good" (value line only; label it "track omitted: AqiBand") with R5 beneath it. Label R5 "shown only when the air reading is stale".
 b) f7-today-widget, Home A, iOS 338×158pt, "Larkspur Loop", with the same two rows as R6 and the R6 line. The rest of the widget stays at full ink; only the stated line changes.
 c) f3-bills-list, Home A, web 390: the header "3 upcoming · $306.17 through Mon 2 Nov" with the "Your household" ScopeChip beside it (wrapping under it if narrow), and "Updated just now" under the header.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of dimming, skeletoning or reflowing a warm screen while refreshing, keep it and show "Updating…" (and the hairline after 1s) — because stale content is still useful.
- Instead of a hairline that loops until the request ends, stop it at 5s and leave "Updating…" — because idle loops stop within 5s.
- Instead of a custom animated hairline, use the platform's system indeterminate indicator — because a custom loop is a motion spec nobody needs to maintain.
- Instead of greying a whole widget when only AQI is old, put the age words on the air line — because the other facts are still current.
- Instead of a toast, use this line — because toasts vanish before people read them.
- Instead of "Last synced", write "Updated" or "As of" — because "synced" is jargon.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: updating · updated · failed · offline · fact-stale · widget-horizon. States: fresh · refreshing · stale · failed · offline. <size|platform> is "any". Example: "FreshnessLine / updating / refreshing / any / light".

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "04 FreshnessLine")
 04.A1 The hairline is the platform's system indeterminate progress indicator, with no custom duration. It is exempt from the house style's 300ms motion limit because it is a progress indicator, not a transition. Instead it is capped at 5s, per "idle loops stop within 5s", after which "Updating…" carries the state.
 04.A2 Source example strings were re-dated to the fixtures: "Observed 6:00 AM · AirNow — 9 hours ago" → "Observed 7:00 AM · AirNow — 11 hours ago"; "As of Mon 7:40 AM · Open to refresh" → "As of 7:40 AM · Open to refresh" (the time is today, so the weekday is dropped).
 04.A3 The f3-bills-list research header "Everyone at Larkspur Loop can see these bills · 3 upcoming · $306.17 through Mon 2 Nov" is not drawn: its scope sentence is a third scope wording, against house-style invariant 2 and the ScopeChip copy rules. The crop shows "3 upcoming · $306.17 through Mon 2 Nov" with the "Your household" ScopeChip instead ($306.17 = $142.18 + $84.00 + $79.99).
 04.A4 Date-rule exception (B16): "through Mon 2 Nov" is a range end, not a date row, so it has no relative count ("through in 14 days · Mon 2 Nov" reads badly).
 04.A5 Both 02 grids and the 03 greyscale grid are drawn at 100% on 2400-wide artboards (160 + 12 + 5 × 390 + 4 × 12 = 2170 wide), not at 1440 and not at the B10 50%, so the 12/16 lines stay at type-scale size and the greyscale verdicts can be checked. The 01 and 04 artboards stay 1440; the no-reflow strip and in-context crops are at 100%.
 04.A6 Each FreshnessLine variant is the line for exactly one state (updating → refreshing, updated → fresh, failed → failed, offline → offline, fact-stale and widget-horizon → stale); the other cells do not apply. The source lists variants and states independently, so this mapping is a reading of it.
 04.B1 "As of 7:40 AM · Open to refresh" (re-dated source string) · "idle loops stop within 5s" · "system indeterminate progress indicator · no custom duration · exempt from the 300ms rule, stopped within 5s (see Notes)" · "what does not change" · "no dim, no skeleton, no reflow while refreshing" · "under 1s: no hairline" · "1s or longer: hairline" · "track omitted: AqiBand" · "shown only when the air reading is stale" · "3 upcoming · $306.17 through Mon 2 Nov" · the widget rows "Clark Public Utilities · in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct" and "HOA dues · in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov" · the six row reasons ("Does not apply — this line appears only while refreshing" · "… only while fresh" · "Does not apply — stale is stated per fact (R5)" · "… only after a refresh fails" · "… only while offline" · "… only while one fact is stale" · "… only while the widget is past its refresh horizon").
 04.B2 Sourced, adapted: "3 upcoming · $306.17 through Mon 2 Nov" (f3-bills-list research, scope sentence replaced by the chip; see 04.A3).
 04.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 04.D Keep the sourced sentence "Everyone at Larkspur Loop can see these bills" on f3-bills-list, or replace it with the "Your household" chip as drawn? (04.A3)
 04.E Every FreshnessLine name (one per variant, in its one state).

DONE WHEN
- All 5 artboards exist with their exact names and stated widths, and Notes has the 04 entries with the earlier entries unchanged.
- Both grids have 6 rows × 5 columns with printed keys, are drawn at 100% (no "shown at" scale label anywhere), fit the 2400 artboard, and each row has one drawn cell and four "Does not apply" cells, each with its row's reason.
- The greyscale grid on 03 is at 100% with a verdict beside every drawn cell.
- The "what does not change" strip sits below the grid.
- The R5 cell shows the header with no freshness line, then the air row with the R5 line under it.
- The hairline is drawn as the system indicator in three poses (running, stopped after 5s, Reduce Motion), with no custom duration anywhere.
- No refreshing frame dims, skeletons or reflows the card, and no widget is greyed as a whole.
- Retry has a dashed target; no string says "Last synced", "refreshed at" or "last seen".
- Each in-context crop is labelled with its surface id, platform, width and fixture.
- Scope is stated only by the ScopeChip; no crop prints "Everyone at Larkspur Loop can see these bills".
