 R3 form offline → form: f1-add-place-sheet, signed in. The form uses a message strip in place of the FreshnessLine: "You're offline. We can't look up an address right now." in bodySmall 14/20 text.strong on a surface.sunken strip directly above the address field. The disabled field has a text.muted outline and text.muted placeholder (the disabled exemption), not a border token. The sheet keeps a visible "Close".
   offline: as described.
   reconnecting: the same message, with "Reconnecting" as a caption under it.
   back-online: the field is enabled and the message is gone. No FreshnessLine appears, because a form has no content age; print that note on the cell.
Dark twin: all 9 cells in dark tokens, same geometry, on its 2000-wide artboard. Disabled labels, the disabled button outline and the field outline use dark text.muted (exempt; print no ratio). The disabled button fill and the sunken strips follow B6.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale, 2000 wide)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R1 offline. The line and the what-still-works sentence wrap, the button goes full width, and the reason caption wraps under it at 40pt.
- 200% (Android 412): the same, with the button at least 48dp tall.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10, scope changed): the light grid again at 100% scale, not 50%, fully desaturated, in the same 1498-wide geometry, so the captions stay legible. Every cell reads "yes — words; disabled is stated, not only greyed".
- INCREASE CONTRAST: R1 offline with the reason caption and the what-still-works sentence in text.strong. The disabled label and outline stay text.muted, because the reason caption carries the meaning (B11).

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Disabled controls stay focusable and read their reason:
  iOS: "Compare with a friend, dimmed, Compare needs a connection."
  Android: "Compare with a friend, disabled, Compare needs a connection."
  Web: aria-disabled="true" (not the disabled attribute), with aria-describedby pointing at the reason caption.
- Status changes are announced politely.
- Target rule: the disabled control keeps its target size (B13).

COPY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Start with "You're offline." and then say what still works. On a screen with content, the offline FreshnessLine is the opener and the sentence under it says what still works; a form with no FreshnessLine opens its message strip with "You're offline."
- Exact strings: "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" · "You can still see everything saved here." · "You can keep taking photos." · "Compare needs a connection." · "Will upload when you're back online" · "You're offline. We can't look up an address right now."
- Never "No internet", "Connection lost" or "Network error".

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy): the same on iOS, Android and web.

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three crops at 100%, each labelled with surface id, platform, width and fixture)
 a) f8-native-share-compare, Place B, iOS 393: the offline line at the top with "You can still see everything saved here." under it, then the Place B location row "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with its "Saved place · Only you" ScopeChip, then "Compare with a friend" disabled with "Compare needs a connection." under it. Crop out everything else.
 b) f1-add-place-sheet, signed in, Android 412: R3 offline, with the sheet's visible "Close".
 c) f10-snap-capture-tray, Home A, iOS 393: R2 offline.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of a full-page offline illustration, keep the cached screen readable with the offline line on top — because people still need what they already had.
- Instead of silent dead buttons, disable the control and put the reason under it — because a button that does nothing looks broken.
- Instead of a red or amber banner, use plain or surface.sunken with text.strong — because being offline is a condition, not an error.
- Instead of blanking stale data, keep it with "as of 7:04 AM" — because a blank throws away true information.
- Instead of "You're offline" twice in a row, let the offline line open and the next sentence say what still works — because the repeat adds nothing.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: cached-screen · queued-writes · form. States: offline · reconnecting · back-online. <size|platform> is "any". Example: "OfflineNotice / form / reconnecting / any / dark".

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "05 OfflineNotice")
 05.A1 The form variant uses a message strip above the field in place of the FreshnessLine in all three states (the contract's anatomy puts the FreshnessLine at the top), and shows neither when back online, because a form has no content age. Its reason sits above the field, not under it.
 05.A2 The used-in line is the sentence "every surface with an offline state (43 of 59)", not a list of ids.
 05.A3 Both 02 grids and the 03 greyscale grid are drawn at 100% on 2000-wide artboards (160 + 24 + 3 × 422 + 2 × 24 = 1498 content width), not at 1440 and not at the B10 50%, so captions and bodySmall stay at type-scale size. The 01 and 04 artboards stay 1440; in-context crops are at 100%.
 05.A4 The copy rule "Start with 'You're offline.' and then say what still works" is met on content screens by the offline FreshnessLine as the opener plus a what-still-works sentence under it (bodySmall 14/20 text.secondary) that does not repeat "You're offline". The per-control reason captions carry what does not work.
 05.A5 The disabled button has a 1px text.muted outline on its sunken fill (matching the disabled field in R3), because sunken on a base card is about 1.1:1 and border tokens are never the only edge. Disabled label and outline are exempt from contrast; no ratio is printed.
 05.B1 "Reconnecting · as of 7:04 AM" · "Reconnecting" · "You can still see everything saved here." · "You can keep taking photos." · "plain" · "sunken strip".
 05.B2 Spoken labels: "Compare with a friend, dimmed, Compare needs a connection." · "Compare with a friend, disabled, Compare needs a connection."
 05.B3 Sourced, not invented: "Uploading 2 of 3" (the live-status pattern from the research brief, section 5).
 05.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 05.D none
 05.E Every OfflineNotice name.

DONE WHEN
- All 5 artboards exist with their exact names and stated widths, and Notes has the 05 entries with the earlier entries unchanged.
- Both grids have all 9 cells with printed keys, are drawn at 100% (no "shown at" scale label anywhere), fit the 2000 artboard, and R1 back-online shows both sub-cells stacked.
- The greyscale grid on 03 is at 100% with a verdict beside every cell.
- R1 and R2 back-online both show a FreshnessLine; R2 back-online reads "Uploading 2 of 3".
- R1 and R2 offline and reconnecting show a what-still-works sentence under the line, and no cell prints "You're offline" twice.
- Cached content is never dimmed or blanked; no frame uses a red, amber or other semantic banner.
- Every disabled control has its reason caption under it (the form's field: the message strip above it), stays focusable (a focus ring is drawn once), and keeps its 44pt / 48dp / 44px target; the disabled button has a text.muted outline.
- text.muted appears only on disabled labels, the disabled button outline and the disabled field; text on sunken strips is text.strong.
- The used-in line reads exactly "every surface with an offline state (43 of 59)".

name: StatusChip
job: One status per object (bills and invites), stated in words.
text:
########## SEND 1 OF 2 (paste on its own; wait for the stop before the next send) ##########
Component 00a-06: StatusChip, send 1 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

THIS SEND (in order)
 1. 00a · StatusChip · 01-anatomy · light
 2. 00a · Notes: add the subheading "06 StatusChip" with 06.A1–06.A6, 06.B2 and 06.D below. Leave earlier entries unchanged.
Then stop and wait for send 2.

PURPOSE (print): One status per object (bills and invites), stated in words.
USED IN (print): f3-bills-list, f3-bill-detail-web, f3-members-roster, f8-seasonal-aha, f10-bill-provenance, f9-block-founders-panel.

ANATOMY (callouts on "Overdue")
① Pill, radius pill, height 24pt / 24dp / 24px.
② Padding 8 horizontal; 4 gap between glyph and text.
③ Leading 12pt glyph, the only place a semantic hue may appear. No glyph is a plain circle or ring (B8).
④ Text captionMedium 12/16/500, text.strong. captionMedium is a published design-system style (design-tokens.md) and is the source spec's "caption medium"; it is recorded on Notes (06.A6).
⑤ Fill surface.sunken (dark: B6). No border.
⑥ The chip is not a target; its row is (B13). Print "not a target".

GLYPHS (a labelled row; draw exactly)
- Upcoming and deadline chip: calendar outline, text.strong.
- Deadline "Today": calendar outline; light text.strong, dark semantic.warning.
- Due today: clock face drawn as a rounded square with hands, not a circle; light text.strong (warning fails on sunken), dark semantic.warning.
- Overdue: exclamation mark in a triangle outline, semantic.error.
- Paid: plain check stroke, no enclosing shape, semantic.success.
- Expires: hourglass, text.strong.
- Declined: × stroke, text.strong.
- Waiting for your OK: speech-bubble outline with three short dashes inside (not dots; B8), primary.700 standing in for semantic.info (dark: primary.400 (dark link)).

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE
Light, on sunken: text.strong #374151 9.37 · semantic.error #DC2626 4.39 · semantic.success #059669 3.42 · semantic.warning #D97706 2.89 (FAILS, so light warning glyphs use text.strong) · primary.700 #0369a1 5.39.
Dark, on dark raised (chips on dark base and dark app): semantic.warning 4.59 · semantic.success 3.88 · semantic.error 3.03 · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8 6.83 · dark text.strong #F1F5F9 13.35.
Dark, on dark sunken #0F172A (= dark base; chips on a dark raised card): semantic.warning 5.60 · semantic.success 4.74 · semantic.error 3.70 · primary.400 (dark link) 8.33 · dark text.strong 16.30.

ACCESSIBILITY (print)
- The word carries the state and is read at the end of the row label: "Comcast, 79 dollars 99, due in 14 days, Monday 2 November, Upcoming". The glyph is decorative (hidden from assistive tech).
- Non-colour cue: the word. Target: never the chip; the row is (B13).

COPY (print)
- Exactly one chip per row. Sentence case. Dates show the weekday.
- Beyond tomorrow, deadlines, due dates and expiries lead with the relative count: "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct"; "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct"; "due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct". Tonight, today and tomorrow stand alone ("Today"), and a date or time today shows no weekday (write "today").
- Past dates on chips show the date only, with no "x days ago": "Declined · Thu 15 Oct". This is an exception to B16 (06.A5).
- Never "Paid" as a verb in notifications; write "marked paid".

PLATFORMS (print): no platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (print)
- Warning-hue text on a warning tint → text.strong on surface.sunken with the hue on the glyph only, because warning text on its tint is about 3:1.
- Two chips on one row → the one status that matters, because two chips compete and get misread.
- A status chip on a person ("Verified", "Active") → the role in plain text, because people are not statuses.
- A warning-tinted countdown pill (founding window) → a neutral date chip, because countdowns pressure people.
- The date before the count ("Mon 26 Oct · in 7 days") → "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct", because the house style and DateRow lead with the count and every consuming surface copies this chip.
- A disc-shaped status dot → the listed glyphs, because circles belong to ProvenanceMark.

NOTES (subheading "06 StatusChip")
 06.A1 Warning glyphs (Due today, deadline Today) are text.strong in light mode (semantic.warning is 2.89 on sunken) and semantic.warning in dark mode (4.59 on dark raised, 5.60 on dark sunken). "Waiting for your OK" uses primary.700 in place of semantic.info.
 06.A2 Deadline chip ORDER CHANGED: the source spec writes the date first ("Oct 26 · 18 days"). This board leads with the count, matching the house style, the research brief (section 6) and DateRow ("in 11 days · Fri 30 Oct"). All 6 consuming surfaces (and every DateRow-style chip) copy this chip, so any date-first decision must come before publishing.
 06.A3 The invite expiry chip also leads with the count. Alternative if rejected: "Expires Mon 26 Oct".
 06.A4 Re-dated to the fixtures: "Expires Sep 23" → "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct"; "Declined · Sep 15" → "Declined · Thu 15 Oct"; "Oct 26 · 18 days" → "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct".
 06.A5 Past dates on chips show the date only (no "x days ago"), for example "Declined · Thu 15 Oct". This is an exception to B16.
 06.A6 Type: the chip text uses captionMedium 12/16/500, a published design-system style (design-tokens.md) and the source spec's "caption medium". It is not in the house-style type list (caption is 12/16/400), so it is recorded here as a type-scale deviation (B5).
 06.B2 Spoken label: "Comcast, 79 dollars 99, due in 14 days, Monday 2 November, Upcoming".
 06.D Deadline chip: count first (as drawn) or date first? (06.A2)

DONE WHEN
- 01-anatomy has every block above; no glyph is a plain disc or ring, and semantic hues appear only on glyphs.
- Notes has 06.A1–06.A6, 06.B2 and 06.D, with earlier entries unchanged.

########## SEND 2 OF 2 (paste on its own; wait for the stop before the next send) ##########
Component 00a-06: StatusChip, send 2 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message. Keep 01-anatomy as drawn and reuse its glyphs.

THIS SEND (in order)
 1. 00a · StatusChip · 02-variants-states · light
 2. 00a · StatusChip · 04-in-context · light
 3. 00a · StatusChip · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 4. 00a · StatusChip · 02-variants-states · dark
 5. 00a · Notes: append 06.B1, 06.C and 06.E under "06 StatusChip".
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

GRID (02-variants-states: 9 rows × 1 state)
Draw each chip three times side by side: in a surface.base row, on a surface.raised card and in a surface.app list. Print "on surface.base", "on surface.raised" or "on surface.app" in each cell label. They are one chip in three contexts, not variants.
Column: "default (the only state)", key default.
Rows (specimen text → key; a key never contains the specimen):
 1 "Upcoming" → upcoming
 2 "Due today" → due-today
 3 "Overdue" → overdue
 4 "Paid" → paid
 5 "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct" → expires
 6 "Declined · Thu 15 Oct" → declined (past date, date only: 06.A5)
 7 "Waiting for your OK" → waiting
 8 "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct" (deadline chip, count first) → deadline
 9 "Today" (deadline chip) → deadline-today
Dark twin: all 27 cells in dark tokens. Chips on dark base and dark app are filled dark surface.raised; chips on the dark raised card are filled dark surface.sunken (B6).

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context: three crops)
 a) f3-bills-list, Home A, iOS 393: "Clark Public Utilities · $142.18 · due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct", "City of Vancouver water · $84.00 · due in 9 days · Wed 28 Oct" and "Comcast · $79.99 · due in 14 days · Mon 2 Nov", each with one "Upcoming" chip.
 b) f3-members-roster, Home A, web 390: "Maya Chen · Owner" and "Sam Ortega · Member" with NO chips, and the invite row "priya@example.com" with "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct".
 c) f8-seasonal-aha, Place B, Android 412: "Online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct." with the deadline chip "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". Under it, a SourceCaption "Washington Secretary of State · statewide · as of today" with the official mark and the word "Official" printed beside the mark, once on this crop. Label that word "legend once per surface".

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale)
- AX5 (iOS 393): the row "Comcast · $79.99 · due in 14 days · Mon 2 Nov" with "Upcoming". The pair stacks, the chip moves under the title and becomes a wrapping rounded rectangle (radius lg 12) at 40pt with a 24pt glyph. Also draw chip 5 at AX5 to show the longest string wrapping.
- 200% (Android 412): the same at 24sp.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10): every cell reads "yes — the word carries the state". Add a WRONG example: two chips that differ only in fill hue, with the fix "fix: words, one chip".
- Print "Increase Contrast: nothing changes — chip text is already text.strong; glyph hues are decorative because the word carries the state".

PUBLISH KEYS
"StatusChip / <row key> / default / any / <light|dark>". Publish one name per chip per theme; the three backgrounds are one chip. Examples: "StatusChip / overdue / default / any / light" · "StatusChip / deadline / default / any / dark".

NOTES (append)
 06.B1 Invented strings, copied verbatim from this send: grid rows 5, 6 and 8; the three crop a bill rows; the crop b roster rows "Maya Chen · Owner" and "Sam Ortega · Member"; the crop c caption "Washington Secretary of State · statewide · as of today"; the crop c annotation "legend once per surface"; and "fix: words, one chip".
 06.C Any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 06.E Every StatusChip name: 9 chips × light and dark = 18 names.

DONE WHEN
- Both grids have 9 rows on three backgrounds with printed keys, and no key contains a fixture string or date.
- Every future date beyond tomorrow leads with the count, the only past date shows the date only, and no date today carries a weekday; each crop row has at most one chip, the people rows have none, and crop c prints "Official" once.
- Notes has 06.B1, 06.C and 06.E.

name: KindGlyph
job: One drawn glyph per dated kind, used in tiles, rows, pickup card and widget.
text:
########## SEND 1 OF 3 (paste on its own; wait for the stop before the next send) ##########
Component 00a-07: KindGlyph, send 1 of 3. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

THIS SEND: 00a · KindGlyph · 01-anatomy · light
Then stop and wait for send 2.

PURPOSE (print): One drawn glyph per dated kind, used in tiles, rows, the pickup card and the widget.
USED IN (print): x-date-sheet, f5-today-calendar-strip, f4-today-pickup-card, f7-today-widget, f10-extraction-confirm, f3-household-calendar, x-place-file.

ANATOMY (callouts on "Recycling" at 24pt, glyph 2, and on the "Pickup day" tile, glyph 3)
① Line icon on a 24pt / 24dp / 24px grid, 2pt stroke, round caps and joins, text.strong. Use the Pantopus design system's icon style; draw any missing glyph in that style.
② Tile: 42pt rounded square, radius lg 12, fill surface.sunken, 24pt glyph centred.
③ Tile label 8pt below: label 13/18/600, text.strong, centred, wraps to two lines.
④ The whole tile-plus-label cell is the target (B13). The kind picker is a 2-column grid with 8pt gaps: cells are 176 wide on iOS 393 (16pt side margins), 186 on Android 412 and 175 on web 390, all 88 tall. Draw the iOS dimension lines.
⑤ Selected indicator position: 16pt, in the top-right corner of the 176-wide cell, outside the 42pt tile, so it never overlaps the glyph. Mark it on the iOS cell.
⑥ Selected tile edge: 1.5px primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)) around the 42pt tile, so the tile shape stays visible on its primary.50 fill (primary.50 on base is only 1.07). Mark it on a selected iOS cell beside ⑤.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE
text.strong #374151 on base 10.31, on sunken 9.37 · text.primary #111827 (selected label) on primary.50 16.64 · text.muted #9CA3AF 2.54 (disabled only) · primary.700 #0369a1 on primary.50 5.57, on base 5.93 (selected tile edge) · primary.50 #f0f9ff on base 1.07 (fill, never an edge) · dark text.strong #F1F5F9 on dark raised 13.35 · dark text.primary #E5E7EB on primary.900 #0c4a6e 7.64 · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8 on primary.900 4.42 (radio, check and edge only), on dark base 8.33 (selected tile edge).

THE SET (draw all 17 in order; label each "<row label> · key: <key>")
 # | kind | row label (exact) | key | drawing
 1 | garbage | Garbage | garbage | lidded wheeled cart
 2 | recycling | Recycling | recycling | cart with three chasing arrows on its body
 3 | garbage+recycling | Recycling and garbage | garbage-recycling | two overlapping carts
 4 | bulk | Bulk pickup | bulk | armchair
 5 | move-in | Move-in date | move-in | open box with an arrow entering it
 6 | lease ends | Lease ends | lease-ends | key over a door outline
 7 | notice deadline | Notice deadline | notice-deadline | envelope with a small flag
 8 | insurance renews | Insurance renews | insurance-renews | shield with a circular arrow drawn as an open arc
 9 | warranty ends | Warranty ends | warranty-ends | tag with a wrench
 10 | HOA dues | HOA dues | hoa-dues | three adjoining rooftops
 11 | property-tax appeal | Property-tax appeal | property-tax-appeal | document with an upward arrow
 12 | property-tax due | Property-tax due | property-tax-due | document with a dollar sign
 13 | voter registration | Voter registration | voter-registration | ballot entering a slotted box
 14 | bill | Bill | bill | receipt with a zigzag bottom edge
 15 | home event | Home date | home-event | house outline with a small calendar page
 16 | task | Task | task | rounded-square checkbox with a check stroke
 17 | package | Package | package | parcel with tape
Property tax is one kind with two uses; 11 and 12 share the document base. Cart wheels are round sub-parts, which B8 allows. Row 15 is labelled "Home date" because the glossary rules out "event".

TILE → GLYPH MAP (print)
Pickup day → 3 · Move-in date → 5 · Lease ends → 6 · Notice deadline → 7 · Insurance renews → 8 · Warranty ends → 9 · HOA dues → 10 · Property-tax appeal → 11 · Voter registration → 13 · Bill → 14.
No tile (rows, pickup card, widget and tray only): 4, 12, 15, 16, 17, and the pickup glyphs, chosen by which bins go out: "Garbage only" → 1; "Recycling and garbage" → 3; a recycling-only pickup (a city with its own recycling day; not Home A or Place B) → 2.

ACCESSIBILITY (print)
- Decorative (hidden) when a text label is adjacent; otherwise labelled with the row label ("Recycling"). Always paired with visible text; widget and tray glyphs carry their word.
- Each tile is one element: "Pickup day, selected, 1 of 10" (iOS: a button with the selected trait; Android: RadioButton semantics; web: role="radio" inside role="radiogroup").
- Non-colour: shape plus label; selection is the dot or check plus the edge, fill and ink change.
- Target: the tile cell or row, never the glyph alone (B13).

COPY (print)
- Tile labels, exactly: Pickup day · Move-in date · Lease ends · Notice deadline · Insurance renews · Warranty ends · HOA dues · Property-tax appeal · Voter registration · Bill.
- Row labels, exactly: the "row label" column of THE SET. The ones with no tile are Garbage · Recycling · Recycling and garbage · Bulk pickup · Property-tax due · Home date · Task · Package.
- "Pickup day", never "trash day", "garbage day" or "bin day"; "Date", never "event" or "deadline item".

PLATFORMS (print)
- The same glyph on all three platforms. The widget glyph is silhouette-safe like ProvenanceMark: one ink, inner detail cut out, so it survives one-colour accented rendering.
- The one-column large-text list: a trailing check on iOS and web; Material 3 radio buttons on Android.

INSTEAD OF (print)
- Hue-coded glyphs as the only class cue → a silhouette per kind plus a label, because hue alone fails in greyscale and for colour-blind users.
- An unlabelled glyph → the kind's row label beside it, because the glyphs are not universal.
- Guessing a tile's glyph → the TILE → GLYPH map, because every later picker copies this one.
- Selection shown with the focus ring → fill + edge + radio dot + label ink, because selection must look different from focus.
- An empty-ring radio on iOS or web large-text rows → a trailing check on the selected row and nothing on the others, because iOS has no radio control and an empty ring is the unconfirmed mark's shape.
- Emoji or a second icon set → the Pantopus icon style, because the house style forbids a new icon set.

DONE WHEN
- 01-anatomy shows all 17 glyphs with their row labels and keys, the TILE → GLYPH map, the indicator position outside the tile, the selected tile edge, and every printed block above.

########## SEND 2 OF 3 (paste on its own; wait for the stop before the next send) ##########
Component 00a-07: KindGlyph, send 2 of 3. Follow the board rules from the setup message. Use the set (with its row labels), map and anatomy on 01-anatomy.

THIS SEND (in order)
 1. 00a · KindGlyph · 02-variants-states · light
 2. 00a · KindGlyph · 02-variants-states · dark
 3. 00a · Notes: add the subheading "07 KindGlyph" with 07.A1–07.A3, 07.B2 and 07.D below. Leave earlier entries unchanged.
Then stop and wait for send 3.

PART A (02): 17 glyph rows × 4 variant columns, all in the default state.
- row (24pt): the glyph with its row label (THE SET, exact) in bodySmall to its right.
- tile (42pt): tile plus tile label. Glyphs without a tile in the map: "Does not apply — no picker tile; see the map".
- widget (16pt): the glyph with a 1.5pt stroke, its row label beside it in caption.
- tray: 16pt, one ink, dark text.primary on the dark mail-snap tray (dark surface.raised). Label "tray: monochrome, one ink".

PART B (02): the "Pickup day" kind (glyph 3). 4 rows (row · tile · widget · tray) × 5 columns (label → key): default → default · selected tile → selected · disabled → disabled · focused, not selected → focus · selected + focused → selected-focus. Every cell is drawn or prints its reason.
- tile. default: no indicator. selected: fill primary.50 (dark: primary.900) with a 1.5px primary.700 edge around the tile (dark: primary.400 (dark link)); the label stays 13/18/600 with ink text.primary (dark: dark text.primary); in the cell's top-right corner, outside the tile, the 16pt indicator in primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)): a 1.5px ring with an 8pt filled centre (B8 exception, 07.A1). Print "selected = fill + edge + radio dot + label ink". disabled: glyph and label text.muted, fill surface.muted, caption "Already on file" under the label in text.secondary. focus: the B14 ring only, no fill, no edge, no dot. selected-focus: selected plus the B14 ring outside the selected edge.
- row. default as in Part A. selected: "Does not apply — rows are not selectable". disabled: glyph and label text.muted, caption "Already on file" in text.secondary. focus and selected-focus: "Does not apply — the glyph is decorative; its DateRow owns focus".
- widget. default only; the other four: "Does not apply — the widget is read-only".
- tray. default only; the other four: "Does not apply — the tray is read-only".
Then draw the 10 tiles, default, as one 2-column picker in map order.
Dark twin: Parts A and B and the picker in dark tokens; the tile fill follows B6.

NOTES (subheading "07 KindGlyph")
 07.A1 Radio indicators vs invariant 1 ("filled vs hollow means provenance and nothing else"). Two flagged exceptions: (a) the selected tile's corner indicator, a ring with a filled centre (unselected tiles show nothing), from the source spec's "filled radio dot"; (b) Android Material 3 radios in the 200% list, whose unselected option is an empty ring, the UNCONFIRMED silhouette. iOS AX5 and web 200% lists use a trailing check instead, because iOS has no native radio control.
 07.A2 The selected label keeps label 13/18/600 and changes ink from text.strong to text.primary. The source spec's "bold label" is shown by the fill, edge, corner dot and ink change instead of an off-scale 700. No type-scale deviation is recorded. Alternative if rejected: record 700 as a deviation.
 07.A3 Part B has five state columns for every variant (default · selected · disabled · focus · selected-focus). The source lists default · selected tile · disabled; focus is added to show that selection differs from focus. The selected tile also gains a 1.5px primary.700 edge (dark: primary.400 (dark link)), because its primary.50 fill alone (1.07 on base) would lose the tile shape; this matches ChoiceChip and AddressChip.
 07.B2 Spoken label: "Pickup day, selected, 1 of 10".
 07.D (1) Radio indicators (07.A1): keep (b) platform-native, or use the trailing check on Android too? Should (a) become a check stroke in the corner? (2) Selected label (07.A2): weight 600 with the ink change, or 700? (3) Widget bill and HOA lines (07.A8, added in send 3): you-added, or official when a bill comes from a verified source?

DONE WHEN

Inside each row the pair stacks (B9): the tile, grown to 64pt with the glyph at 48pt, sits at the leading edge on top, and the label at 44pt/600 wraps below it across the row width minus the trailing check column (24pt check + 12pt gap), about 301pt. Other rows show no indicator. No ring is drawn on iOS.

Unselected: an empty ring in text.secondary (B8 exceptions, 07.A1).
- Web 200% zoom (390): the iOS form (stacked rows, trailing check on the selected row, nothing on the others), built as role="radio" rows.
- GREYSCALE (B10 subset): the 17 row glyphs and all of Part B, verdict "yes — shape + label". Selected reads by the dot (tile) or the check (iOS and web rows) plus edge, fill and ink, not by fill hue alone.

PUBLISH KEYS
"KindGlyph / <kind key> / <state key> / <variant key: row · tile · widget · tray> / <light|dark>". The widget crop uses the house style's 338×354pt size, because three entries with provenance words do not fit 338×158; each entry is two lines (title; date + mark + word).

Its headline names tomorrow's pickup, so it shows the weekday date alone. Its caption says "as of today" because a date today carries no weekday (B16).
 07.A7 Indicator and large-text geometry: the 16pt selected indicator sits in the cell's top-right corner, outside the 42pt tile. At AX5, Android 200% and web 200% the tile grows to 64pt so the glyph can scale to 48pt (B9) with an 8pt margin, and it stacks above its label in each full-width row (B9 "pairs stack"); the trailing check or radio aligns to the label's first line; words never break mid-word. The Android radio is 24dp, the 2× cap of the platform's 20dp control.

text:

Component 00a-08: AddressChip, send 1 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message.
AddressChip is paired with the ScopeChip sentence you drew in 00a-03. Reuse it exactly: "Only you will see this."

THIS SEND (in order)

PURPOSE (print): Shows a held or selected address as a label: never a map, never coordinates.
USED IN (print): f1-email-verify-handoff, f1-save-confirmation, f1-add-place-sheet, f8-compare-arrival-header.

ANATOMY (callouts on the held chip for Place B)
① Pill, radius pill, fill surface.raised, with a 1px border.default edge as decoration only (1.24:1 on the base card, 1.18:1 on the chip fill). Surface.raised on base is about 1.05:1, so on a base card this edge is in practice the chip's only visible outline; the pin and text carry the chip, as in ⑨. Meaning never depends on the edge.
② 16pt pin glyph in text.strong, 8pt gap. Its round hole is a sub-part (B8).
③ Street "1107 NE Birchfield Ct": bodySmallMedium 14/20/500, text.primary.
④ City "Camas, WA 98607" on the line below: caption 12/16, text.secondary (4.63:1 on raised). On a selected fill the city turns text.primary (see R1 selected in send 2).
⑤ Padding 12 horizontal, 8 vertical; minimum height 44pt.
⑥ At 390 wide, street and city each wrap and are never truncated.
⑦ Optional "Save it", only when the chip is a selectable suggestion row: a text button in label 13/18/600 primary.700, with a target (B13).
⑧ SCOPE SENTENCE RULE (defined only here; every other mention points to ⑧): "Only you will see this." sits 8pt below every held, recovery and duplicate chip. The sender label (R4) is the one exception: it describes someone else's place, so it carries no sentence, and the sentence goes under the recipient's own address field instead. Print "no scope sentence: not your place" on the exception.
⑨ DARK EDGE RULE: fill dark surface.raised. Dark border.default on dark raised is 1.00:1, so dark mode has no border.default edge; the pin and text carry the chip. The selected state keeps its 1.5px primary.400 (dark link) edge. Draw a light and a dark default chip side by side, labelled "dark: no border". The light chip sits on a surface.base card; the dark chip sits on its own dark surface.base card (radius lg 12), never directly on the light artboard.

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE
text.primary #111827 on raised 16.98, on primary.50 16.64 (selected street and city) · text.secondary #6B7280 on raised 4.63, on primary.50 4.54 (not used on the selected fill) · text.strong #374151 on sunken 9.37 · primary.700 #0369a1 on base 5.93, on primary.50 5.57 · border.default #E5E7EB on base 1.24, on raised 1.18 (decoration only) · surface.raised on base 1.05 · dark text.secondary #94A3B8 on dark raised 5.71, on primary.900 3.69 (FAILS, so the selected dark city uses dark text.primary) · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8 on primary.900 4.42 (edge and check only) · dark text.primary #E5E7EB on primary.900 7.64.

ACCESSIBILITY (print)
- Reads the full address: "1107 Northeast Birchfield Court, Camas, Washington 98607". Selected: "…, selected". Sender: "Dana, Camas, Washington". Expired: "1107 Northeast Birchfield Court, Camas, no longer held, Search again, button".
- Non-colour: selected is the check plus the edge; expired is stated in words.
- The chip itself is a label. Its actions ("Save it", "Use for Today", "Search again") are targets (B13).

COPY (print)
- Scope sentence: see ⑧.
- Exact strings (each string is everything after the colon; no outer quote marks belong to it):
  Hold message: We're holding it for 7 days
  Recovery row: 1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas — Save it
  Duplicate message: You already saved this as “Mom’s house” (the curly quotes are part of the string)
  Duplicate action: Use for Today
  Sender label, compact form: Dana · Camas, WA
- Glossary: "Saved place", never "bookmark", "preview" or "draft".

PLATFORMS (print): no platform differences. Draw the same chip on all three platforms.

INSTEAD OF (print)
- A blank retype field when the server holds the address → the held AddressChip, because retyping loses people between steps.
- A map or coordinates → the street and city as text, because a label is enough and a map leaks location.
- An alarm colour for an expired hold → a neutral sunken chip with "Search again", because expiry is not an error.
- A held or selectable chip without its scope sentence → add it (⑧), because a held address must say who sees it.
- The sentence under a sender's chip → under the recipient's own field (⑧), because it would be false about the sender's place.
- A text.secondary city on a selected fill → text.primary (dark: dark text.primary), because dark text.secondary on primary.900 is 3.69.

NOTES (subheading "08 AddressChip")
 08.A1 Dark mode has no border.default edge (1.00:1 on dark raised); the selected 1.5px primary.400 (dark link) edge stays (⑨). In light mode the decorative edge is 1.24 on the base card and 1.18 on the chip fill; with raised on base at about 1.05, it is in practice the only outline, and the pin and text carry the chip.
 08.A2 The sender label (R4) has no scope sentence (⑧). The source spec says the chip is always paired with the sentence.
 08.A3 R1–R3 use the Place B address as specimens, although in the fixture story Jordan already saved it on Sat 10 Oct. The duplicate message You already saved this as “Mom’s house” is kept verbatim, with curly inner quotes, for the specimen only.
 08.A4 The recovery-row example "1402 NE 3rd Ave, Camas — Save it" became "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas — Save it" (the Place B fixture).
 08.A5 Selected cells set both street and city in text.primary (dark: dark text.primary, 7.64 on primary.900). The city does not keep text.secondary there: dark text.secondary on primary.900 is 3.69, and light text.secondary on primary.50 is only 4.54.
 08.B1 Invented strings: "We're no longer holding this address." · "Search again" · "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas" (the prefilled search) · "Check your email" (crop a heading) · "Your address" (the recipient's field label, crop c) · "no scope sentence: not your place" · "dark: no border".
 08.B2 Spoken labels: "1107 Northeast Birchfield Court, Camas, Washington 98607" · "…, selected" · "Dana, Camas, Washington" · "1107 Northeast Birchfield Court, Camas, no longer held, Search again, button" (expired).
 08.D Sender label without the scope sentence (08.A2): accept?

DONE WHEN
- 01-anatomy has callouts ①–⑨, the light and dark pair (the dark chip on its own dark surface.base card), and every printed block.
- Notes has 08.A1–08.A5, 08.B1, 08.B2 and 08.D, with earlier entries unchanged.

########## SEND 2 OF 2 (paste on its own; wait for the stop before the next send) ##########
Component 00a-08: AddressChip, send 2 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message. Use the anatomy, the scope sentence rule ⑧ and the dark edge rule ⑨ on 01-anatomy.

THIS SEND (in order)
 1. 00a · AddressChip · 02-variants-states · light
 2. 00a · AddressChip · 04-in-context · light
 3. 00a · AddressChip · 03-scaling-greyscale · light
 4. 00a · AddressChip · 02-variants-states · dark
 5. 00a · Notes: append 08.C and 08.E under "08 AddressChip".
Then stop and wait for the next component message.

GRID (02: 4 rows × 3 columns)
The addresses are specimens only (08.A3). Columns (label → key): default → default · selected → selected · expired (neutral) → expired. R1–R3 follow ⑧; R4 is its exception. Use the exact strings from COPY on 01-anatomy.
 R1 held → held (f1-email-verify-handoff): the chip, then the hold message We're holding it for 7 days, then the scope sentence.
   selected: fill primary.50 (dark: primary.900), a 1.5px primary.700 edge (dark: primary.400 (dark link)), and a trailing 16pt check stroke in primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)). Street and city are both text.primary (16.64 on primary.50; dark: dark text.primary, 7.64 on primary.900). The city never keeps text.secondary on the selected fill (08.A5).
   expired: fill surface.sunken, text in text.strong, the caption "We're no longer holding this address." and a text button "Search again", which opens search prefilled with "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas". No warning or error hue.
 R2 recovery row → recovery-row (f1-save-confirmation): a full-width 44pt row with the recovery row string 1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas — Save it, where "Save it" is the action; then the scope sentence.
   selected: the R1 selected treatment (including text.primary for all text), with the check replacing "Save it". expired: the R1 expired treatment in row form.
 R3 duplicate → duplicate (f1-add-place-sheet): the chip, then the duplicate message You already saved this as “Mom’s house”, then the duplicate action Use for Today as a 44pt text button; then the scope sentence.
   selected: the R1 selected treatment (including text.primary for all text), after "Use for Today" is chosen. expired: "Does not apply — a saved place does not expire".
 R4 sender label → sender (f8-compare-arrival-header): the pin glyph, "Dana" in bodySmallMedium and "Camas, WA" in caption; compact form Dana · Camas, WA. No scope sentence (⑧).
   selected and expired: "Does not apply — a sender label is neither selectable nor held".
Dark twin: all 12 cells in dark tokens, following ⑨; selected cells use dark text.primary for street and city.

IN CONTEXT (04: three crops)
 a) f1-email-verify-handoff, web 390: the heading "Check your email", with R1 default under it.
 b) f1-save-confirmation, iOS 393: R2 default.
 c) f8-compare-arrival-header, web 1440 cropped to 720 wide: the R4 sender chip over Dana's column with no sentence, and in the empty second column the recipient's own address field, labelled "Your address", with "Only you will see this." under it.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03)
- AX5 (iOS 393): R1 and R2. Street and city wrap onto several lines, the pill becomes a rounded rectangle (radius lg 12), "Save it" moves under the address as a full-width 44pt button, and the pin scales to 32pt.
- 200% (Android 412): the same, with the button at 48dp.
- Web 200% zoom (390): the same.
- GREYSCALE (B10): "yes — pin + text; selected = check + edge"; expired cells: "yes — words".
- INCREASE CONTRAST: R1 default with the city line in text.strong; the decorative border is unchanged.

PUBLISH KEYS
"AddressChip / <held · recovery-row · duplicate · sender> / <default · selected · expired> / any / <light|dark>", one name per drawn cell: 9 per theme. Example: "AddressChip / held / expired / any / light".

NOTES (append)
 08.C Any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 08.E Every AddressChip name: 9 cells × light and dark = 18 names.

DONE WHEN
- Both grids have 4 × 3 cells with printed keys, and every "Does not apply" cell prints its reason.
- ⑧ holds in every cell and crop, including crop c; selected has the fill, the 1.5px edge (in dark too) and the check; expired uses no warning or error hue.
- In every selected cell, light and dark, street and city are text.primary (dark: dark text.primary, 7.64); no text.secondary sits on a selected fill.
- The COPY strings appear exactly, including the curly quotes in the duplicate message.
- No street or city is truncated, and no map or coordinates appear.

text:
Component 00a-09: ChoiceChip. Follow the board rules (B1–B18) from the setup message. This is the last component; after this batch the board is complete.

ARTBOARDS AND BATCH PLAN (this turn, in this order, exact names)
 1. 00a · ChoiceChip · 01-anatomy · light: callouts, the token table, the per-platform R3 and R5 forms, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF
