PURPOSE (print): Small single-choice chips for channel, role, time and filter; they are never status badges.
USED IN (print): f3-invite-composer, f4-briefing-optin-card, f10-mail-piece-photo, f3-bills-list, f4-notification-settings.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy; callouts on the time group "6:30 AM · 7:00 AM · 7:30 AM · 8:00 AM", 7:00 AM selected)
① Height 32pt / 32dp / 32px visual inside a target (B13). Draw both outlines.
② Radius pill; padding 12 horizontal; 8 gap between chips.
③ Label 13/18/600.
④ Selected: fill primary.50; 1px primary.700 outline (5.93:1 on base, so the shape stays visible although the fill is only 1.07:1); text primary.700 (5.57:1 on the fill); a leading 12pt check stroke in primary.700 with a 4pt gap. Dark: fill primary.900, 1px primary.400 (dark link) outline, text dark text.primary, check primary.400 (dark link).
⑤ Unselected: 1px outline in text.secondary (dark: dark text.secondary) and text.strong label. Print "spec border.strong → text.secondary (see Notes)": border.strong is 1.47:1, and the house style says an input's only edge uses text.secondary ink or darker.
⑥ Focus: the B14 ring, shown on an unselected chip and on a selected chip.
⑦ Disabled: text and 1px outline both text.muted (dark: dark text.muted), no check, and a reason caption under the group in text.secondary. No border token is the edge. Print "disabled controls are exempt from WCAG contrast; the reason caption carries the meaning (see Notes)".

TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE (01-anatomy)
primary.700 #0369a1 on primary.50 5.57, on base 5.93 (selected outline) · primary.50 #f0f9ff on base 1.07 (fill only) · text.strong #374151 on base 10.31 · text.secondary #6B7280 4.83 (unselected outline) · text.muted #9CA3AF 2.54 (disabled text and outline) · border.strong #D1D5DB 1.47 (not used as the edge) · border.focus #0284c7 4.10 · dark: text.primary #E5E7EB on primary.900 #0c4a6e 7.64 · primary.400 (dark link) #38BDF8 outline 8.33 on dark base and 6.83 on dark raised, check 4.42 on primary.900 · dark text.secondary #94A3B8 outline 6.96 · dark text.muted #64748B 3.75 on dark base (disabled).

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 5 rows × 5 columns, drawn in the web and Android chip form)
Columns (label → key): default → default · selected → selected · disabled → disabled · focus → focus · selected + focus → selected-focus (shows that selection and focus look different).
In R1–R4 the disabled cell disables every chip in the group and prints the row's reason caption under it. R5 differs.
 R1 channel → channel: "Email" · "Username" · "Share instead". default: none selected. selected: "Email". disabled: "You're offline. Invites need a connection." focus: on "Username". selected-focus: "Email".
 R2 role → role: "Member" · "Guest". A caption 12/16 text.secondary capability line under the group describes the selected role only. Member: "Sees and edits the calendar, sees bills and who paid, sees who lives here". Guest: "Same as Member until Sun 1 Nov · in 13 days" (no cell selects Guest).
   default: none selected, no capability line; cell note "caption appears after a role is chosen". selected: "Member" + Member line. disabled: both disabled, no capability line, reason "You're offline. Invites need a connection." focus: on "Guest", none selected, no capability line. selected-focus: "Member" + Member line.
 R3 time → time: "6:30 AM" · "7:00 AM" · "7:30 AM" · "8:00 AM". default: none selected. selected: "7:00 AM". disabled: "You're offline. Your briefing time will save when you're back online." focus: on "7:30 AM". selected-focus: "7:00 AM".
 R4 filter → filter: "Photographed", one toggle chip. default: off. selected: on. disabled: "You're offline. Filters need a connection." focus: off. selected-focus: on.
 R5 segment → segment: "Upcoming" · "Paid" · "All". default: "Upcoming" selected; cell note "a segment always has one selected". selected: "Upcoming". disabled: "Upcoming" stays enabled and selected (cached bills still show); "Paid" and "All" disabled; reason "You're offline. Paid and All need a connection." focus: "Upcoming" selected, focus on "Paid". selected-focus: "Upcoming".
Dark twin: all 25 cells with the dark tokens from ④, ⑤ and ⑦.

PER-PLATFORM FORMS (01-anatomy, side by side, light only)
R3 and R5, each in the default and selected states, on ios, android and web = 12 drawings. iOS R5 is the native segmented control (UISegmentedControl look, 32pt, selected segment raised); R3 on iOS is a Pantopus chip. Android uses Material 3 filter chips (leading check when selected, 32dp visual, 48dp target) with Pantopus tokens and the pill radius instead of the M3 8dp corner; Android R5 is a single-select row of those chips. Web: chips as specified.

SCALING AND GREYSCALE (03-scaling-greyscale)
Large-text frames draw R1, R2 (Member selected, capability line under the selected row), R3 and R5 as one-column rows. R4 stays a single chip that grows with its 44pt / 26sp label and becomes a rounded rectangle (radius lg 12) when it wraps (B9).
- AX5 (iOS 393): each option is a full-width row, at least 44pt tall, label 44pt, wrapping. Selected row: primary.50 fill, label primary.700, trailing 24pt check stroke in primary.700. Unselected rows: no fill, no indicator. No ring. R5's segmented control becomes these rows too.
- 200% (Android 412): rows at least 48dp, label 26sp, Material 3 radio on the leading edge (the platform control; flagged B8 exception). Selected row: primary.50 fill, label primary.700, a 24dp radio with a 2dp primary.700 ring and a 12dp filled primary.700 centre, no trailing check. Unselected rows: no fill, label text.strong, a 24dp empty radio with a 2dp text.secondary ring.
- Web 200% zoom, two frames. 390 wide (195 px effective, B9): below the 360 px switch point, so draw the AX5 row form (trailing check, no ring), built as role="radio" rows. 1440 wide (720 px effective), cropped to the group: the chips wrap onto several lines and stay chips. Print "switch to rows below 360 px effective width".
- GREYSCALE (B10): each cell reads "yes — selected = check + fill + outline; focus = ring"; disabled cells read "yes — reason caption". Add a WRONG example: a selected chip that differs only by hue, with "fix: add the check".
- INCREASE CONTRAST (B16): R3 with unselected outlines in text.strong, and the Android unselected radio rings in text.strong. Selected chips are unchanged; disabled chips stay text.muted (B16).

IN CONTEXT (04-in-context)
 a) f3-invite-composer, iOS 393, Home A: channel chips (Email selected), the field "priya@example.com", role chips (Member selected) with the Member capability line, then the primary button "Send invite".
 b) f4-briefing-optin-card, Android 412: "A morning heads-up?", the time chips (7:00 AM selected), then three equal-weight buttons "Yes", "Not now" and "No thanks". Label "Yes" with the note "opens the OS dialog; no second Yes".
 c) f3-bills-list, Home A: "Upcoming / Paid / All" as chips in a web 1440 crop (720 wide), and as the segmented control on iOS 393.

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Selection is shown by check, fill and outline, not colour alone. The focus ring is separate from selection.
- R1, R2, R3 and R5 are radio groups. iOS: buttons with the selected trait ("7:00 AM, selected, 2 of 4"). Android: selectable semantics ("7:00 AM, selected"). Web: role="radiogroup" with role="radio" and aria-checked; arrow keys move between chips.
- R4 is not a radio group; it is a toggle. Web: a button with aria-pressed. iOS: a button with the selected trait. Android: toggleable semantics. Spoken: "Photographed, off" / "Photographed, on".
- Disabled chips stay focusable and read their reason.
- Targets: a target (B13) around the 32 visual, with 8pt gaps.

COPY (print on 01-anatomy): Sentence case; exact strings as in the grid. Times are written "7:00 AM" (space, capital AM), never "6:00pm" or "7:40 am".

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy): iOS: R5 is the native segmented control; R1–R4 are Pantopus chips. Android: Material 3 filter chips with the pill radius; R5 is a single-select chip row. Web: :focus-visible ring, no hover-only affordance. Large text: trailing-check rows on iOS and web; Material 3 radios on Android.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of a ChoiceChip as a status badge, use StatusChip — because a choice chip looks tappable.
- Instead of a status chip on a person, write the role in plain text — because people are not statuses.
- Instead of a border token as any chip's only edge, use text.secondary (unselected) or text.muted (disabled) — because an input's edge must be visible.
- Instead of a selected chip bounded only by its 1.07:1 fill, add the 1px primary.700 outline — as AddressChip's selected edge does.
- Instead of the focus ring doubling as selection, keep the ring for focus and fill + check + outline for selection — because they are different states.
- Instead of truncating long labels at large text, switch to one-column rows — because truncated choices cannot be told apart.
- Instead of an empty-ring radio on iOS or web rows, use a trailing check on the selected row — because iOS has no radio control and an empty ring is the unconfirmed mark's shape.
- Instead of disabling a segment that still has cached content, disable only the segments that need a connection — because the reason must match what is disabled.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: channel · role · time · filter · segment. States: default · selected · disabled · focus · selected-focus. <size|platform> is "any" for all 50 grid cells (25 light + 25 dark). The 12 per-platform drawings are "ChoiceChip / {time,segment} / {default,selected} / {ios,android,web} / light". ChoiceChip total: 62 names. Examples: "ChoiceChip / time / selected / any / dark" · "ChoiceChip / segment / selected / ios / light".

NOTES ENTRIES (subheading "09 ChoiceChip")
 09.A1 Unselected outline text.secondary instead of spec border.strong (see ⑤).
 09.A2 Disabled text and outline text.muted, no border token; exempt from WCAG contrast; the reason caption carries the meaning (see ⑦).
 09.A3 Selected chip adds a 1px primary.700 outline (dark primary.400); the spec names only the fill (see ④).
 09.A4 R5 disabled keeps "Upcoming" enabled and selected; only "Paid" and "All" are disabled (see R5).
 09.A5 R2 shows the capability line only for the selected role (see R2).
 09.A6 R5 default shows "Upcoming" selected, because a segment always has one selection.
 09.A7 Android chips keep the pill radius instead of the M3 8dp corner.
 09.A8 Android 200% rows use Material 3 radios, including the empty ring (same flagged exception as 07.A1 (b)); iOS and web rows use a trailing check and no ring.
 09.A9 Web zoom has two frames: 390 (rows) and 1440 at 200% (wrapping chips).
 09.A10 The grid adds a selected-focus column, not in the contract's four states, to show that selection and focus look different.
 09.B1 Invented: "You're offline. Invites need a connection." · "You're offline. Your briefing time will save when you're back online." · "You're offline. Filters need a connection." · "You're offline. Paid and All need a connection." · "Send invite" · "caption appears after a role is chosen" · "a segment always has one selected" · "switch to rows below 360 px effective width" · "fix: add the check" · "opens the OS dialog; no second Yes".
 09.B2 Spoken labels: "7:00 AM, selected, 2 of 4" · "7:00 AM, selected" · "Photographed, off" · "Photographed, on".
 09.B3 Sourced, not invented: the Member capability line (f3-invite-composer research); "Same as Member until Sun 1 Nov · in 13 days" (adapted from f3-invite-composer research, date re-fixtured); "6:30 AM · 7:00 AM · 7:30 AM · 8:00 AM" and "Yes" / "Not now" (f4-briefing-optin-card); "No thanks" (brief section 7, the lasting decline); "A morning heads-up?" (glossary).
 09.C List any cell you could not draw, or "none".
 09.D Add to 07.D: the same Android radio question applies to ChoiceChip's 200% rows.
 09.E All 62 ChoiceChip names, then a closing count of every name in section E.

DONE WHEN
- All 5 artboards exist with their exact names. Notes has the 09 entries, every earlier entry is unchanged, and sections A–E are complete for all nine components.
- Both grids are 5 × 5 with printed keys, and every cell is drawn.
- Every selected chip has the fill, the leading check and the 1px outline. Focus is shown by the ring only.
- No chip uses a border token as its only edge.
- The R5 disabled cell disables only "Paid" and "All".
- Crop b shows "Yes", "Not now" and "No thanks" at equal weight.
- Only the Android 200% frame draws radio rings. The web 390 frame shows rows, and the 1440 frame shows wrapping chips.
- Section E lists 62 ChoiceChip names and gives the closing count.

name: Board setup
job: Board rules for every component on this board. Send first; draws nothing.
text:
Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is Foundations board 00b: Data instruments. This message sets up the board. Don't draw anything yet.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
This project draws seven components as reference specimens, not as screens: ScaleStrip, AqiBand, FourteenDayStrip, YearBand, SlotMeter, PublicPointMap and FactCount. Later screen prompts, sent from separate projects that can't see this one, ask for these components by exact name. Once published, these specimens are the only definition of each component. Draw every number, token and string exactly as the component messages give it.

HOW THIS PROJECT RUNS
- This message holds the board rules: G1–G8 and R1–R12. They apply to every artboard in this project. Later messages call them "the board rules from the setup message".
- After this message, I'll send one component message per turn, in this order: ScaleStrip, AqiBand, FourteenDayStrip, YearBand, SlotMeter, PublicPointMap, FactCount.
- ScaleStrip and AqiBand each arrive in two parts (part 1, then part 2). The two parts count as one component message. Part 2 relies on everything in part 1.
- Each component message (or part) includes its ARTBOARDS list and a BATCH PLAN. Draw only the first batch. Then stop and wait until I type "continue" or send the next part. Never start another component's artboards early.
- The last batch of every component updates 00b · Notes (R12).
- Everything you need is in the house style, this message, and the current and earlier component messages in this project. Don't open other projects.

PUBLISH (my step, after I accept a component)
When I accept a component, I add it to the Pantopus design system under its exact name. That includes its light and dark specimens and every variant and state. Your job is to make that step mechanical:
- Give every drawn grid cell and every named extra specimen a publish name (R10).
- List the names on 00b · Notes.
- Stand-ins (R11) and anything marked "do not publish" never get a publish name.

SHARED GRAMMAR (all seven instruments)
G1. Each instrument states its fact in words and numbers. The graphic repeats the fact and never replaces it.
G2. Nothing adds up to a grade, score, percentage or verdict. No progress ring, completion ring, countdown, streak or confetti appears anywhere. An authority's own band names are allowed even when they contain a percentage; each component message lists the allowed ones. "N of M" appears only where a component message allows it.
G3. Nothing depends on colour alone. The EPA AQI hues are the only sanctioned colour scale, and even there the category is printed in words.
G4. Three shapes mean provenance (00a · ProvenanceMark) and nothing else: a solid disc (Official), a ring (On record, not confirmed) and a solid disc with a knocked-out tick (You added this). No position marker, pointer, bullet, callout end, segment or badge on this board is a plain disc or ring. A component message that needs an exception describes it.
G5. A mark, cell or segment is never a tap target on its own. The target is the row, the whole instrument or a labelled button.
G6. Each instrument has a one-sentence summary and a spoken label, and both are printed on its artboards. The same facts also appear nearby as rows or a list.
G7. Every provenance mark keeps at least 3:1 contrast in every state. Staleness is always stated in words.
G8. Widgets and the share card are standalone surfaces. They print the provenance word next to each mark or in a legend line inside the block.

BOARD RULES
R1 · Artboard format and naming.
- Name every artboard "00b · <Component> · <NN-name> · <light|dark>", exactly as the component's ARTBOARDS list gives it. This overrides the house-style artboard pattern, because one specimen artboard shows several platforms. The last artboard is "00b · Notes".
- Each artboard is 1440 wide and as tall as its content. Light artboards use surface.app; dark artboards use dark surface.app.
- Above each artboard, print its exact name in label 13/18/600 text.strong.
- At the top inside each artboard, print three lines, as the component message gives them:
  - the component name, in h1 30/36/700 text.primary
  - its purpose line, in body 16/24 text.secondary
  - "Used in: <surface ids>", in caption 12/16 text.secondary
- Section headings use overline 11/16/600 caps, for example ANATOMY, VARIANT × STATE, AX5 AND 200%, GREYSCALE, IN CONTEXT, ACCESSIBILITY and INSTEAD OF.

R2 · Frames and cards.
- Draw specimens at true size (1pt = 1px on the artboard) inside plain frames, named as the message names them: iOS 393, Android 412, web-390, web-1440, and the widget outlines 338×158 and 338×354.
- In the three phone frames, draw the specimen card 358 wide with 16pt padding, which leaves 326pt of content width. Left-align the card at a 16pt frame margin. The right margin is then 19pt in iOS 393, 16pt in web-390 and 38pt in Android 412.
- All phone geometry assumes 326pt of content width unless a message says otherwise.
- Light cards use surface.base, radius lg 12, shadow sm and 16pt padding.
- Dark cards use dark surface.raised with a 1px dark border.strong decorative edge. The card edge carries no meaning, so the 3:1 minimum doesn't apply to it.
- Each component message gives its own web-1440 card width.

R3 · Units.
- A size given in pt is the same number in dp (Android) and px (web).
- Only target minimums differ by platform: 44pt on iOS, 48dp with 8dp gaps on Android, and 44px on web.
- Spacing uses the 4px scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64.
- A few micro offsets inside instruments are deliberately off that scale: 6, 3, 2 and 1pt. Use them only where a component message states them, and never for layout spacing.
- Type uses only these sizes:
  - the house type scale
  - medium (500) weights of body, bodySmall and caption at the same sizes: bodyMedium, bodySmallMedium and captionMedium
  - the R7 sizes
  - the 11pt widget minimum
  - OG sizes, where a component message states them

R4 · Callouts.
- Callouts sit in an annotation gutter outside the UI, in caption 12/16 text.strong. Gutter labels ("specimen", "specimen value", "stand-in — …") use the same style.
- Leader lines are 1px text.secondary and end in a short perpendicular tick, never a dot (G4).
- Dimension lines are 1px text.secondary with 4pt end ticks.
- Each callout names the part, its size and its token, for example "Track · 12pt · fill surface.raised · keyline 1px text.secondary".
- Callouts appear on 01-anatomy artboards and wherever a message asks for them.

R5 · Tokens and dark mode.
- Label every colour by its token name. Hex values appear on the board only in contrast tables a message asks for and in the AQI swatch row.
- The dark hex values in these rules and in the component messages are for drawing. In callouts, print the token name followed by "(dark)", for example "surface.raised (dark)".
- On dark artboards, use exactly this mapping:
  - surfaces: surface.base → #0F172A · surface.raised → #1E293B · surface.app → #020617 · surface.sunken → #0F172A · surface.muted → #111827
  - text: text.primary → #E5E7EB · text.secondary → #94A3B8 · text.strong → #F1F5F9
  - borders: border.default → #1F2937 and border.strong → #374151 (both are decoration only) · border.focus → #38BDF8
  - primary.700 → #38BDF8. This applies to links, text buttons and any edge a message names, because primary.700 is only 2.47:1 on dark raised.
- These tokens keep their light values in dark mode and are labelled by token name:
  - the primary.600 fill (3.57:1 on dark raised)
  - semantic.error glyphs (3.03:1)
  - semantic.warning glyphs (4.59:1)
- Semantic hues go on glyphs only.
- On dark cards, surface.sunken fills (#0F172A on #1E293B) look darker than the card. This is intended, because keylines and text carry the edges.
- A sunken-filled shape that sits directly on dark base uses dark surface.raised instead, so that it stays visible.
- Never use the light infoBg wash in dark mode, because dark text.primary on it is only 1.16:1. Component messages give the dark highlight.
- The EPA AQI hues never change in dark mode.
- This board draws no selection state.

R6 · Contrast numbers (WCAG 2). Opacities are alpha-blended over their surface first. Use these numbers and don't recompute them. Print only the rows a message asks for. A "tinted cell" is surface.sunken at 40% over base.
Light:
- text.secondary: 4.83 on base · 4.63 on raised · 4.51 on app · 4.39 on sunken. That is below 4.5, so text on sunken uses text.strong.
- text.strong: 9.37 on sunken · 10.31 on base
- text.primary: 17.74 on base · 16.12 on sunken
- primary.700: 5.93 on base · 5.68 on raised · 5.39 on sunken
- primary.600 fill: 4.10 on base
- glyphs: semantic.error 4.83 on base · semantic.warning 3.19 on base
- stale mark (the 00a stale variant, text.primary at 50%): 3.39 on base · 3.36 on raised · 3.34 on app · 3.32 on sunken
- on a tinted cell: text.secondary 4.65 · stale mark 3.36
- Never use text.secondary at 50% or text.muted for readable text. Both fail 4.5:1.
Dark:
- text.secondary: 6.96 on dark base · 5.71 on dark raised
- text.primary: 11.82 on dark raised · 14.42 on dark base
- text.strong: 16.30 on dark base · 13.35 on dark raised
- #38BDF8: 6.83 on dark raised · 8.33 on dark base
- stale mark (dark text.primary at 50%): 4.45 on dark base · 4.10 on dark raised · 4.48 on dark app
- on a dark tinted cell: text.secondary 6.23 · stale mark 4.27
- decoration only: dark border.strong 1.42 on dark raised · dark border.default 1.00 on dark raised

R7 · AX5 and 200%.
- iOS AX5 sizes: h1 58 · h2 56 · h3 55 · body and bodyMedium 53 · bodySmall and bodySmallMedium 49 · label 44 · caption and captionMedium 43 · overline 40.
- Android 200% sizes (Android 14 non-linear scaling): h1 38 · h2 36 · h3 34 · body 28 · bodySmall 26 · label 25 · caption 24 · overline 22. Medium weights use the same sizes as their base styles.
- Web: 200% browser zoom on web-1440, which gives an effective layout 720 CSS px wide.
- Graphic geometry keeps its size, and text reflows around it. This covers tracks, cells, segments, markers, glyph-only buttons, and marks inside cells, lanes and tracks.
- Marks inside text lines (captions, rows, legends) scale with their text.
- Text wraps and never truncates or ends in an ellipsis. Side-by-side pairs stack. Widgets fall back to text only, as each message states.
- Draw iOS AX5 in a 393 frame and Android 200% in a 412 frame, each as tall as needed.

R8 · Greyscale.
- Redraw the listed specimens at 100% desaturation.
- Under each one, print in caption text.secondary the non-colour cue that still carries the meaning, in the words the component message gives.

R9 · Grids and keys.
- A variant × state grid has variant rows and state columns, in the order the message gives.
- Print each row and column label in label 13/18/600 text.strong. Under each label, print its key as "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- A key is lowercase and hyphenated. It never contains spaces, "/", a fixture string or a date. Each component message lists its keys; use them exactly.
- Each cell holds one specimen at true size, or the stacked specimens the message asks for. Under the specimen, print the cell's keys, for example "detail · stale".
- A combination that has no meaning prints "n/a — <reason>" in caption text.secondary and nothing else. Use the one reason the message gives. Never leave a cell blank.
- Every specimen outside a grid gets the extra key the message gives. So does a specimen stacked inside a cell that the message gives its own extra key.

R10 · Publish names. Give one name to each drawn grid cell and each extra specimen, in one of two forms:
- "<Component> / <variant key> / <state key> / <light|dark>"
- "<Component> / extra / <extra key> / <light|dark>"
Names use keys only. n/a cells get no name.

R11 · Borrowed parts and stand-ins.
- These instruments use parts from boards 00a, 00c and 00d. Use the published part when the design system has it.
- Otherwise, draw the stand-in described below and label it in the gutter "stand-in — the 00a/00c/00d specimen replaces it".
- Don't develop a stand-in beyond this description, and never give it a publish name.
The stand-ins:
- 00a · ProvenanceMark: a mark at XS 12pt or S 16pt, in text.secondary at full opacity.
  - Official: a solid disc.
  - On record, not confirmed: a ring with a stroke of at least 1.5px.
  - You added this: a solid disc with a knocked-out tick (a true cut-out).
  - Stale variant: the same shape in text.primary at 50%, always paired with age words.
- 00a · SourceCaption: one caption 12/16 line in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken), in the pattern [ProvenanceMark S] authority · scope word · as-of. It wraps and never truncates.
- 00a · FreshnessLine: one caption line in text.secondary that states the age in words, with an optional 16pt leading glyph.
- 00a · ScopeChip: a 24pt pill on surface.sunken, holding a 12pt person or house glyph and the label in label 13/18 text.strong.
- 00a · KindGlyph: a 24pt line icon with a 2pt stroke, in text.strong.
- 00c · InlineErrorRow: a row in the component's own slot, with no tinted background. It holds:
  - a 16pt error glyph (semantic.error on the glyph only)
  - the sentence, in body text.primary
  - a 44pt "Retry" text button in primary.700
- 00c · DateRow: a row at least 56pt tall. It holds:
  - a leading KindGlyph
  - the title, in body text.primary
  - a trailing ProvenanceMark S
  - line 2, in caption text.secondary, with the relative and absolute date ("Tomorrow", or "in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct") and a short SourceCaption
- 00c · FactRow: a 56pt row. It holds the label in bodySmall text.secondary above the value in body text.primary, a ProvenanceMark and a trailing chevron.
- 00c · TextActionRow (outbound): a row at least 44pt tall with a 1px text.secondary edge, a verb-led label in primary.700 and a trailing "↗".
- 00d · WarmingSkeleton: surface.sunken shapes with the component's final geometry and radius, and no text.
  - It reserves the exact final height.
  - It shimmers by default and is static under Reduce Motion.
- 00d · QuietDayReceipt: draw only the form a component message describes, exactly as described.

R12 · Fixtures, motion, focus and 00b · Notes.
- Use the house-style FIXTURES exactly. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific.
- Draw every quoted string exactly as written.
- Label any value that isn't tied to a fixture address "specimen value" in the gutter.
- Show motion as static annotated frames, never as a loop. Annotate Reduce Motion wherever it changes something.
- Keyboard focus on web is a 2px border.focus outline with a 2px offset around the focusable row, strip or button (#38BDF8 in dark).
- 00b · Notes is one light artboard, 1440 wide.
  - It has sections A to G. Divide each section by component, with the component name as an h3 subheading.
  - Create it in the last batch of the first component.
  - Each later component appends its entries in its own last batch and keeps everything already there.
- The sections:
  - A. Invented strings: every quoted string that is not in the house-style fixtures or the component contract.
  - B. Assumptions.
  - C. Normalisations.
  - D. Deviations from the contract. I sign off on each one.
  - E. Open questions for the founder, numbered across the whole board.
  - F. n/a cells, each with its reason.
  - G. Publish names (R10).
- Start section B with a "Board" subsection that records:
  - the artboard naming override (R1)
  - the off-scale micro offsets, and the medium type weights (R3)
  - the 358-wide phone cards, left-aligned at a 16pt frame margin, with right margins of 19pt (iOS 393), 16pt (web-390) and 38pt (Android 412) (R2)
  - the decorative dark card edge in border.strong, and the dark sunken fills (R2, R5)
  - the dark values for surface.sunken, surface.muted, text.strong and border.strong, which the house style does not define and this board assumes (R5)
  - stale marks, drawn as the 00a stale variant (text.primary at 50%), which passes 3:1 (R6, R11). This is the only place the board records the stale treatment; components don't repeat it.

Reply 'ready' and wait for the first component.

name: ScaleStrip
job: The four-layer reading instrument: one authority's own ordered bands per row. It must never add up to a grade.
text:
Component 00b-01: ScaleStrip, part 1 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message.
Part 1 holds the full specification and the first four artboards. Part 2, my next message, adds artboards 05–08, the dark twins and the Notes, and relies on everything in this part.

ARTBOARDS AND BATCH PLAN FOR PART 1
Draw these four, using the exact names and this order. Then stop and wait for part 2.
1. 00b · ScaleStrip · 01-anatomy · light
2. 00b · ScaleStrip · 02-layers-by-state · light
3. 00b · ScaleStrip · 03-compare · light
4. 00b · ScaleStrip · 04-instrument-states · light

PURPOSE (print it): The four-layer reading instrument. It draws one row per authority on that authority's own ordered bands, and it never adds up to a grade.
USED IN (print it): f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f8-compare-arrival-header, f8-compare-reveal, f8-compare-sheet, f8-og-compare-card.
WEB-1440 CARD: 640px wide, with 608px of content.
SPECIMEN CLOCKS
- Ready Air rows, including the compare "You" row, are drawn at 7:10 AM on Mon 19 Oct, so "observed 7:00 AM" counts as fresh. Print "specimen time 7:10 AM" in the gutter.
- Stale Air rows use TODAY, 6:10 PM.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy; put a callout on every part)
- Row order is fixed as Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon, and rows are never re-sorted, because people compare rows by position.
- A row contains, from top to bottom:
  - the layer name, in label 13/18/600 text.strong
  - the value line "Word · number", in bodyMedium 16/24/500 text.primary
  - the track zone
  - the band names
  - 00a · SourceCaption
- Row padding is 12pt top and bottom. Gaps: name → value 4pt · value → track zone 8pt · track zone → band names 4pt · band names → caption 8pt.
- Each row is at least 48pt tall and is a single target. Markers and pointers are never targets.
- Layout:
  - Below 560pt (phones and web-390), the row is stacked, with a 326pt track.
  - At 560pt and wider (web-1440), the row has two columns: left 237px, gap 16px, right 355px. The left column stacks the name, the value line and the SourceCaption. The right column holds the track zone and the band names, top-aligned with the value line.
  - AX5 and 200% are stacked.
  - Part 2 defines the OG column.
- Track zone: 24pt tall, with a 12pt track centred in it.
- Track:
  - equal-width bands per layer (the layers don't share an axis)
  - filled surface.raised
  - 1.5px text.secondary separators (4.63:1 on raised)
  - a 1px text.secondary keyline with radius xs 4 around the whole track
  - the least hazard on the left
- Occupied band: a 2px text.primary outline inside its edges.
- Marker: a vertical capsule, 4 × 20pt, radius pill.
  - Core: text.primary. Halo: 2px surface.base, which makes it 8 × 24pt overall. The halo is #0F172A in dark.
  - It is centred in the occupied band and extends 4pt beyond the track top and bottom.
  - It is never a disc (G4).
- Band names, in caption 12/16 text.secondary:
  - Up to 2 lines each, never truncated.
  - Flood and Radon print all their names. Wildfire prints the two end names plus the occupied one.
  - The occupied name is set in captionMedium 12/16/500 text.primary, directly under the marker. If it comes within 8pt of an end name, it replaces that end name.
  - Air prints "0–50" · "51–100" · "101–150" · "151–200" · "201–300" · "301+", with the occupied range in captionMedium text.primary.
- Bands:
  - Flood, by annual chance: "Minimal (X)" · "0.2% a year (shaded X)" · "1% a year or more (A/V zones)". The value line prints the actual zone code. These FEMA annual-chance names and "1% chance each year" are the band names G2 allows.
  - Wildfire (USFS): "Very low" · "Low" · "Moderate" · "High" · "Very high".
  - Radon: "Zone 3 · low potential" · "Zone 2 · moderate potential" · "Zone 1 · highest potential". Never "N of M".
  - Air: the AqiBand instrument-row variant. It is the only coloured track. The next component defines AqiBand; draw this row exactly as follows:
    - six equal-width 12pt segments in the house-style EPA ColorVision Assist hues
    - 2px gaps in the host surface
    - a 1px text.secondary keyline on each segment, with radius xs 4 on the outer corners
    - on the occupied segment, a 2px text.primary inner outline
    - the same 4 × 20pt capsule, placed by value within its segment
    - no reading: segments in surface.sunken with their keylines, and no marker
    - the value line leaves out the pollutant
- Fixture rows (HOME A). All are Official; "●" stands for the drawn Official mark.

  | Row | Label | Value | Occupied | Caption |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Flood | "Flood zone" | "Zone X — minimal flood hazard" | band 1 | "● FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021" |
  | Wildfire | "Wildfire hazard potential" | "Moderate · 3 of 5" | band 3 | "● USFS · quarter-mile area · 2023" |
  | Air | "Air quality index (AQI)" | "AQI 42 · Good" | 84% of Good | "● AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM" |
  | Radon | "Radon zone" | "Zone 1 — highest potential (county)" | band 3 | "● EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home" |

- Summary. Print this one sentence under the 01 fixture instrument: "Flood Zone X, minimal flood hazard; Wildfire Moderate, 3 of 5; Air AQI 42, Good; Radon Zone 1, county-wide."
- Specimen value: a Flood row with "Zone AE — 1% chance each year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years)" and band 3 occupied.

VARIANTS [row keys]
- V1 Flood [flood] · V2 Wildfire [wildfire] · V3 Radon [radon] · V4 Air [air].
- V5 compare [compare]: two identical labelled pointers replace the capsule. Filled vs hollow means provenance only.
  - Track zone, 60pt tall, from top to bottom:
    - a 16pt line "Dana", in captionMedium text.primary
    - the 8pt sender pointer
    - the 12pt track
    - the 8pt "You" pointer
    - a 16pt line "You"
    Band names sit 4pt below the track zone.
  - Pointers: triangles 12 wide × 8 tall, in text.primary with a 2px surface.base halo.
    - The sender pointer points down, with its tip on the track top. The "You" pointer points up, with its tip on the track bottom.
    - Each pointer is centred in its band. On Air, it is placed by value.
  - Each occupied band is outlined; a band both places share gets one outline. The two pointers share an x position on the non-Air layers, and on Air only when the values are equal.
  - Value lines: "Dana: <value>" and "You: <value>". When the band is shared, print one line, "Both: <value>".
  - Chip: "Same band" or "Different band", right-aligned on the layer-name line.
    - A 24pt pill in surface.sunken, 8pt side padding, captionMedium text.strong, no glyph and no hue.
    - On compare rows, the layer-name line is 24pt tall, and the name is vertically centred on the chip. The other row gaps are unchanged.
  - Header: "Dana · Camas, WA — what's on record for this area".
- V6 no data [no-data] (Flood, Wildfire, Radon): bands in surface.sunken, keyline and separators unchanged, no marker and no outline, value "Not on record".
- V7 not studied (Flood): the same greyed track, with the value "FEMA hasn't mapped flood hazard here".
- V8 non-burnable (Wildfire): the same greyed track, with the value "Non-burnable land cover (USFS)".
- V6–V8 must each look different from Wildfire "Very low", because missing data is not a low reading.
- V9 frozen [frozen]:
  - Captions end "as of Sat 12 Sep 2026".
  - The Air caption reads "AirNow · on Sat 12 Sep 2026", and the Air value reads "AQI 42 · Good · on Sat 12 Sep".
- V10 collapsed [collapsed], for arrival headers below 640px:
  - one wrapping body row, at least 44pt tall
  - the whole row is the target, and there are no tracks
  - text: "Dana · Camas, WA · Flood X · Wildfire Moderate · Air 42 · Radon Zone 1 ›"

STATES [column keys]
- loading [loading]: 00d · WarmingSkeleton.
  - Only the track keyline and separators show.
  - The label and value become surface.sunken bars of 60×12 and 140×16.
  - The exact row height is reserved.
- ready [ready].
- partial, loading [partial-loading]: some rows are ready and others are loading.
- partial, failed [partial-failed]: the Air row's slot shows 00c · InlineErrorRow "We couldn't reach AirNow just now" with Retry. The other rows are ready.
- differs [differs]: the "Different band" chip (V5).
- stale [stale], at 6:10 PM:
  - The Air row keeps its value and marker.
  - Its caption reads "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM — 11 hours ago", with the 00a stale mark. The age words carry the staleness.
  - The other rows are unchanged.
- AX5 [ax5]: text stacked above a full-width track. Part 2 draws this, on 06.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE CONTRACT (part 2 records these on Notes D for my sign-off)
- The 4 × 20pt two-tone capsule replaces the contract's "Marker: 12pt two-tone".
- The 12 × 8 triangle pointers in V5 replace the contract's "same marker form" for compare.

ARTBOARD CONTENTS (part 1; part 2 adds the dark twins)
01-anatomy:
- a Wildfire detail row, with every callout
- the fixture instrument in iOS 393, with the summary under it
- the same instrument on web-1440 in two columns, with a callout on the 237 / 16 / 355 split [extra key two-column]
- an R6 table: text.secondary on base and on raised, text.strong on sunken, and the stale mark on base and on raised
02-layers-by-state: a grid of 5 rows × 6 columns.
- Rows: flood · wildfire · air · radon · wildfire-very-low (labelled "Wildfire very low (for contrast)").
- Columns: loading · ready · no-data · not-studied-non-burnable · stale · frozen.
- flood × ready: add the Zone AE specimen under Zone X.
- flood × not-studied-non-burnable is V7; wildfire × not-studied-non-burnable is V8.
- air × no-data: use the AqiBand no-reading row ("No reading for this address right now"), not V6.
- These cells are n/a, with these reasons:
  - air × not-studied-non-burnable: "n/a — AirNow has no such class; see AqiBand no reading"
  - radon × not-studied-non-burnable: "n/a — EPA zones cover every county"
  - flood × stale, wildfire × stale and radon × stale: "n/a — dated datasets carry their effective date, not an age"
- wildfire-very-low × ready: a normal track with band 1 occupied and the value "Very low · 1 of 5", aligned with the greyed wildfire cells. The row's other cells read "n/a — contrast row; only ready is needed".
03-compare: a web-390 instrument comparing "Dana · Camas, WA" with You (keys "compare · differs").
- Flood: both in band 1; "Same band"; "Both: Zone X — minimal flood hazard".
- Wildfire: "Different band"; "Dana: Moderate · 3 of 5"; "You: Low · 2 of 5".
- Air: both AQI 42, inside Good; "Same band"; "Both: AQI 42 · Good". Two caption lines: "Dana: AirNow · on Sat 12 Sep 2026" and "You: AirNow · observed 7:00 AM".
- Radon: both Zone 1; "Same band"; "Both: Zone 1 — highest potential (county)".
- Flood, Wildfire and Radon each print one frozen caption, for example "● FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021 · as of Sat 12 Sep 2026".
- Only You's wildfire reading ("Low · 2 of 5") is a specimen value; label it so in the gutter.
- Under the instrument, print the one-sentence compare summary "Dana's area and yours share 3 of 4 bands; wildfire differs.", followed by the compare spoken label.
- Beside the instrument, draw V10 twice. Neither copy may truncate:
  - at 390 wide (keys "collapsed · ready")
  - at 320 wide, wrapping [extra key collapsed-320]
- Below the instrument: the compare Wildfire row in two columns on web-1440 [extra key compare-two-column].
04-instrument-states: the instrument five times in iOS 393, keyed "instrument · <state key>", in this order: loading · ready · partial-loading (with Air loading) · partial-failed · stale. Print all four spoken labels under ready, and under each other state print only the labels that change.

ACCESSIBILITY (each row is one element; web rows are focusable)
- Under ready on 04:
  - "Flood zone: Zone X, minimal flood hazard, scale Minimal to 1% a year or more. FEMA, effective September 2021. Official."
  - "Wildfire hazard potential: Moderate, 3 of 5, scale Very low to Very high. USFS 2023. Official."
  - "Air quality index 42, Good, category 1 of 6. AirNow, observed 7 AM. Official."
  - "Radon zone: Zone 1, highest potential, scale Zone 3 to Zone 1. EPA, county-wide. Official."
- Changed labels on 04:
  - loading: "Loading", once for the whole container
  - partial-loading: "Loading", on the Air row
  - partial-failed: "Air quality: We couldn't reach AirNow just now.", with the Retry button named "Retry air quality"
  - stale: "Air quality index 42, Good, category 1 of 6. AirNow, observed 7 AM, 11 hours ago. Official."
- On 03: "Wildfire hazard potential. Dana: Moderate, 3 of 5. You: Low, 2 of 5. Different band. Scale Very low to Very high. USFS 2023."

COPY
- Use these verbatim: "Zone X — minimal flood hazard" · "Zone AE — 1% chance each year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years)" · "Wildfire hazard potential: Moderate · 3 of 5" · "Radon Zone 1 — highest potential (county)".
- Pair a word with a number on every layer except Radon.
- Sender rows describe places. Outbound actions start with a verb.
- "N of M" appears only in Wildfire readings, in "category 1 of 6", and in the compare summary's "3 of 4 bands".
- Never write: "100-year floodplain", "minimal risk", "wildfire risk", "better", "worse", "wins".

PLATFORMS: web draws it as SVG; iOS (SwiftUI) and Android (Compose) draw it natively. The geometry is identical on all three; only the target minimums differ by platform.

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of a grade, star, radar chart, cross-layer ramp or shared 0–100 axis, draw each authority's own bands, because the layers never add up to a verdict.
- Instead of arrows, trophies or better/worse words, print "Different band" or "Same band", because a difference between places is not a ranking.

CARRY TO NOTES (part 2 writes these, together with its own entries)
- A: the compare summary "Dana's area and yours share 3 of 4 bands; wildfire differs."
- D: the two deviations listed above.
- G: the part 1 extras: two-column, collapsed-320 and compare-two-column.

DONE WHEN (part 1)
- The four artboards above exist with their exact names.
- The 02 grid is 5 × 6, with no blank cell.
- Both V10 widths are drawn.
- The summary on 01 and the compare summary on 03 are each one sentence.

The brief's "Zone 1 — highest potential of EPA's 3 zones" → the contract's "Radon Zone 1 — highest potential (county)".

name: AqiBand

text:
Component 00b-02: AqiBand, part 1 of 2. Follow the board rules from the setup message.
Part 1 holds the full specification and the first two artboards. Part 2, my next message, adds artboards 03–06, the dark twins, the publish names and the Notes, and relies on everything in this part.

ARTBOARDS AND BATCH PLAN FOR PART 1
Draw these two, using the exact names and this order. Then stop and wait for part 2.
1. 00b · AqiBand · 01-anatomy · light
2. 00b · AqiBand · 02-variants-by-state · light

PURPOSE (print it): The one officially coloured scale. It shows the EPA AQI with its category name and is drawn the same way everywhere air appears.
USED IN (print it): f1-today-air-band, f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, x-provenance-sheet, f8-og-compare-card, f8-compare-reveal.
WEB-1440 CARD: 640px wide, with 608px of content.

SPECIMEN CLOCKS
AirNow readings are hourly, so the age of a reading decides its state. On every artboard that shows one of these specimens, print its specimen time once in the gutter.
- Ready and offline specimens: 7:10 AM on Mon 19 Oct, so "observed 7:00 AM" counts as fresh.
- Alert and still-above specimens: 4:10 PM.
- Stale specimens: TODAY, 6:10 PM, which gives "— 11 hours ago".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy; put a callout on every part)
- Segments: six equal-width category segments in the EPA ColorVision Assist hues. These are the only non-token colours in the product.
- Swatch row: show the hues as a row, with each name and RGB value:
  - aqi.good: Good 158,255,145
  - aqi.moderate: Moderate 255,201,5
  - aqi.usg: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 255,130,5
  - aqi.unhealthy: Unhealthy 240,34,0
  - aqi.veryUnhealthy: Very Unhealthy 137,9,151
  - aqi.hazardous: Hazardous 100,0,21
- Segment height: 16pt in the detail variant (Today), 12pt in the instrument row, and 8pt in the widget micro variant.
- Gaps: 2px between segments, in the host surface. That is surface.base on light cards and surface.raised (dark) on dark cards.
- Keylines: each segment gets its own 1px text.secondary keyline, because some hues nearly vanish against their surface (Good is 1.22:1 and Moderate 1.54:1 on white; Hazardous is 1.08:1 on dark raised). The outer corners of the first and last segments have radius xs 4.
- Detail segment width: (326 − 5 × 2) ÷ 6 = 52.7pt. On web-1440: (608 − 10) ÷ 6 = 99.7px.
- Range labels: centred under each segment, in caption 12/16 text.secondary: "0–50" · "51–100" · "101–150" · "151–200" · "201–300" · "301+".
  - The occupied label switches to captionMedium text.primary.
  - The occupied segment gets a 2px text.primary inner outline.
- Marker: the ScaleStrip capsule, 4pt wide.
  - Core: text.primary. Halo: 2px surface.base. In dark mode the halo stays the fixed dark tone #0F172A.
  - Height is the segment height + 8pt: 24pt in detail, 20pt in the instrument row, 16pt in widget micro.
  - It is never a disc (G4).
  - It passes 3:1 on every hue in both themes, because one of its two tones always contrasts.
- Marker position:
  - Position within the segment = (value − segment low) ÷ (segment high − segment low).
  - For position only, the "301+" segment spans 301–500.
  - AQI 42 sits at 84% of Good. AQI 118 sits at 35% of Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.
  - Values above 500 clamp to the right end of "301+", and the actual number is still printed.
- Marker contrast table. Print it on 01: core and halo contrast against each hue.

  | Hue | Light core | Light halo | Dark core | Dark halo |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Good | 14.50 | 1.22 | 1.01 | 14.59 |
  | Moderate | 11.50 | 1.54 | 1.25 | 11.57 |
  | USG | 7.14 | 2.49 | 2.01 | 7.18 |
  | Unhealthy | 4.17 | 4.26 | 3.44 | 4.19 |
  | Very Unhealthy | 2.15 | 8.24 | 6.65 | 2.17 |
  | Hazardous | 1.31 | 13.52 | 10.92 | 1.32 |

- Value line: above the band, in bodyMedium text.primary.
  - Fixture: "AQI 42 · Good · PM2.5". Alert: "AQI 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups · PM2.5".
  - The category and number always sit on the card in text.primary, never on a fill (text.primary on Hazardous is only 1.31:1).
  - The value line is the visible summary.
  - Inside ScaleStrip, the pollutant is left out.
- Health statement: below the band, in body 16/24 text.primary, verbatim from EPA.
  - Good: "Air quality is satisfactory, and air pollution poses little or no risk."
  - Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups: "Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects. The general public is less likely to be affected." Then add the PM2.5 line: "People with heart or lung disease, older adults, children, and people of lower socioeconomic status are the groups most at risk."
- PANTOPUS NOTE: Pantopus context, labelled as ours. It appears on the alert and still-above specimens only.
  - It is a separate block below the EPA statement. The EPA statement stays above it, unchanged.
  - The block holds the overline "PANTOPUS NOTE", then, in bodySmall text.primary, "Your alert level is 101. You can change it in Notifications."
  - On still-above, the block holds a second line directly below that one, also in bodySmall text.primary: "Still above your alert level (101) since 4:00 PM. No new alert until it drops below 101 and rises again."
- Threshold rule: drawn at the user's chosen threshold (101, 151 or 201), never hard-coded.
  - A 1.5px dashed vertical rule (3 on, 2 off) in text.primary, extending 6pt beyond the band top and bottom.
  - When the threshold equals a segment's low value, centre the rule in the 2px gap before that segment. 101 sits in the Moderate/USG gap; 151 sits in the USG/Unhealthy gap.
  - The threshold number sits above the rule, in caption text.primary ("101").
  - "Crossed 101 at 4:00 PM" appears in bodySmallMedium text.primary, with a leading 16pt alert glyph in semantic.warning (on the glyph only).
  - The fixture threshold is 101, the server default. Also draw one specimen at 151, labelled "threshold 151 (not crossed)".
  - In the instrument row, the threshold number sits to the right of the rule's top end, and the track zone grows from 24pt to 40pt, in the alert cell only.
- 00a · SourceCaption: "● AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM". On alert, it reads "observed 4:00 PM". "●" stands for the drawn Official mark.

VARIANTS [row keys]
- V1 detail [detail]: the Today card.
- V2 instrument row [instrument-row]: the Air row inside ScaleStrip, with 12pt segments and no health statement.
  - In ready, stale and no-reading, it must match the ScaleStrip artboards exactly.
  - The alert cell (40pt track zone and threshold rule) is an AqiBand-only form that the ScaleStrip artboards don't draw.
- V3 widget micro [widget-micro]: the block inside the medium widget.
  - Band: 120 × 8pt, with no range labels and no statement.
  - Beside the band, in label 13/18 text.primary: "Air · Good 42". On alert: "Air · Sensitive groups 118".
  - Under it, a caption line of 11pt or larger: an XS Official mark, then "Official · AirNow · 7:00 AM" (G8).
- V4 no reading, V5 alert and V6 still above threshold (no new push) are drawn in their state columns:
  - V5 = the threshold rule, "Crossed 101 at 4:00 PM", the 00a · ScopeChip "Your household", and the PANTOPUS NOTE.
  - V6 = the V5 detail card, unchanged, with the still-above line added as the second line of the PANTOPUS NOTE.

STATES [column keys]
- ready [ready], at 7:10 AM.
- stale [stale], at 6:10 PM:
  - Hues and marker are unchanged.
  - The caption reads "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM — 11 hours ago", with the 00a stale mark. The age words carry the staleness.
- no reading [no-reading] (V4):
  - Segments are surface.sunken with their keylines, with no marker and no outline. Range labels stay.
  - The value line becomes "No reading for this address right now", in body text.primary.
  - A second specimen, for a failed provider, adds 00c · InlineErrorRow "We couldn't reach AirNow just now" with Retry [extra key no-reading-provider-failed].
- alert [alert] (V5), at 4:10 PM.
- still above [still-above] (V6), at 4:10 PM.
- offline [offline], at 7:10 AM: the 00a · FreshnessLine "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" sits above the band, which is drawn from cache.

ARTBOARD CONTENTS (part 1)
01-anatomy:
- the V1 detail card at AQI 42 on iOS 393, with every callout
- the swatch row
- the marker contrast table
02-variants-by-state: a grid of 3 rows × 6 columns.
- Rows: detail · instrument-row · widget-micro.
- Columns: ready · stale · no-reading · alert · still-above · offline.
- detail row:
  - ready: V1 at AQI 42
  - stale: V1 with the stale caption
  - no-reading: V4, with the no-reading-provider-failed specimen stacked under it
  - alert: V5 at AQI 118
  - still-above: V6
  - offline: V1 under the FreshnessLine
- instrument-row row:
  - ready: V2 at AQI 42, "AQI 42 · Good", with range labels
  - stale: V2 with the stale caption
  - no-reading: V2 greyed, with "No reading for this address right now"
  - alert: V2 at AQI 118 with the threshold rule, and no statement or note
  - still-above: "n/a — the still-above line belongs to the detail card; the row keeps its alert form"
  - offline: "n/a — the host instrument shows one FreshnessLine for all four rows"
- widget-micro row:
  - ready: the V3 block, "Air · Good 42"
  - stale: "n/a — widget age is the widget's own 'As of' line (f7-today-widget)"
  - no-reading: V3 greyed, "Air · No reading"
  - alert: V3 at AQI 118, "Air · Sensitive groups 118", with no threshold rule
  - still-above: "n/a — widgets show only the current reading"
  - offline: "n/a — the widget keeps its last snapshot (f7-today-widget)"
- Under the grid, draw three extras:
  - threshold 151 (not crossed), at AQI 118 [extra key threshold-151]
  - a clamp specimen at AQI 612, labelled "specimen value", with the marker at the right end and the value "AQI 612 · Hazardous · PM2.5" [extra key clamp]
  - six capsules, one per segment, showing 3:1 in both themes [extra key marker-on-every-hue]

ACCESSIBILITY
- The summary is the value line. The band is one element. Spell out "Air quality index (AQI)" once per surface.
- "category N of 6" is allowed in spoken labels only.
- Print these labels under their 02 cells:
  - detail ready: "Air quality index 42, Good, category 1 of 6. AirNow, observed 7 AM."
  - detail stale: "Air quality index 42, Good, category 1 of 6. AirNow, observed 7 AM, 11 hours ago."
  - detail no-reading: "Air quality: No reading for this address right now."
  - detail alert: "Air quality index 118, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, category 3 of 6. AirNow, observed 4 PM."
  - detail still-above: "Air quality index 118, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, category 3 of 6. Still above your alert level, 101, since 4 PM. AirNow, observed 4 PM."
  - detail offline: "You're offline. Air quality index 42, Good, category 1 of 6. AirNow, observed 7 AM."
  - instrument-row ready, stale and alert: the matching detail label followed by " Official." (the ScaleStrip Air-row form)
  - instrument-row no-reading: "Air quality: No reading for this address right now." (no "Official.", because no reading is shown)
  - widget-micro ready: "Air quality 42, Good. Official, AirNow, 7 AM."
  - widget-micro no-reading: "Air quality: no reading. Official, AirNow."
  - widget-micro alert: "Air quality 118, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups. Official, AirNow, 4 PM."
- Separators and keylines keep the band readable in greyscale. In tinted widgets, the printed name carries the meaning.
- The band is not a target. Retry and row actions are 44pt / 48dp / 44px.

COPY
- EPA names and health text are verbatim: "Good", "Moderate", "Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups", "Unhealthy", "Very Unhealthy", "Hazardous".
- "Sensitive groups" appears only in widgets.

PLATFORMS: the geometry is identical on iOS, Android and web. The widget differences are defined on 03, in part 2.

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of a proportional 0–500 track, draw six equal segments ending in "301+", because proportional widths squeeze 0–100 and can't place readings above 500.
- Instead of brand blue or an invented ramp, use the EPA hues, because this is the authority's own scale.
- Instead of "Air quality is satisfactory for everyone", print EPA's exact sentence, because a paraphrase is an EPA reporting error.
- Instead of hiding the band on a good day, draw it at AQI 42 with "Good", because a quiet reading is still a reading.

text:
Component 00b-03: FourteenDayStrip. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): The next two weeks at this address, drawn as a shape. The strip sits above list rows, and those rows are the real tap targets.
USED IN (print it): f5-today-calendar-strip, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, f1-today-tab, x-place-file.
WEB-1440 CARD: 648px wide (616px of content), so each cell is 44px.
TYPE (two styles this component adds to the house scale; use them only as named):
- captionMedium 12/16/500. iOS AX5 → 43, Android 200% → 24.
- widgetCaption 11/16/400, widgets only. At AX sizes the widget drops to its text fallback (05), so widgetCaption has no AX5 or 200% size.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- Header: the 00a · ScopeChip "Your household" (HOME A), then the summary label "Next 14 days: 6 items" in label 13/18 text.strong. The summary is the strip's one-sentence summary.
- Strip: 14 equal cells across the content width, today on the left. At 326pt the pitch is 23.3pt.
  - One track: radius sm 6, a 1px text.secondary keyline, and 1px text.secondary separators between cells.
  - Cell height 76pt, top to bottom: 6pt padding · up to 3 XS (12pt) ProvenanceMarks stacked with 4pt gaps (44pt) · a 4pt gap · a 16pt line reserved for "+N" · 6pt padding.
  - "+N" appears when a cell has 4 or more mark items (3 marks, then "+N"). It is in caption 12/16 text.strong (#F1F5F9 dark), because text.secondary on sunken is only 4.39:1. Otherwise the reserved line stays empty.
  - All marks use one ink, text.secondary at full opacity, centred in the cell. Marks never dim, in any state (C11).
- Cell fill: weekdays surface.sunken at 100%, weekends surface.sunken at 40%. Opacity marks the weekend, never hue, and the initials also name it (or "Sat–Sun" where there are no initials).
- Civic, state or county rule: a solid 4pt bar, full cell height, in text.strong. The bar is centred if the cell has no other marks. Otherwise it sits 2pt from the cell's left edge and the marks shift 3pt right. A bar never counts toward the 3-mark limit or "+N". A rule is never a dot. YearBand uses the same bar rule.
- Holiday move: the mark sits on the moved day. The usual day gets a struck ghost: the same shape at full text.secondary ink, crossed by a 1.5px diagonal strike in text.primary (#E5E7EB dark). The strike carries the meaning, and the DateRow names the move in words.
- Labels under the strip:
  - Row 1: weekday initials under every cell, in caption text.secondary: "M T W T F S S M T W T F S S". Draw them only where the pitch is 20pt or more. They are never spoken.
  - Row 2: anchors in captionMedium text.strong: "Today" left-aligned under cell 1 and "Mon 26 Oct" left-aligned under cell 8.
- Below the strip: one 00c · DateRow per item. The foot is a persistent 48pt row "+ Add a date", with the glyph and label in primary.700 (#38BDF8 dark).
- Fixture window, HOME A, Mon 19 Oct–Sun 1 Nov:

  | Cell | Day | Item (DateRow title) | Mark |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | Tue 20 Oct | Recycling and garbage | hollow (city schedule, not confirmed) |
  | 5 | Fri 23 Oct | Clark Public Utilities bill | tick |
  | 8 | Mon 26 Oct | Voter registration, online or mail, must arrive by | state bar |
  | 9 | Tue 27 Oct | Garbage only | hollow |
  | 10 | Wed 28 Oct | City of Vancouver water bill | tick |
  | 14 | Sun 1 Nov | HOA dues | tick, weekend cell |

  DateRow line 2 dates (R11): "Tomorrow"; "in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct"; "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct"; "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct"; "in 9 days · Wed 28 Oct"; "in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov".
- Two extras for 01. Each is a separate specimen outside the window, labelled "specimen" in the gutter:
  - Overflow cell [extra key overflow-cell], Mon 2 Nov: the county rule "Property tax 2nd half" as the bar 2pt from the left, plus four tick items (Comcast bill, "Swap furnace filter", "Library books due", "Drop off old paint"). Draw 3 marks shifted 3pt right, then "+1". Callout: "Bar = county rule, not counted in +N; 4 marks → 3 + '+1'; 6 + 44 + 4 + 16 + 6 = 76pt".
  - Holiday-move pair [extra key holiday-move], PLACE B: the Thanksgiving notice moves the usual Thu 26 Nov pickup to Fri 27 Nov. Draw a hollow mark on Fri 27 Nov and a struck ghost on Thu 26 Nov. DateRow: "Thanksgiving — moved to Fri 27 Nov · City of Camas 2026 calendar", line 2 "in 39 days · Fri 27 Nov".

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 Today card [today-card]: as above.
- V2 widget medium [widget-medium], for the 338×158 widget (306 × 126pt content). Widget fill: surface.base in light and dark raised #1E293B in dark, so the sunken cells stay visible.
  - The strip spans 306pt, so the pitch is 21.9pt.
  - Cell height 60pt: 6pt · up to 2 XS marks with a 4pt gap (28pt) · 4pt · a 16pt "+N" line · 6pt. With 3 or more mark items, draw 2 marks, then "+N" (N = items − 2).
  - Under the strip, one 16pt line in widgetCaption: the anchors "Today" and "Mon 26 Oct" in text.strong (no initials), plus "Sat–Sun" in text.secondary, centred under cells 6–7 and 13–14.
  - Then one 16pt legend line in widgetCaption text.secondary with inline S marks. The widget is a standalone surface (C14), so the legend prints a word for each shape drawn in that specimen, and the bar is always keyed as an official rule. HOME A: "○ On record · ✓ You added · ▮ Official rule". PLACE B: "○ On record · ▮ Official rule".
  - Height used: 60 + 4 + 16 + 4 + 16 = 100pt. The remaining 26pt holds f7-today-widget's header line, which carries both the place label and the widget's "As of" text. f7-today-widget owns that line's layout. Print this budget in the gutter.
  - No rows and no add row.
- V3 year-band window crop [x-place-file]. Label it "window crop — YearBand defines the band". It has two forms, each copied from YearBand (00b-04):
  - Phone form (on 03, inside an iOS 393 frame): YearBand's phone anatomy. 326pt wide, 12 columns of 27.2pt ("Oct"–"Sep"), four labelled 24pt lanes with the HOME A month groups, bars, count numerals (captionMedium text.primary) and Tuesday ticks.
  - Desktop form (on 07 crop (c), web-1440): a crop of YearBand's exact-day band (00b · YearBand · 03-desktop-exact-day). It shows the 128px label column plus the Oct and Nov columns (60px each). Items sit on exact days under YearBand's collision rule, so the You lane shows one tick at 23 Oct with "4". The state bars are at 26 Oct and 3 Nov, and the county bar is at 2 Nov.
  - Both forms, per lane, paint in this order: lane fill · window wash · keyline and separators · ticks · today rule · marks, bars and numerals. Marks, bars and numerals carry a 1pt halo that matches the fill beneath them, so the today rule stops short of them and never cuts through the Oct You tick. Light: base lanes and a surface.sunken wash. Dark: base #0F172A lanes and a raised #1E293B wash.
  - The today rule is at 19 Oct. The wash covers 19 Oct–1 Nov and carries the window, with the legend "Shaded: next 14 days". A 1px dashed text.secondary edge marks the end of 1 Nov. In the phone form, that edge sits about 1.8pt from the Oct/Nov separator, so it also rises 4pt above the top lane as a tick.
  - Batch 3 of YearBand checks the phone form against YearBand's phone anatomy and the desktop form against YearBand 03-desktop-exact-day.
- V4 empty: the cells with no marks, then the 00d · QuietDayReceipt line "Checked — nothing in the next two weeks", then "+ Add a date". Summary: "Next 14 days: nothing on file".
  - QuietDayReceipt stand-in: a 16pt bare stroked check in text.secondary (no disc) and the sentence in bodySmall text.primary, always starting with "Checked". The check never sits at a mark position. This is the one exception to grammar rule 4 (Notes E).

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- loading [loading]: a 00d · WarmingSkeleton with 14 cell outlines on surface.sunken and a bar for the header, with no marks or text. It reserves the full height and is static under Reduce Motion.
- ready [ready].
- empty [empty]: V4.
- stale [stale]: the strip is unchanged. The 00a · FreshnessLine "Updated 2h ago" appears under the header, and its words carry the staleness.
- permission-denied [permission-denied]: the viewer may not add dates. The add row is absent, with no ghost row. The strip and rows are unchanged.
- T1 [t1]: PLACE B, with the ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you".
  - One hollow mark on Thu 22 Oct only (frequency Not set), with the DateRow "Pickup day · frequency not set", line 2 "in 3 days · Thu 22 Oct", source City of Camas.
  - The state bar on Mon 26 Oct, with its DateRow line 2 "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct".
  - Summary: "Next 14 days: 2 items". The add row is present, and dates added here stay Only you.
- error [error]: no strip. The slot shows only a 00c · InlineErrorRow "We couldn't load your dates just now" + Retry. This is an error row, not an absence.
- highlighted row [highlighted-row]: after the push "Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow", the Tue 20 Oct DateRow is highlighted and accessibility focus moves to it. The strip is unchanged. Light: an infoBg wash with a 1px semantic.info outline. Dark: per C6. The highlight fades over 300ms after 4s. Under Reduce Motion it appears and disappears without animation.

ARTBOARD CONTENTS
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 01-anatomy · light:
- V1 on iOS 393 with every callout, including the 76pt cell budget.
- The overflow cell and the holiday-move pair, each magnified 4× and labelled.
- R6 contrast table: text.secondary on base, on sunken and on a weekend cell; text.strong on sunken; primary.700 on base. Note under it: "Stale marks use the same ink."
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 02-variants-by-state · light and · dark:
- Rows: today-card · widget-medium. Columns: loading · ready · empty · stale · permission-denied · t1 · error · highlighted-row.
- Layout (fits 1440): three stacked grids of up to 3 columns. Each grid has its own header row and a 160-wide header column. Columns are 358 wide with 24 gaps. The grids hold (loading · ready · empty) / (stale · permission-denied · t1) / (error · highlighted-row). The highlighted-row cell holds the start frame. Under the grids, one extra row labelled "highlighted-row · start and end frames" draws both frames side by side.
- today-card row: as in STATES.
- widget-medium row:
  - loading: "n/a — widgets never show skeletons"
  - ready: V2, HOME A
  - empty: V2 cells with no marks, and "Checked — nothing in the next two weeks" in widgetCaption in place of the legend line
  - stale: "n/a — widget age is the 'As of' text in f7-today-widget's header line"
  - permission-denied: "n/a — the widget has no rows or add row"
  - t1: V2, PLACE B (Thu 22 Oct hollow, state bar on Mon 26 Oct, PLACE B legend)
  - error: "n/a — the widget keeps its last snapshot (f7-today-widget)"
  - highlighted-row: "n/a — the widget has no rows"
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 03-widget-and-window · light and · dark:
- V2 at true size inside a 338×158 outline. Label the rest "owned by f7-today-widget" and print the 100pt budget in the gutter.
- Beside it, the V3 phone form with a leader line to a V1 strip: "same data". The state bar on 26 Oct matches in both.
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 04-platforms-and-voiceover · light (this artboard is the accessibility and platform spec):
- iOS: the strip is one adjustable element with one focus outline; its label is the summary. Draw four consecutive steps (one day per swipe), each in a speech bubble:
  - "Tuesday 20 October: Recycling and garbage, city schedule, on record, not confirmed"
  - "Wednesday 21 October: nothing on file"
  - "Thursday 22 October: nothing on file"
  - "Friday 23 October: Clark Public Utilities bill, you added this"
  - Annotate: "A tap on the strip scrolls to the rows. Cells are not targets; rows follow DateRow."
- Android: the same element, with the TalkBack custom actions "Next day" and "Previous day".
- Web-390: annotate "Hidden from assistive tech because the rows duplicate it; otherwise a list of full-date labels."
- Web-1440: the only per-cell targets. Each cell is a 44px button with its own focus ring (C12). Its accessible name is the native day readout, for example "Tuesday 20 October: Recycling and garbage, city schedule, on record, not confirmed". Empty days read "Wednesday 21 October: nothing on file". Activating a cell moves focus to that day's first row. Hover reveals nothing new.
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 05-ax5-200 · light:
- V1 at iOS AX5:
  - The cells keep their size.
  - The initials are dropped, because 43pt initials do not fit a 23.3pt pitch.
  - The anchors become wrapped lines above the strip ("Today · Mon 19 Oct", "Mon 26 Oct").
  - A caption under the strip keeps the weekend cue: "Lighter cells are Sat and Sun".
  - The summary, rows and add row wrap and grow.
- The same at Android 200%.
- V2 at AX sizes falls back to text: "Next 14 days: 6 items · Tomorrow: Recycling and garbage (on record, not confirmed)".
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 06-greyscale · light: the light 02 artboard, desaturated. Per C8, print one caption under each grid row:
- today-card: "Provenance by shape; rules by bar; weekends by opacity plus initials; moves by strike; empty by the word 'Checked'."
- widget-medium: "Provenance by shape plus legend words; rules by bar plus 'Official rule'; weekends by opacity plus 'Sat–Sun'; empty by the word 'Checked'."
00b · FourteenDayStrip · 07-in-context · light: three mini crops.
- (a) f5-today-calendar-strip on iOS 393: V1 with its rows and the legend line "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this".
- (b) f1-today-tab on Android 412: the strip card inside Today, with its ScopeChip "Your household".
- (c) x-place-file on web-1440: V1 with per-cell buttons, above the V3 desktop form (the exact-day crop defined in V3).
- Under the crops, in caption text.strong: "Also used in: f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet → V2 widget medium · f7-widget-tap-landing → V1 with the highlighted row."

ACCESSIBILITY: see 04. Non-colour cues: see the 06 captions.

COPY: "Next 14 days: N items". Dates always show the weekday, and DateRow line 2 adds the relative count beyond tomorrow. Pickup rows name the bins. Deadlines say "must arrive by". The add row reads exactly "+ Add a date".

PLATFORMS: see 04.

INSTEAD OF (contract doNot)
- No class hue as the only cue: one ink, with the DateRow KindGlyph carrying the class.
- No 6pt dots with ticks: 12pt XS marks, the smallest size where the shapes stay distinct.
- No 14 tiny tap targets on phones: 23pt cells fail 44pt / 48dp (04).
- No statewide or county dot: a full-height bar, because a rule is not an item at this address.
- No even rhythm through a holiday week: the moved day plus a struck ghost.

PUBLISH NAMES (list on Notes G)
- Each drawn 02 cell: "FourteenDayStrip / <row key> / <column key> / <light|dark>".
- Extras: overflow-cell and holiday-move (01, light), highlighted-row-frames (02, light and dark), year-band-window (03, light and dark), web-1440-cell-buttons (04, light), widget-text-fallback (05, light).

NOTES (last batch: append a FourteenDayStrip part to each section of 00b · Notes)
- A. Invented strings: list every quoted string above that is not in the fixtures or the contract.
- B. Assumptions:
  - The cell is 76pt (6 + 44 + 4 + 16 + 6).
  - The widget cell is 60pt, with up to 2 marks, then "+N" (N = items − 2), within 100pt of the 158pt widget. The other 26pt is f7-today-widget's header line, which carries the label and the "As of" text.
  - The widget fill is base in light and raised in dark. The widget legend keys only the shapes drawn, and a bar is always keyed "Official rule".
  - PLACE B's frequency is Not set, so only Thu 22 Oct is drawn. The Thanksgiving move is drawn because the City of Camas notice covers every Thursday route.
  - The overflow cell is outside the window.
  - The strip counts pickups as items; YearBand does not.
  - The dark window wash is raised #1E293B, because dark sunken equals the dark lane fill.
  - In the window crop, the today rule paints under marks, bars and numerals, which carry a 1pt halo. The wash carries the window, and on phones the dashed edge also rises 4pt above the lanes.
  - captionMedium 12/16/500 and widgetCaption 11/16/400 are added to the type scale for this component.
- C. Normalisations: the contract's "Next 14 days: 9 items" → the fixture count "6 items". The empty line follows QuietDayReceipt ("next two weeks").
- D. Deviations: stale marks and holiday ghosts stay at full ink (C11); the contract's 50% opacity is not used.
- E. Open question for 00d: QuietDayReceipt uses a bare stroked check, while grammar rule 4 reserves the ticked disc for "You added this". Should the exemption stay (bare stroke, no disc, always followed by "Checked"), or should its CheckItems get a glyph that is not a check?

DONE WHEN (checks not stated above)

text:
Component 00b-04: YearBand. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): Twelve months of dated rules in four source lanes. It shows the same data as FourteenDayStrip at a longer zoom.
USED IN (print it): x-place-file, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery.
WEB-1440 CARD: 880px wide (848px of content).
TYPE (two styles this component adds to the house scale; use them only as named):
- captionMedium 12/16/500. iOS AX5 → 43, Android 200% → 24.
- widgetCaption 11/16/400, widgets only. At AX sizes the widget drops to its text fallback (05), so widgetCaption has no AX5 or 200% size.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy-phone, with a callout on every part)
- Scope: the 00a · ScopeChip "Your household" (HOME A), above the summary header.
- Summary header, in label 13/18 text.strong: "Next 12 months: 10 dates. Next, in 4 days: Clark Public Utilities bill due Fri 23 Oct." The pickup rhythm is not counted as dates.
- Top line (16pt): "Today" in caption text.primary above the today rule, and "2027" above "Jan".
- Month columns: 12, current month first, in caption text.secondary: "Oct Nov Dec Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep". Phone: 326pt, so each column is 27.2pt.
- Lanes, in order: "You" · "Your city" · "Your county" · "Your state".
  - Phone stack per lane: a 16pt label line (captionMedium text.strong) · a 24pt lane · a 4pt gap. At 768px and wider, the labels sit in a 128px left column.
  - Lane track: surface.base fill, a 1px text.secondary keyline, radius xs 4, and 1px text.secondary month separators.
  - Paint order in each lane: lane fill · window wash · keyline and separators · rhythm ticks · today rule · marks, bars and numerals.
  - Marks, bars and numerals carry a 1pt halo that matches the fill beneath them, so the today rule stops short of them. On phones the rule (≈16.7pt) would otherwise cut across the Oct You tick (7.6–19.6pt). Callout this.
- Marks on phones: one group per month per lane.
  - Each group is an XS 12pt ProvenanceMark centred in the column. When the group has 2 or more items, add a count numeral in captionMedium text.primary, 1pt to the right of the mark.
  - A mixed-provenance group shows the hollow mark, and the rows list each item.
- Rules: county and state rules are solid 4pt bars, full lane height, in text.strong (the same rule as FourteenDayStrip). On phones a bar is centred in its month column, with a numeral when there are 2 or more.
- Collision rule (768px and wider only; exact-day placement happens only there):
  - Use drawn extents: a mark is 12px wide and a bar is 4px wide. Once a cluster holds 2 or more items, its numeral adds 1px plus the numeral's width (about 7px for one digit in captionMedium).
  - Work left to right within each lane. An item joins the current cluster if its left edge is less than 2px from the cluster's right edge (its mark or bar, plus the numeral once there is one). Otherwise the item starts a new cluster.
  - A cluster is drawn as one item at its earliest day, with its count numeral 1px to the right. Mixed provenance shows the hollow mark.
  - Rhythm ticks are not items and never merge.
  - Item centres: x = 128 + 60 × (month index + (day − 0.5) ÷ days in month), where Oct is month index 0.
- Today rule: 1.5px text.primary through all four lanes at 19 Oct (19/31 into Oct).
- Shaded 14-day window: 19 Oct–1 Nov across all lanes.
  - Wash: light surface.sunken; dark raised #1E293B (dark lanes are base #0F172A, so a sunken wash would vanish).
  - The wash carries the window, and the legend line under the band names it: "Shaded: next 14 days".
  - A 1px dashed text.secondary edge marks the end of 1 Nov. On phones that edge sits about 1.8pt past the Oct/Nov separator, so it also rises 4pt above the top lane as a tick, to tell it apart.
- Pickup rhythm, "Your city" lane:
  - Label line: "Your city", an XS hollow mark, and the caption "Pickup every Tuesday · city schedule" in caption text.secondary. At 768px and wider these sit in the label column under "Your city".
  - Ticks: 1.5 × 8pt in text.secondary, one per service week, centred vertically.
  - After the last published city calendar (Dec 2026), the Jan–Sep keyline turns dashed (3 on, 2 off). The caption "Projected after Dec 2026 (last published city calendar)" sits on its own 16pt caption line directly under the Your city lane.
  - Holiday moves on phones: that week's tick is 11pt tall with a 1.5px strike.
  - Holiday moves at 768px and wider: if the moved day is at least 14px from the usual day, the tick moves to the real day and a struck ghost (same shape, full ink) sits on the usual day. Otherwise use the phone form.
- The band reserves its full height while loading.
- Caption under the band, in text.secondary: "The same dates are listed below." Then come 00c · DateRow and 00c · FactRow rows, which are the table.
- Fixture data, HOME A:
  - You (all ticks): Oct "2" (Clark Public Utilities bill Fri 23 Oct; City of Vancouver water bill Wed 28 Oct) · Nov "2" (HOA dues Sun 1 Nov; Comcast bill Mon 2 Nov) · Dec (water-heater warranty ends Sat 12 Dec) · Mar "2" (lease notice deadline Mon 1 Mar; lease ends Wed 31 Mar).
  - Your city: the weekly Tuesday rhythm, on record, not confirmed. There is no holiday move in the published window.
  - Your county: a bar in Nov (property tax 2nd half due Mon 2 Nov; the row may add "moved from Sat 31 Oct").
  - Your state: bars in Oct (online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct) and Nov (in person until 8:00 PM Tue 3 Nov).
  - Total: 10 dates (7 + 1 + 2).

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 place file, HOME A [place-file-home-a]: as above.
- V1 place file, PLACE B [place-file-place-b], with the ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you":
