  - Your city: no rhythm (frequency Not set). One tick on Thu 22 Oct, and the Thanksgiving move in Nov ("moved to Fri 27 Nov", from the published 2026 calendar).
  - City label line: an XS hollow mark and "Pickup day Thursday · frequency not set". The keyline stays solid and there is no projected caption line, because there is no rhythm to project.
  - Your county: a bar in Nov. Your state: bars in Oct and Nov.
  - Summary: "Next 12 months: 3 dates. Next, in 7 days: voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct."
- V2 widget large [widget-large], 338×354pt, with 306×322 of content. Every V2 specimen uses HOME A. Fill: surface.base in light, raised #1E293B in dark (the lanes stay base).
  - 12 columns of 25.5pt. Lane labels are place names: "You · Vancouver · Clark County · Washington".
  - The city label line reads "Vancouver", then the hollow mark, then "On record".
  - Numerals sit 1pt right of the mark, as on phones, in widgetCaption text.primary. The mark and numeral are centred as a group (a 25.5pt column leaves about 6.75pt).
  - The widget draws the today rule (with the same paint order and 1pt halos as V1) but no shaded window.
  - Legend line in widgetCaption text.secondary with inline S marks: "○ On record · ✓ You added · ▮ Official rule". The widget is a standalone surface (C14), so the legend keys only the shapes it draws, and a bar is always keyed as an official rule.
  - All text is at least 11pt.
  - Height budget (print it in the 04 gutter), 268pt in total:
    - label "Larkspur Loop" 20 · gap 4 · top line 16 · month labels 16 · gap 4
    - lanes: 4 × (16 + 24) + 3 × 4 = 172
    - projected caption line 16 ("Projected after Dec 2026") · gap 4 · legend 16
  - The remaining 54pt belongs to f7-today-widget's "As of" line and padding.
  - At AX sizes the widget drops to text (05).
- V3 gallery sample [gallery-sample]: V2 with the HOME A data, static, inside a gallery preview frame no wider than 358.

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- loading [loading]: a 00d · WarmingSkeleton with four lane outlines on surface.sunken, at the exact final height. Static under Reduce Motion.
- ready [ready].
- empty checked [empty-checked]: V4.

name: SlotMeter
job: An honest, dated Founding Neighbor window. Fails closed.
text:
Component 00b-05: SlotMeter. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): An honest, dated Founding Neighbor window. When anything is uncertain, it fails closed.
USED IN (print it): f9-founding-meter-preview, f9-block-founders-panel, f9-nearby-cells-map, f9-verification-promise-copy, f9-invite-rewards-card.
TYPE (one style this component adds to the house scale): bodyMedium 16/24/500. iOS AX5 → 53, Android 200% → 28.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- Heading "Founding Neighbor" in bodyMedium text.primary.
- Segments: five bounded capsules, each 40 × 12pt, radius pill, with 4pt gaps (216pt in total). Taken segments come first, from the left.
  - Taken: solid primary.600 fill with a 1.5px primary.700 edge (#38BDF8 dark, per C6).
  - Open: surface.base fill with a 45° diagonal hatch (1.5px lines every 4pt) in text.secondary, and a 1.5px text.secondary edge.
  - Fixture: 2 taken, 3 open.
- Numeral label, 8pt right of the segments, in label 13/18 text.primary: "3 of 5 open". This count of open slots is the one sanctioned "N of M" here. It counts what is left and never measures progress.
- Elapsed bar, 8pt below the segments: 4 × 216pt, radius pill.
  - The elapsed part is solid text.secondary. The remaining part is an unfilled 1px text.secondary outline (never a border token).
  - The window opened Mon 5 Oct and closes Tue 27 Oct. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct, so the elapsed part is 138pt. Callout: "elapsed 138pt of 216pt; decorative".
  - The bar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech; the date pill carries the meaning.
- Date pill, 8pt below the bar: a neutral 24pt pill with a surface.sunken fill, holding a 12pt calendar glyph and "Closes Tue 27 Oct" in label 13/18, both in text.strong.
- RankBadge (part of this specimen, published only with SlotMeter). It appears only in V2 (HOME A), because a Block Founder rank cannot exist on an unclaimed place.
  - It always sits below the meter, at least 24pt away, never in the same row or sentence as the tier.
  - It is a separate squared shape: 128 × 64pt, radius md 8, surface.sunken fill, a 1px text.secondary edge, 12pt horizontal padding (104pt of text width) and 8pt vertical padding.
  - It holds the overline "BLOCK FOUNDER" in overline 11/16/600 caps +0.5 text.strong, then "#3" in h2 24/32/600 text.primary.
  - At default size the overline sits on one line (it measures about 91–100pt, inside 104pt). It breaks as "BLOCK / FOUNDER" only at AX sizes, where the badge grows vertically.
- R6 contrast table on 01: primary.600 fill on base, primary.700 on base, text.secondary on base, text.strong on sunken.

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 preview card [preview-card] (f9-founding-meter-preview, PLACE B): the heading, meter and date pill, plus the caption "A badge — no money or fee change. You can still claim this address." in bodySmall text.secondary. No RankBadge.
- V2 Block Founders panel [block-founders-panel] (f9-block-founders-panel, HOME A): the meter and date pill in the tier section, and the RankBadge "#3" in a separate rank section below.
- V3 wall line replacement [wall-line]: body text.primary only, with no meter: "3 Founding Neighbor slots are still open on this block."

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- open [open].
- closed [closed]: the meter is absent. Zero open slots counts as closed, so an empty meter is never drawn. In V2, only the tier section is removed. The rank section with "#3" stays, because the RankBadge is a separate earned shape that the founder already holds.
- lookup failed [lookup-failed]: the entire card is absent. In V2, both the tier and rank sections are removed, because the rank comes from the same failed lookup. In V3, the line is absent.
- Closed and lookup-failed cells are absence specimens per C5: draw the host context around the gap, plus the dashed gutter annotation box beside each removed section.

ARTBOARD CONTENTS

- V1 at true size, with every callout.
- Below the V1 card, the RankBadge as a separate labelled part, with the gutter note "RankBadge · shown in V2 (HOME A) only".

- The contrast table.

- Absence cells:

  - block-founders-panel, closed: the panel without its tier section, with the rank section and "#3" still drawn.
  - block-founders-panel, lookup-failed: the panel without its tier and rank sections.
  - wall-line (closed and lookup-failed): the cells-map wall without the line.
- Under the grid, one extra absence specimen [extra key zero-open], with the gutter label "0 of 5 open → treated as closed".
- Dark:
  - The taken fill stays primary.600 (3.57:1 on dark raised), with a #38BDF8 edge.
  - The open fill becomes dark base #0F172A. The hatch uses dark text.secondary, at 6.96:1 on that open fill.
  - The open edges and the elapsed bar use dark text.secondary, at 5.71:1 on dark raised.
00b · SlotMeter · 03-not-provenance · light: one frame with three labelled encodings side by side:
- The SlotMeter (solid vs hatched, plus "3 of 5 open").
- The PublicPointMap cells-map bucket labels: four small rectangles with a 1px text.secondary outline and a 70% surface.base fill, printing "0", "1–5", "6–15" and "16+" in label 13/18 text.primary.
- The 00a · ProvenanceMark legend "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this", with drawn marks.
- Caption: "Solid vs hatched means taken vs open. Filled vs hollow means provenance only."
00b · SlotMeter · 04-ax5-200-greyscale · light:
- V1 at iOS AX5, with the RankBadge drawn as a separate part below it:
  - The segments keep their size, and the numeral label moves below them.
  - The date pill grows and wraps, becoming a rounded rectangle (radius lg 12).
  - The RankBadge grows vertically, with "BLOCK / FOUNDER" on two lines.
- The same at Android 200%.
- V1 and V2 desaturated, captioned "Taken vs open by texture plus numeral."
00b · SlotMeter · 05-in-context · light: five mini crops.
- (a) f9-founding-meter-preview on web-390: V1 on the PLACE B preview.
- (b) f9-block-founders-panel on iOS 393: V2.
- (c) f9-nearby-cells-map on Android 412: V3 as the wall line.
- (d) f9-verification-promise-copy on iOS 393 and (e) f9-invite-rewards-card on iOS 393: each is one line naming the tier, "Founding Neighbor · 3 of 5 open · Closes Tue 27 Oct", and never the rank in the same sentence.

ACCESSIBILITY
- The meter is one element. Its spoken label, printed on 01: "Founding Neighbor slots: 3 of 5 open, closes Tuesday 27 October."
- The RankBadge reads "Block Founder number 3".
- Taken vs open is shown by solid vs hatched, plus the numeral.
- The meter is not a target. Any card action is 44pt / 48dp / 44px.
- Absent states are silent: nothing is announced.

COPY
- Never write "permanent" unless the data model guarantees it.
- Rank ("Block Founder #3") and tier ("Founding Neighbor") never share a sentence.
- Closing dates are dates, never "closes in 6 days" or hh:mm.

PLATFORMS: identical on iOS, Android and web; only the target minimums differ.

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of hollow segments for open slots, draw hatched segments with an ink edge, because hollow means "on record, not confirmed".
- Instead of a warning-tinted pill, draw a neutral surface.sunken pill, because a badge deadline is not an alarm.
- Instead of an hh:mm or "closes in 6 days" countdown, print "Closes Tue 27 Oct", because live countdowns manufacture urgency.
- Instead of a border-token fill for the remaining time, draw a text.secondary outline, because border tokens are never the only edge of a segment.
- Instead of a 2px elapsed bar, draw a 4pt bar, because a 1px outline cannot be drawn around a 2px shape.
- Instead of an empty meter at 0 open, or a meter after a failed lookup, render nothing, because the meter must never promise a slot the system cannot honour.
- Instead of a disc or ring for the rank, draw the squared RankBadge, because discs and rings mean provenance.

PUBLISH NAMES (list on Notes G)
- Each 02 cell: "SlotMeter / <row key> / <column key> / <light|dark>". Absence cells are published too, as the rule that nothing renders.
- Extras: zero-open (02, light and dark), rank-badge (01, light), ax5 (04, light).

NOTES (last batch: append a SlotMeter part to each section of 00b · Notes)
- A. Invented strings: list every quoted string above that is not in the fixtures or the contract, including the normalised "Closes Tue 27 Oct" and the normalised spoken label.
- B. Assumptions:
  - The window opened Mon 5 Oct and closes Tue 27 Oct, with 2 of 5 slots taken.
  - The RankBadge is 128 × 64pt so the overline fits one line at default size (104pt text width). It breaks and grows only at AX sizes.
  - The RankBadge appears only in V2 (HOME A).
  - When the window is closed, the panel keeps the rank section. When the lookup fails, the rank section is removed too, because it comes from the same lookup.
  - bodyMedium 16/24/500 is added to the type scale.
- C. Normalisations: the contract's "Closes Tue, Sep 22" → "Closes Tue 27 Oct", because Tue 22 Sep is before TODAY and that window would be closed. The spoken "closes Tuesday September 22" follows it.
- D. Deviations: the contract's "2px elapsed bar" is drawn 4pt tall with an outlined remaining part, because a 1px outline cannot surround a 2px bar.
- E. Open question (add it to YearBand's relative-count question): "Closes Tue 27 Oct" has no relative count, although dates beyond tomorrow normally add one ("in 8 days"). This follows the no-countdown rule. Should it stay that way?

text:
Component 00b-06: PublicPointMap. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): Shows exactly where neighbours see a post, drawn at true scale from the server's stable public point.
USED IN (print it): f9-privacy-mirror, f9-nearby-cells-map.

FRAMES: 02 cells are drawn at iOS 393 geometry (326pt content). Controls reserve 96pt (148pt for V3). The Android values, 104dp (160dp for V3), apply on 03.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part; the address is HOME A and the viewer is Maya Chen)
- V1 stack, top to bottom: map thumb · 8pt · caption · 8pt · controls. In context only, the hidden-from-neighbors row sits between the caption and the controls, with 8pt above and below it.
- Map thumb: 16:9, 326 × 183pt, radius md 8, 1px text.secondary edge. The frame is centred on the public pin.
  - Base map, neutral tokens only, no brand tint: land is surface.sunken; streets are 4pt surface.base lines with 1px text.secondary casing.
  - Street labels: caption 12/16 text.strong with a 2px surface.base halo: "NE 18th St", "NE 138th Ave", "NE 23rd St".
- Public pin: one 24pt teardrop in text.primary, 2px surface.base halo, 6pt surface.base centre.
- Pin label chip, above the pin: a pill in surface.base, 1px text.secondary edge, shadow md, reading exactly "What neighbors see" in label 13/18 text.primary.
- Scale bar, bottom left, on an 80% surface.base plate: a 1.5px text.primary line with end ticks; labels "0", "0.1", "0.2 mi" in caption 12/16 text.primary on the plate. The thumb spans about 0.8 mi, so 0.2 mi = 81pt.
- Caption, bodySmall text.primary, the map's one-sentence summary, used exactly: "Neighbors see your posts at this spot, the same spot every time, about 0.3 mi from your address."
- Hidden-from row (f9-privacy-mirror; draw only in context): "Hidden from neighbors: your street address, your home on the map".
- Controls:
  - Each button is 44 × 44pt on iOS and web and 48 × 48dp on Android: radius md 8, surface.base fill, 1px text.secondary edge, 20pt text.primary glyph. The accessible names are the words below.
  - One two-row cluster at every size. Left edge of the content width: a zoom column, "Zoom in" (+) above "Zoom out" (−), 8pt apart. Right edge: a 3 × 2 arrow pad with 8pt gaps. Top row: "Move map up" (↑) in the middle slot. Bottom row: "Move map left" (←), "Move map down" (↓), "Move map right" (→).
  - Size: the pad is 148pt wide on iOS and web (3 × 44 + 2 × 8) and 160dp on Android. The cluster needs at least 208pt (224dp) with a 16pt minimum gap between column and pad, so it fits 326pt. It is 96pt tall on iOS and web and 104dp on Android.
  - Disabled buttons: fill unchanged, still focusable, with a reason. Light: glyph and edge in text.muted. Dark: glyph and edge in #475569 (an added dark value, listed on Notes D), so disabled stays distinct from the enabled #94A3B8 edge. Disabled controls are exempt from the contrast minimums; the reason text carries the meaning.
  - Focus order: Zoom in, Zoom out, Move map up, Move map left, Move map down, Move map right, then List cells when present.
- Cells-map parts (V3):
  - V3 stack, top to bottom: map 326 × 326 (the same base map at the same zoom, with streets and street labels, no pin, no chip, scale bar bottom left) · 8pt · summary line · 4pt · FreshnessLine · 8pt · controls · 8pt · List cells.
  - Grid: three columns and three rows of 108/110/108pt, no gaps; neighbouring cells share one 1px text.secondary outline. Each cell has a 70% surface.base fill over the base map.
  - Each cell prints its bucket label centred in label 13/18 text.primary: "0", "1–5", "6–15" or "16+".
  - The user's cell gets a 2px primary.600 inner outline inside its rectangle (the contract calls it a ring; #38BDF8 in dark mode), and "Your cell" in caption text.primary, centred 4pt below its bucket label.
  - "List cells": a text button (primary.700; #38BDF8 in dark mode), left-aligned, 44pt tall (48dp on Android). The V3 controls block is therefore 148pt tall on iOS and web (96 + 8 + 44) and 160dp on Android (104 + 8 + 48).
- Contrast table on 01, R6 rows, each labelled with its kind and threshold:
  - text.secondary on base · text ("Simplified map") and edges · 4.5:1
  - text.secondary on sunken · outline (map edge, street casing) · 3:1
  - text.strong on sunken · text (street labels) · 4.5:1
  - text.primary on sunken · text and pin · 4.5:1
  - primary.700 on base · text ("See the spot", "List cells") · 4.5:1
  - primary.600 on the 70% base cell fill (light) · outline · 3:1
  - #38BDF8 on the dark cell fill · outline · 3:1

PENDING DECISION: range box R (not a variant)
- The ±0.005° box is centred on the home by definition, so drawing it may reveal the home. Until the founder answers the range-box question on Notes E, draw R only on 00b · PublicPointMap · 01-anatomy · light, inside a dashed 1px text.secondary annotation frame labelled "PENDING DECISION — do not publish". Draw it on no other artboard and never publish it.
- How to draw it: the real box, about 1.11 km tall × 0.78 km wide (about 0.69 × 0.49 mi), as a 1.5px dashed text.secondary rectangle with no fill. Use a zoom where the 326pt thumb spans about 1.6 mi, so the box is about 141 × 99pt and fits the 183pt-tall thumb with a margin. The scale bar reads "0", "0.25", "0.5 mi" (0.25 mi = 51pt). The box sits off-centre in the frame.

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 privacy mirror [privacy-mirror]: as in ANATOMY.
- V2 composer one-liner [composer-one-liner]: a row at least 44pt tall with a 16pt pin glyph in text.secondary, the bodySmall text.primary line "Neighbors see this post at the same spot as your other posts, about 0.3 mi from your address.", and a trailing 44pt text button "See the spot" (primary.700; #38BDF8 in dark mode) that opens V1. No map is drawn.
- V3 cells map [cells-map]: the V3 stack from ANATOMY.
  - Cell names and buckets, user's cell in the centre:

    - bottom row: South-west 0 · South 0 · South-east 1–5
  - Summary line, bodySmall text.primary: "14 neighbor posts in your cell in 30 days. 3 Pantopus posts not counted."
  - 00a · FreshnessLine: "Updated 12m ago".

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- ready [ready].
- loading [loading]: a 00d · WarmingSkeleton panel: a surface.sunken 16:9 block (square for V3), with the controls drawn as outlines at their reserved height. V1 loading shows the caption as text. V2 shows its text immediately. Static under Reduce Motion.
- vector fallback [vector-fallback]: when tiles fail, land is surface.base and streets are 1px text.secondary lines. "Simplified map" in caption text.secondary sits 4pt above the map. Everything else stays: on V1 the street labels, pin, chip, scale bar and caption; on V3 the same cells, bucket labels, "Your cell" outline, scale bar and text lines.
- offline [offline]:
  - With a cache: the cached map. The pan and zoom buttons are disabled, with the reason caption "Moving the map needs a connection." in caption text.secondary.
    - V1 stack: map · 4pt · FreshnessLine "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" · 8pt · caption · 8pt · controls · 4pt · reason caption.
    - V3 stack: the V3 stack with "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" in place of "Updated 12m ago", and the reason caption 4pt below the controls, then 8pt, then "List cells", which stays enabled and lists the cached buckets.
  - With no cache: the reserved map slot (16:9, square for V3) is a surface.sunken block with the centred line "You're offline. The map needs a connection." in body text.strong. All buttons are drawn disabled, including "List cells"; the centred line is their reason.
    - V1: the caption stays (map slot · 8pt · caption · 8pt · controls).
    - V3: the summary line and FreshnessLine are not drawn, because there are no counts without data (map slot · 8pt · controls · 8pt · List cells).

ARTBOARD CONTENTS

Street labels and scale-bar labels stay at their base size, because map labels are graphic geometry under the AX5 rule. The glyph buttons keep their size and the two-row cluster.

name: FactCount
job: States how much is on file without implying incompleteness.
text:
Component 00b-07: FactCount. Follow the board rules from the setup message. This is the last component on the board.

PURPOSE (print it): States how much is on file for the address, without implying that anything is missing.
USED IN (print it): x-place-file, f11-keeper-strip, f1-claim-receipt.

FRAMES: 02 cells are drawn on a 358pt iOS card. Draw the target outline around the whole block (at least 44 × 44pt; the block height when taller).

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- A vertical block, at most 160pt wide. The place file header and the keeper strip use the same geometry.
- Line 1: the integer in h3 20/28/600 text.primary (the contract gives only its weight, "label weight" = 600; the h3 size is a design choice, see Notes B), a 4pt gap, then "on file" in caption 12/16 text.secondary, sharing one baseline.
- Line 2, 6pt below line 1: category pips, one labelled pip for each category that has anything known, in this fixed order: Place · Dates · Money · People · Proof.
  - Pip: height = its text line height + 4pt (20pt at default), radius pill, surface.sunken fill, captionMedium 12/16/500 text.strong (9.37:1), 8pt horizontal padding, 4pt gaps. captionMedium is the board's weight-500 caption and scales as caption (AX5 43, 200% 24).
  - Pips wrap to a further line when needed, 4pt below the previous pip line. For the fixture, Place · Dates · Money fills the first pip line and People wraps, so V1 and V2 are 78pt tall (28 + 6 + 20 + 4 + 20).
  - A pip is always a word, never a bare dot, so categories are carried by words, not colour.
- Unknown categories draw nothing (see INSTEAD OF).
- Target: the whole block is one target of at least 44pt (48dp on Android, 44px on web), extended beyond the visible block if needed. Tapping it opens the place file; inside x-place-file, it scrolls to the list.
- Fixture: HOME A shows "14 on file" with Place · Dates · Money · People.
- Contrast table on 01, R6 rows: text.primary on base · text · 4.5:1; text.secondary on base · text · 4.5:1; text.strong on sunken · text · 4.5:1. In dark mode, pips on a dark raised card use dark sunken #0F172A; pips on dark base use dark raised #1E293B (R5).

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 place file header [place-file-header]: "14 on file" with Place · Dates · Money · People, left-aligned.
- V2 keeper strip [keeper-strip]: "14 on file" with Place · Dates · Money · People, right-aligned within 160pt. Line 1 and each pip line are right-aligned; pip order still reads left to right.
- V3 T1 [t1] (PLACE B, "Saved place · Only you"): "7 on file" with Place · Dates only (only these two can exist at T1). Height 54pt (28 + 6 + 20).
- Claim-time count (extra, only in the f1-claim-receipt crop): "11 on file" with Place · Dates, because the facts carried into a claim come from T1.

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- default [default].
- loading [loading]: a 00d · WarmingSkeleton: a surface.sunken integer bar 24 × 28pt (the line height), a 6pt gap, then two 48 × 20pt pill shapes on one line with a 4pt gap, aligned as the variant. The block reserves the final height of the variant it replaces: 78pt for V1 and V2, 54pt for T1. Static under Reduce Motion.
- offline [offline]: the count stays. The 00a · FreshnessLine "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" sits 4pt below the block, wraps within 160pt, and is aligned like the variant (left for V1 and T1, right for V2).

ARTBOARD CONTENTS
00b · FactCount · 01-anatomy · light: V1 with every callout, one pip magnified 4×, and the contrast table.
00b · FactCount · 02-variants-by-state · light and · dark: a grid.
- Rows: place-file-header · keeper-strip · t1. Columns: default · loading · offline.
- Every cell is drawn. The t1 row shows the ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you" beside the block.
- Print the spoken label under each default cell.
00b · FactCount · 03-ax5-200-greyscale · light:
- V1 and V2 at iOS AX5: the integer and "on file" stack; pips grow to their scaled line height + 4pt with 4pt gaps and wrap one per line if needed; the 160pt maximum width is lifted to the full row; in the keeper strip the block moves below the name and mood line.
- The same at Android 200%.
- All three variants desaturated, captioned "Categories by printed words, not colour."
00b · FactCount · 04-in-context · light: three mini crops.
- (a) x-place-file on iOS 393: the header "Your place file" with V1 "14 on file" and the ScopeChip "Your household".
- (b) f11-keeper-strip on Android 412: Ollie (otter) with the mood word "On it", the mood line "Recycling and garbage go out tomorrow by 6:30 AM", and V2 "14 on file".
- (c) f1-claim-receipt on web-390: "11 on file" with Place · Dates in the claim receipt, at claim time.

ACCESSIBILITY
- The block is one element. Its spoken label starts with the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name):
  - V1 and V2: "14 on file: place, dates, money, people."
  - T1: "7 on file: place, dates."
  - Claim receipt: "11 on file: place, dates."

COPY
- Use "on file" exactly. Never "X of Y", never "knows" (no "Ollie knows"), never a percentage.

PLATFORMS: identical on iOS, Android and web; only the target minimums in ANATOMY differ.

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of a closed five-segment ring with outlined empty segments, draw the integer and word pips for known categories only, because an empty slot reads as a task left undone.
- Instead of a progress bar, level or XP, draw the plain count, because the count states what is held, not how far someone has come.
- Instead of a count-up animation (in any state, including loading), show the final number at once, because motion here implies an achievement.
- Instead of "3 of 6 things on file", write "14 on file", because fractions imply incompleteness.
- Instead of different counts for the same home on different surfaces, show "14 on file" everywhere at the same moment, because drift reads as an error.
- Instead of the spoken "14 things on file", say "14 on file", because the spoken name must contain the visible text.
- Instead of greyed placeholder pips, outlines or "0" for unknown categories, draw nothing, because the host x-place-file owns any "You can also add" list; this component never draws one.

PUBLISH NAMES (list them on Notes G)
- Each 02 cell: "FactCount / <row key> / <column key> / <light|dark>".
- Extras: "FactCount / claim-time / light" (from 04) and "FactCount / ax5 / light" (from 03).

NOTES (last batch: append a FactCount part to each section, then finish the board)
- A. Invented strings: "7 on file"; "Your place file"; the three spoken labels; "On it"; "Recycling and garbage go out tomorrow by 6:30 AM"; the greyscale caption "Categories by printed words, not colour."; the FreshnessLine value "You're offline · as of 7:04 AM" (the pattern comes from 00a).
- B. Assumptions: the claim-time receipt shows Place · Dates only, because claimed facts come from T1. The brief's "You can also add" list belongs to the host x-place-file, not to this component. PLACE B has 7 facts on file. The integer is drawn at h3 size; the contract gives only its weight. Pips use captionMedium 12/16/500, which scales as caption at AX5 and 200%.
- C. Normalisations: none for FactCount.
- D. Deviations:
  - The pips sit below the integer, not beside it as the contract says, so the block fits its 160pt maximum width.
  - The contract gives the keeper strip "11 on file". The keeper strip shows "14 on file" to match the place file for the same home; "11 on file" is used only as the claim-time count.
  - The contract's spoken label "11 things on file: …" is drawn as "14 on file: …", so the spoken name contains the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3).
- E. none for FactCount.
- Finish the board:
  - Section F lists every n/a cell on the board with its reason (including PublicPointMap composer-one-liner × vector-fallback). FactCount has none.
  - Section G lists every publish name on the board, including the FactCount names above.
  - Section E: keep every question already there, in its existing order, and number them consecutively from 1. Do not drop or merge any question, and update any "open question (n)" reference on the board to match. The list is expected to include (in any order): the range box, relative counts, the 00a stale-mark style question (if present), the QuietDayReceipt check, and the PM2.5 sentence.

- 00b · Notes is complete for the whole board: sections A–G, with every component's entries.

name: Board setup

text:
Setup 00c-00: Foundations board 00c, Rows and lists.

Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is Foundations board 00c, "Rows and lists". Read this message, then reply. Draw nothing yet.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
This is a component specimen board with no screens. I will send one component per message, in this order: DateRow, FactRow, FirstWeekRow, BillRow, MemberRow, InviteRow, NotificationRow, TextActionRow, LockedActionRow, GrantLimitList, InlineErrorRow, ThumbnailRail. Each component message is that component's complete specification. This message holds only the rules for all twelve, R1 to R14 ("the board rules").
Later screen projects will use these components by exact name and key, with no other reference, so every specimen must be complete, exact and labelled. ATTACH: none.

PUBLISH
When I accept a component, I add it to the published Pantopus design system under its exact name above. Its variants and states are published under the printed keys from its grid (R7), e.g. DateRow variant "deadline-voter", state "highlighted-arrival". Never publish a drawing labelled "stand-in" (R11); those components come from their own Foundations boards.

HOW EACH COMPONENT TURN WORKS
- Each component message ends with ARTBOARDS, a BATCH PLAN and DONE WHEN. Draw only what the BATCH PLAN lists for the current turn, then stop and wait for "continue". Never start a component before its message arrives.
- Before stopping, check the batch against DONE WHEN and name anything missing.
- If a component message and these rules disagree, the component message wins; note it on Notes.
- Ask a question only if two readings would produce materially different components.

R1. ARTBOARDS
- Name each artboard "00c · <ComponentName> · <NN-what> · <light|dark>", exactly as the component's ARTBOARDS list gives it (this replaces the house style's surface naming). Show the name as a visible label above the frame in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- Each component gets exactly five artboards, in this order:
  01-anatomy · light: one specimen at 2x with numbered callouts (R3), then five labelled text panels: ACCESSIBILITY, COPY RULES, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF, USED IN.
  02-grid · light: the variant × state grid at 1x (R7).
  03-ax5-200-greyscale · light: at the top, two large-text columns labelled "iOS · AX5 (body 53pt)" and "Android · 200%" (Android 14 nonlinear scaling), per R9. Below, full width at 1x, a greyscale (0% saturation) copy of the whole 02 grid, per R10.
  04-in-context · light: the crops the component names (R13).
  05-grid · dark: the 02 grid in the same layout in dark tokens (R5), plus the 1x anatomy specimen in dark at top left.
- The last artboard in the project is "00c · Notes" (R14).

R2. CANVAS AND UNITS
- Artboards are at least 1440 wide, on surface.app (dark: dark app). Grow them to fit cells at 1x; never scale a cell down.
- 1pt = 1dp = 1px. Callouts give iOS pt, or all three where they differ ("44pt / 48dp / 44px").
- Row frames unless a cell says otherwise: iOS 393pt with 16pt side margins (361pt content); Android 412dp (380dp content); web-390 390px (358px content); web-1440 a 720px list column.
- Spacing and radii by name (spacing.2 = 8, spacing.3 = 12, spacing.4 = 16; md 8, lg 12).

R3. CALLOUTS
- Outside the component: a numbered circle (1px text.secondary outline), a 1px text.secondary leader, and a caption with size and token, e.g. "② title · body 16/24/400 · text.primary". Numbers match the component's ANATOMY list.
- Callouts never overlap the component. Spacing uses 1px dimension lines ("16pt · spacing.4").
- Draw every target as a dashed 1px text.secondary rectangle labelled "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px".
- Every 01-anatomy has a "web menu" callout (R12), worded as the component message says.

R4. TYPE AND LIGHT TOKENS
- Type scale only: body 16/24/400 · bodyMedium 16/24/500 · bodySmall 14/20/400 · bodySmallMedium 14/20/500 · label 13/18/600 · caption 12/16/400 · captionMedium 12/16/500 · overline 11/16/600 caps +0.5. SF Pro on iOS, Roboto on Android, system-ui on web. Amounts use tabular figures.
- Token names only, never hex on a component. Light values are in the house style; this board also uses primary.50, primary.700, errorBg, infoBg and identity.home.
- text.muted appears nowhere on this board.
- Secondary-role text (captions, "Not set", disabled labels, reason captions) is text.secondary on base, raised and app, and text.strong on surface.sunken and errorBg, where text.secondary fails (R6).
- Text buttons and links are bodySmallMedium primary.700 unless a component says otherwise.
- Semantic hues and identity.home go on glyphs and rules only, never on text.
- Border tokens are decoration. Row separators are 1px border.default hairlines inset 16pt from the leading edge, and no row relies on a hairline as its only edge. Any edge that carries meaning uses text.secondary ink.

R5. DARK MODE (every 05)
Dark tokens: surface.base #0F172A, raised #1E293B, sunken #0F172A (same as base), app #020617; text.primary #E5E7EB, text.strong #F1F5F9, text.secondary #94A3B8; border.default #1F2937, strong #374151, subtle #1E293B, focus #38BDF8. Links and text buttons use dark border.focus.
Dark has no infoBg, errorBg, primary.50, primary.700 or semantic tokens, and dark sunken equals base. Use exactly these substitutes, and record each use on Notes:
- D1 Highlight: dark raised wash plus the 4pt leading bar in dark border.focus. On a row already on raised (D3), the bar alone.
- D2 Write-failure fill: dark raised plus a 1.5px error border.
- D3 A row on sunken in light sits on dark raised, with dark text.strong.
- D4 Any sunken fill (skeleton bars, avatars, chip fills, thumbnail slots, a disabled filled button) becomes dark raised on a base row and dark border.strong on a raised row; text inside is dark text.strong.
- D5 Selection: dark raised plus a 1.5px dark border.focus edge plus a leading check in dark border.focus. Never primary.50.
- D6 Non-link primary.700 graphics (progress rings, spinners, unread dot) use dark border.focus; ring tracks use dark border.strong.
- D7 Semantic glyph hues and the identity.home rule keep their light values, on glyphs and rules only. Caption the R6 ratio beside the first occurrence on each 05.
- D8 Any card gets a 1px dark text.secondary keyline, because dark border.default on raised is 1.00:1. Caption its ratio beside the first occurrence.
Increase Contrast: no separate artboard. Every R6 check must also hold under Increase Contrast; the only change is that light cards get the same text.secondary keyline as D8. Write this once as a caption on each 05.

R6. CONTRAST TABLE (use these numbers in captions; never place a pair marked FAIL)
Light text, 4.5:1:
- text.primary: 16 or more on every light surface · text.strong: 9.37 or more on every light surface
- text.secondary: base 4.83 · raised 4.63 · app 4.51 · infoBg 4.54 · sunken 4.39 FAIL · errorBg 4.42 FAIL
- primary.700: base 5.93 · sunken 5.39 · primary.50/infoBg 5.57 · errorBg 5.42
Light graphics, 3:1:
- border.focus: base 4.10 · infoBg 3.84 · sunken 3.72
- success: base 3.77 · sunken 3.42
- warning: base 3.19 · sunken 2.89 FAIL
- error: base 4.83 · sunken 4.39
- identity.home: base 3.30 · infoBg 3.09 · sunken 2.99 FAIL
- text.secondary glyph or keyline: base 4.83 · raised 4.63 · app 4.51 · sunken 4.39
- primary.700 ring on border.strong track: 4.03
Dark text, 4.5:1:
- text.primary: base 14.42 · raised 11.82 · text.strong: 9.41 or more everywhere
- text.secondary: base 6.96 · raised 5.71 · on border.strong 4.02 FAIL
- border.focus links: base 8.33 · raised 6.83
Dark graphics, 3:1:
- border.focus: base 8.33 · raised 6.83 · on border.strong 4.81
- success: base 4.74 · raised 3.88 · on border.strong 2.74 FAIL
- warning: base 5.60 · raised 4.59
- error: base 3.70 · raised 3.03 · on border.strong 2.13 FAIL
- identity.home: base 5.42 · raised 4.44
- text.secondary keyline (D8): raised 5.71 · app 7.87

R7. GRID LABELS AND KEYS
- Variants are rows, labelled at the left in label 13/18 text.strong. States are columns, labelled at the top in overline 11/16/600.
- Each label reads exactly "<code> · <key>" with the codes and keys from the component message (e.g. "V3a · deadline-voter", "S2a · highlighted-arrival"). Under it, print "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- Keys are lowercase and hyphenated, with no spaces, no "/", no fixture string and no date. Publish names use keys only.
- Under every cell, in caption 12/16 text.secondary, print exactly "<ComponentName> · <variant key> · <state key>" (e.g. "DateRow · deadline-voter · done").
- Draw only the cells in GRID CELLS. Every other position stays empty canvas: no frame, no label, no "n/a".
- An n/a cell appears only where a component writes "n/a": a plain cell reading "n/a — <reason>" in caption text.secondary, with the normal cell caption. Never draw a ghost component there.

R8. TARGETS, FOCUS, HIGHLIGHT, SELECTION, DISABLED
- Targets: 44pt iOS, 48dp Android with 8dp gaps, 44px web. A ProvenanceMark, glyph or dot is never a target by itself.
- Focus: a 2px border.focus ring 2px outside the whole row. When a row holds a separate target (link, overflow, Retry, Resend, Add, dismiss), focus on it rings that target only.
- Highlight (arrival from a notification): an infoBg wash across the row plus a 4pt border.focus bar on the leading edge, full height. No outline, never a check. If the row has a 2px identity.home rule, the bar sits directly inside it. In an "on arrival" frame the focus ring is also drawn 2px outside the row, so bar and ring never touch. Dark: D1.
- Selection: primary.50 fill plus a leading check glyph. Dark: D5.
- Focus, highlight and selection must look different. Wherever a grid has a highlighted or selected cell, a focused cell sits directly beside it.
- Disabled text actions look the same everywhere: label in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken, per R4), never primary.700 or text.muted, still focusable, with a reason caption directly under it in caption 12/16 (same colour rule). Disabled filled buttons: surface.sunken fill, text.strong label (dark: D4).
- Disabled controls stay in the accessibility tree with their reason as a hint.

R9. AX5 / 200% (every 03)
- Text wraps and never truncates, except a field the component names as truncating at default sizes only.
- Side-by-side pairs stack. Trailing elements (amount, mark, chevron, text action) move below the text block, aligned to its leading edge, and keep their targets.
- Leading glyphs and marks scale with the text; ProvenanceMark keeps its shape. Row heights grow; stated heights are minimums.

R10. GREYSCALE (every 03)
Draw the whole 02 grid desaturated, same labels and captions. Beside it, caption each variant or state with its non-colour cue, e.g. "done = tick glyph + 'You marked this done'". A cell that reads only through colour is a defect: fix the component.

R11. SHARED STAND-INS
If the published design system has one of these, use it; otherwise draw this stand-in, labelled "stand-in". Components may add their own.
- ProvenanceMark: OFFICIAL = solid disc; ON RECORD, NOT CONFIRMED = ring, stroke at least 1.5px; YOU ADDED = solid disc with a knocked-out tick (a cut-out, never a second colour). Ink text.secondary (dark: dark text.secondary). S = 16pt in rows; XS = 12pt minimum. Spoken "official", "on record, not confirmed", "you added this". Filled vs hollow means provenance only. Every other check on this board is a bare stroke, never a disc.
- Legend line: "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this" in caption text.secondary, or the word beside the first mark.
- ScopeChip: pill, 24pt, surface.sunken fill (dark: D4), 12pt glyph plus label 13/18 text.strong. Exactly "Saved place · Only you" (person glyph) or "Your household" (house glyph), spoken "Visible to only you" / "Visible to your household". Sentences exactly "Only you will see this." / "Everyone in this household will see this."; where finance access differs, name the people ("You and Sam can see these"), never "Everyone". When the chip opens the scope control, draw its 44pt / 48dp target.
- StatusChip: pill, 24pt, captionMedium, surface.sunken fill (dark: D4), text.strong; any semantic hue on a leading glyph only; one per row.
- InlineUndo: the row collapses in place to "<what happened> · Undo", announced with role=status. Undo is focusable, 44pt, and stays until the user leaves the screen. No countdown.
- WarmingSkeleton: surface.sunken bars (dark: D4) in the final geometry and height, no text, announced once as "Loading" (aria-busy on web); static under Reduce Motion.
- FreshnessLine / OfflineNotice: caption text.secondary, e.g. "You're offline · as of 5:52 PM" (invented). No banner colour.

R12. PLATFORMS AND THE WEB MENU
- Unless a component's PLATFORMS says otherwise, write "No platform differences" in its panel.
- Custom actions are VoiceOver custom actions on iOS and TalkBack custom actions on Android.
- On web, custom actions that are not already visible buttons get a row menu button: a 20px ellipsis in a 44px target at the row's trailing edge. An existing overflow button or visible buttons already are the web menu; never add a second. Draw it in every web crop where it applies.

R13. IN-CONTEXT CROPS (every 04)
- Label each crop "<surface id> · <ios|android|web-390|web-1440>". Show only enough host to place the component: outlines, section titles, neighbouring rows.
- Every crop that shows a ProvenanceMark also shows the legend line and the place's ScopeChip: "Your household" for Home A, "Saved place · Only you" for Place B.

R14. FIXTURES, MOTION, NOTES
- Use the house-style FIXTURES. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific; relative counts come from it. Dates always show the weekday ("Fri 23 Oct"), never numeric formats, never "midnight". Emails use @example.com. No percentage or completion fraction is drawn on any specimen, callout or crop; an INSTEAD OF panel may name one only as the pattern to avoid.
- Motion: highlights fade within 300ms. Under Reduce Motion they cross-fade, spinners are removed and in-progress labels stay as static text. Idle loops stop within 5s.
- "00c · Notes" is the last artboard. Create it when a BATCH PLAN first says so; update it whenever a BATCH PLAN says so. One line per item.
  Board section first: each D1–D8 with the components that used it and the D7/D8 ratios; the Increase Contrast note; the R11 stand-ins you drew; any string you added that no message lists; any state you could not draw, and why.
  Then one section per component, in delivery order, under its exact name, with the lists its message gives: Invented strings · Fixture deltas · Contract conflicts (each "drawn as X instead of contract Y") · Assumptions.

Reply 'ready' and wait for the first component.

name: DateRow
job: One dated fact in a list: the row grammar shared by the strip list, calendar agenda, place file Dates and reminder rows.
text:
Component 00c-01: DateRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: DateRow. This message is the complete DateRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). One dated fact in a list. Its row grammar is shared by the 14-day strip list, the calendar agenda, the place file Dates section and reminder rows.

USED IN (panel): f5-today-calendar-strip · f3-household-calendar · x-place-file · x-date-sheet · f3-household-notifications · f7-today-widget.

EXTRA STAND-INS FOR THIS COMPONENT (label each "stand-in", per R11)
- KindGlyph: a 24pt line icon with a 2pt stroke in text.strong, with one distinct drawing per kind: garbage, recycling, garbage+recycling, notice deadline, warranty ends, HOA dues, property-tax due, property-tax appeal, voter registration. Never one generic calendar icon.
- SourceCaption: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "authority · scope · as-of". It wraps and never ellipsises the authority.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V3a at 2x for callouts ①–⑦ and ⑩. Beside it, draw V3c in S3 (done) at 2x for callouts ⑧ and ⑨.
① Row: minimum height 56pt, padding 16pt horizontal and 12pt vertical, on surface.base. The whole row is the target: draw the dashed target rectangle around it.
② Leading KindGlyph, 24pt, text.strong, top-aligned with the title, with a 12pt (spacing.3) gap after it.
③ Title: body 16/24/400, text.primary. It wraps and is never truncated.
④ Line 2: caption 12/16 text.secondary, the relative date then the absolute date, e.g. "in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct". "Tonight", "Today" and "Tomorrow" stand alone, with no absolute date after them. An approximate date reads "about Dec 2026".
⑤ SourceCaption short form (authority · scope). It continues line 2 after a middot, or wraps to line 3.
⑥ Trailing ProvenanceMark S (16pt), vertically centred, with 8pt (spacing.2) between it and the text. It is not a target.
⑦ Optional chip after the title reading "Statewide — WA", in ScopeChip geometry (24pt pill, surface.sunken fill, label 13/18 text.strong) with a 12pt state-outline glyph. It states coverage, not visibility.
⑧ Annual rows and self-entered rows: a 2px identity.home rule on the leading edge, full row height, plus a recurrence caption on the last line in caption text.secondary ("Every year", "Every month" or "Does not repeat").
⑨ Done tick: a 16pt stroke check before the title. It is a bare stroke, not a disc, so it cannot be mistaken for the YOU ADDED mark.
⑩ Web menu callout: "web menu: a row menu button (20px ellipsis, 44px target) after the mark, holding Edit · Remind me · Where this comes from · Mark done".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
V1 pickup. Home A as of TODAY, before Maya confirmed her pickup day. The title names the bins.
- V1a · pickup-both: garbage+recycling glyph · title "Recycling and garbage" · line 2 "Tomorrow · Waste Connections · city schedule" · hollow mark.
- V1b · pickup-garbage: garbage glyph · "Garbage only" · "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct · Waste Connections · city schedule" · hollow mark.
- V2 · holiday-moved (Place B, Camas): garbage glyph · "Thanksgiving — moved to Fri 27 Nov" · "in 39 days · Fri 27 Nov · City of Camas 2026 calendar" · hollow mark.
V3 deadline. The weekday is always shown, and received-by deadlines say "must arrive by".
- V3a · deadline-voter: voter registration glyph · "Online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct" · chip "Statewide — WA" · "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct · Washington Secretary of State · statewide" · filled mark.
- V3b · deadline-notice: notice deadline glyph · "Tell your landlord in writing by Mon 1 Mar 2027" · "in 133 days · Mon 1 Mar 2027 · Lease ends Wed 31 Mar 2027" · last line "Does not repeat · Reminder Sat 30 Jan 2027" · YOU ADDED mark · identity.home rule.
- V3c · deadline-tax: property-tax due glyph · "Property tax, 2nd half" · "in 14 days · Mon 2 Nov · Clark County Treasurer · county-wide" · last line "Every year" · filled mark · identity.home rule.
- V4 · conditional-rule: property-tax appeal glyph · "Property-tax appeal window" · "Closes Thu 1 Jul 2027, or 60 days after your value notice was mailed" · "Clark County Board of Equalization · county-wide" · last line "Every year" · filled mark · identity.home rule.
- V5 · reminder: warranty glyph · "Reminder: Water-heater warranty ends Sat 12 Dec" · "in 54 days · Sat 12 Dec · You added this" · last line "Does not repeat" · YOU ADDED mark · identity.home rule.
- V5x · reminder-approx (fixture delta: the warranty date was entered as approximate): warranty glyph · "Water-heater warranty ends" · "about Dec 2026" · last line "Does not repeat" · YOU ADDED mark · identity.home rule.
- V6 · money: HOA dues glyph · "HOA dues" · amount "$285.00" in bodyMedium with tabular figures, right-aligned and placed before the mark · "in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov · You added this" · last line "Every month" · YOU ADDED mark · identity.home rule.

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, S2a, S2b, SF, S3, S4)
- S1 · default.
- S2 · highlighted: arrival from a notification, per R8 (dark: D1), with accessibility focus moved onto the row. Drawn as two columns:
  - S2a · highlighted-arrival: infoBg wash, 4pt leading bar, and the focus ring 2px outside the row.
  - S2b · highlighted-decayed: wash and bar gone; the focus ring remains.
- SF · focused: the R8 focus ring on the whole row.
- S3 · done: the ⑨ tick before the title; title and line 2 in text.secondary; line 2 prefixed "You marked this done ·". Done is personal. On every row, including the civic V3a row, it stays Only you and is never shown to the household.
- S4 · permission-hidden: the row is not rendered at all.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 26 cells)
- S1 and S3: V1a, V1b, V2, V3a, V3b, V3c, V4, V5, V5x and V6 (20 cells).
- S2a and S2b: V1a and V3a (4 cells).
- SF: V3a, so it sits directly beside V3a S2a and V3a S2b (1 cell).
- S4: one cell, in the V6 row: a three-row list of V1a, [absent V6], V3a. The rows above and below close the gap, with no placeholder and no ghost row. An annotation arrow outside the list reads "row absent: viewer lacks permission" (1 cell).
- Outside the V3a S3 cell, annotate: "done stays Only you".

DARK (05)
- Rows stay on dark surface.base. Highlight uses D1. The "Statewide — WA" chip fill uses D4. Marks and the done tick use dark text.secondary; each KindGlyph uses dark text.strong.
- The identity.home rule keeps its hue (D7). Beside the first one, caption "identity.home on dark base 5.42:1".
- Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V3a and V6 in both columns.
- The title wraps to as many lines as it needs.
- The "Statewide — WA" chip drops below the title.
- Line 2 wraps at middots.
- The amount and the mark move below the text block: the amount first, then the mark, scaled to about 28pt.
- The KindGlyph scales to 32pt and stays top-aligned.
- The identity.home rule stays full height.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- provenance = disc vs ring vs disc with knocked-out tick.
- done = stroke tick + "You marked this done".
- highlighted = 4pt leading bar.
- annual = 2px rule + "Every year".
- kind = KindGlyph shape.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The whole row is one element and one target (minimum 56pt), read in visual order. The mark and the glyph are not targets.
- Spoken pattern: "<title>, <line 2 as shown>, <authority, scope>, <mark name>". The label speaks only the dates the row shows, so "Tomorrow" is spoken as "tomorrow" with no absolute date. Example: "Recycling and garbage, tomorrow, Waste Connections city schedule, on record, not confirmed."
- Done rows start with "You marked this done". Done stays Only you.
- Custom actions: Edit · Remind me · Where this comes from · Mark done. On web they sit in the ⑩ row menu button.
- Non-colour encoding: the glyph shape carries the kind, the mark shape carries provenance, the leading bar carries highlight, and the words carry done.
- Contrast: text at least 4.5:1; mark at least 3:1 (text.secondary on base, 4.83:1).

COPY RULES (panel)
- For deadlines, the title names the action: "Tell your landlord in writing by Mon 1 Mar 2027".
- Received-by deadlines say "must arrive by".
- Dates are spelled out with the weekday ("Mon 26 Oct"), never 10/26/2026.
- Beyond tomorrow, the relative count comes first: "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". Conditional rules (V4) are exempt from the relative count.
- Source captions carry a scope word: "Clark County Treasurer · county-wide".
- Pickup titles use exactly "Recycling and garbage" or "Garbage only".
- Holiday moves read "moved to Fri 27 Nov", never "delayed" or "cancelled".
- "I did this" reads "You marked this done" and stays Only you.

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences, except that web adds the ⑩ row menu button (R12).

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of red text or an overdue chip on an annual date that has passed, draw the next occurrence with its "Every year" caption. Annual dates never inherit overdue red.
- Instead of one generic calendar icon for every row, draw the specific KindGlyph. The glyph is what tells kinds apart without colour.
- Instead of a greyed placeholder row for a date the viewer may not see, draw nothing. A ghost row leaks that something exists.
- Instead of a numeric date like 10/26/2026, draw "Mon 26 Oct". The weekday is what people plan by.

IN CONTEXT (04): three crops, each with the legend line and the ScopeChip (R13).
1. f5-today-calendar-strip · ios, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; a card (radius lg) holding a 14-cell strip drawn only as a plain outline (the strip is specified on another board), above rows V1a, V3a and V6; a foot row "+ Add a date"; the legend line. Annotate the strip: "strip cells are not targets; the rows below are".
2. x-place-file · web-1440, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; section overline "DATES"; rows V3b, V4 and V5, each with its ⑩ row menu button; the legend line.
3. f3-household-calendar · android, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; an agenda with the day header "Tue 20 Oct" and row V1a in S2a; the legend line.

NOTES (add a "DateRow" section to 00c · Notes)
- Invented strings: "city schedule" · "Washington Secretary of State · statewide" · "Reminder Sat 30 Jan 2027" as a caption · the "Reminder:" title prefix · "Every year" · "Every month" · "Does not repeat".
- Fixture deltas: V1a and V1b show Home A as of TODAY, before Maya confirmed Tuesday (hollow) · V5x: the warranty date was entered as approximate ("about Dec 2026") instead of Sat 12 Dec 2026 · V6: HOA dues appears both as a household bill (BillRow) and as a self-added monthly date.
- Contract conflicts: "Statewide — WA" drawn in ScopeChip geometry as a coverage chip, instead of one of ScopeChip's two exact strings · highlighted drawn as a wash plus a leading bar, instead of contract "wash + outline", so it never looks like focus.
- Assumptions: V2 has a hollow mark on an official city holiday move, because Place B's schedule is unconfirmed · V5x carries the identity.home rule and "Does not repeat", like every other self-entered row.

ARTBOARDS (exact names)
- 00c · DateRow · 01-anatomy · light
- 00c · DateRow · 02-grid · light
- 00c · DateRow · 03-ax5-200-greyscale · light
- 00c · DateRow · 04-in-context · light
- 00c · DateRow · 05-grid · dark
- 00c · Notes (created in this component's Turn 2)

BATCH PLAN
- Turn 1 (now): 00c · DateRow · 01-anatomy · light and 00c · DateRow · 02-grid · light. Stop and wait for "continue".
- Turn 2 (after "continue"): 03-ax5-200-greyscale · light, 04-in-context · light and 05-grid · dark. Then create 00c · Notes with its board section (R14) and the DateRow section above. Stop and wait for the next component message.

DONE WHEN
- The five DateRow artboards exist, named exactly, each with its visible label, and 00c · Notes exists as the last artboard.
- 01 shows callouts ①–⑩ with size and token, the dashed row target, and the five panels with the text above.
- 02 and 05 hold exactly the 26 listed cells, with every row and column labelled "<code> · <key>" plus its printed key, and every cell captioned "DateRow · <variant key> · <state key>".
- V3a SF sits beside V3a S2a and S2b, and bar, ring and wash are each distinct. S2a shows bar and ring without touching.
- The done tick is a bare stroke check; the YOU ADDED mark is a disc with a knocked-out tick; every mark is at least 12pt with a 1.5px ring stroke.
- Every row has its own KindGlyph, and no row is red or carries an overdue chip.
- The S4 cell shows no ghost row and carries its annotation arrow; the V3a S3 cell carries "done stays Only you".
- 03 shows V3a and V6 in both columns, following the AX5 rules above, and the greyscale grid with its five captions.
- 04 shows the three crops, each with the legend line and ScopeChip; the web crop shows the row menu button on every row.
- 05 uses D1, D4 and D7 (with its 5.42:1 caption) and carries the Increase Contrast caption.
- Every string on the board is in this message or listed on Notes.

name: FactRow
job: One row per fact in the place file and settings: known, missing, or not available at this tier.
text:
Component 00c-02: FactRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: FactRow. This message is the complete FactRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). One row per fact in the place file and in settings. The fact is known, missing, or not available at this tier.

USED IN (panel): x-place-file · f6-home-basics-rows · f1-today-tab · f3-household-block · f9-verification-promise-copy · f4-notification-settings.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw three specimens at 2x, stacked: V1a (known, chevron), V2a (missing, "Add") and the ⑦ disclosure row.
① Row: minimum height 56pt, padding 16pt horizontal, on surface.base, content vertically centred.
② Label: bodySmall 14/20, text.secondary, above the value.
③ Value: body 16/24, text.primary.
④ ProvenanceMark S (16pt) after the value, with an 8pt (spacing.2) gap. It is not a target.
⑤ Trailing element: either a chevron (16pt, text.secondary) or a text action in bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), e.g. "Add".

- SF · focused.
- S2 · loading: a WarmingSkeleton exactly 56pt high, with a 144pt-wide label bar above a 253pt-wide value bar (at 361pt content width) and no text.
- S3 · offline. The value stays readable. A text action that needs the network is disabled per R8 (text.secondary, focusable) with the reason caption "You're offline. You can add this when you're back." under it. A chevron row (V1a, V7) stays readable and opens cached content, so it looks like S1. On V6, "Open Settings" stays enabled, because it opens the system settings and needs no connection: draw V6 unchanged with the annotation "Open Settings works offline".

- The mark and the chevron, or "Add", drop below the value.

- missing = ask sentence + "Add", not colour.

- done = stroke check + "Pickup day set".

- Targets follow ⑧. A row with a chevron is one target (44pt / 48dp / 44px; 56pt visual). A text action is a separate button, and its row is not a target.

- "Not set" is in text.secondary.

INSTEAD OF (panel)

name: FirstWeekRow
job: The single Today pointer to the next first-week ask, from a bounded set that is already started.
text:
Component 00c-03: FirstWeekRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: FirstWeekRow. This message is the complete FirstWeekRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). The single pointer on Today to the next first-week ask. It comes from a bounded set of steps that the person has already started.

USED IN (panel): f1-today-tab · x-place-file · f4-briefing-optin-card. (f4-briefing-optin-card is not cropped on 04: it only hosts the row, so it adds nothing beyond the f1-today-tab crop.)

FIXTURE DELTA (applies to every FirstWeekRow specimen). The specimens show Place B (Jordan Lee) on Tue 13 Oct 2026, 3 days after the Sat 10 Oct save. The 7-day activation window runs Sun 11 Oct through Sat 17 Oct and closes after Sat 17 Oct. The hidden variant (V2) shows Mon 19 Oct, when the window has closed. Place B's pickup day is known (Thursday, City of Camas); its pickup frequency is Not set.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1a at 2x.
① One row, 48pt high at default sizes: padding 16pt horizontal and 12pt vertical (12 + 24 + 12 = 48), on surface.base. At default sizes the step text is one line; if it wraps, the row grows and the dismiss button stays top-aligned.
② Text in bodyMedium 16/24, text.primary: "Next: set your pickup day →". The arrow is part of the link. The whole row except the dismiss button is the link target: draw its dashed target.
③ Trailing dismiss button: a 16pt close glyph in text.secondary inside a 44pt / 48dp target, with 8dp between it and the link target. Draw its dashed target too.
④ Callout listing the bounded set: "Save (already done) · Pickup day · Reminder or widget · One date or person".
⑤ Callout: "Only steps reachable at the current tier are counted. Verify, profile and photo are never steps."
⑥ Callout: "Shown for 7 days (the activation window)."
⑦ Web menu callout: "the visible dismiss button is the only extra action; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1a · next-pickup: "Next: set your pickup day →". For Place B this step means confirming the known day and setting the frequency.
- V1b · next-widget: "Next: put today on your home screen →" (invented). It may wrap at 361pt; if it does, apply the ① rule.
- V2 · hidden (set complete, dismissed, or window closed): draw an outline of the Place B Today section stack (ScopeChip, pickup section, air section) with no FirstWeekRow and no gap where it would be, plus the annotation "hidden: set complete, dismissed, or 7 days passed".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SFl, SFd, S2)
- S1 · default.
- SFl · focused-link: the focus ring around the link target only.
- SFd · focused-dismiss: the focus ring around the dismiss button only.
- S2 · dismissed (stored on the server): the row collapses in place to the InlineUndo "Hidden from Today · Undo" (invented). Undo has a 44pt target and stays until the user leaves Today. There is no countdown.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 7 cells)
- S1: V1a, V1b and V2 (V2 is one cell, in the S1 column).
- SFl and SFd: V1a, side by side, each ringing only its own target (2 cells).
- S2: V1a and V1b (2 cells).

DARK (05)
- The row sits on dark surface.base. Text is dark text.primary, the close glyph dark text.secondary, and "Undo" dark border.focus.
- No substitutes beyond the token swap are needed. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1a in S1 and V1a in S2, in both columns.
- The text wraps to two or more lines, and the arrow stays at the end of the text.
- The dismiss button stays top-aligned at the trailing edge and keeps its target (overrides R9: a dismiss control stays top-trailing).
- The row grows beyond 48pt.
- In S2, "Undo" wraps below "Hidden from Today" and keeps its 44pt / 48dp target.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- next step = the words; no colour is used.
- dismissed = "Hidden from Today · Undo".
- hidden = absence, carried by the annotation.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The row is one link: "Next: set your pickup day. Link."
- Dismiss is a separate button, "Dismiss next step" (invented), and is also offered as a custom action on the link.
- Undo is announced with role=status and is focusable.
- Targets: the link row is 48pt; the dismiss button is 44pt / 48dp / 44px, 8dp from the link.

COPY RULES (panel)
- Name only the next step, in sentence case, verb first. Never show a count or fraction of steps.
- The row shows for 7 days, matching the activation window.
- Step strings come from the set: "set your pickup day", "put today on your home screen" (invented), "add one date that matters" (invented).

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of "3 of 6" or any denominator, draw "Next: <step> →". Naming the next step moves people without pressure.
- Instead of counting verify, profile or photo, draw only the four set steps reachable at the viewer's tier. A step you cannot do is not a step.
- Instead of a checklist card, draw this single 48pt row. The full list lives in the place file.

IN CONTEXT (04): two crops (R13).
1. f1-today-tab · ios, Place B: ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you"; then V1a; then the pickup section outline, showing "Pickup day" with a hollow mark, and the legend line.
2. x-place-file · web-390, Place B: ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you"; the same step drawn as two published FactRow variants: V1c (label "Pickup day" · value "Thursday · City of Camas" · hollow mark · chevron), then V2b (label "Pickup frequency" · value "Not set" in text.secondary · action "Add"). Annotation: "same set, same storage". Add the legend line (R13). No row menu button.

NOTES (add a "FirstWeekRow" section to 00c · Notes)
- Invented strings: every string marked (invented) above.
- Fixture deltas: specimens on Tue 13 Oct 2026, 3 days after the Sat 10 Oct save; the 7-day window runs Sun 11 Oct through Sat 17 Oct · V2 on Mon 19 Oct, after the window closed · the pickup step for Place B covers both confirming the known day (FactRow V1c) and setting the frequency (FactRow V2b) · the set step "One date or person" is drawn as "add one date that matters" because the person half is locked for Place B at T1 ("Claim this address first") and is not counted.
- Contract conflicts: the contract lists a "fraction" variant (a done-count in front of the next step); not drawn, because house invariant 6 and the research brief rejected it. The contract's "no-fraction" variant is drawn as V1a and V1b · link target drawn as the whole row minus the dismiss button (contract: whole-row link), so dismiss can have its own target.
- Assumptions: at AX5 / 200% the dismiss button stays top-trailing, overriding R9 (trailing elements move below the text) because a dismiss control belongs at the top-trailing corner.
- Not cropped: f4-briefing-optin-card, because it only hosts the row.

ARTBOARDS (exact names)
- 00c · FirstWeekRow · 01-anatomy · light
- 00c · FirstWeekRow · 02-grid · light
- 00c · FirstWeekRow · 03-ax5-200-greyscale · light
- 00c · FirstWeekRow · 04-in-context · light
- 00c · FirstWeekRow · 05-grid · dark
- 00c · Notes (update)

BATCH PLAN
- Turn 1 (now): 01-anatomy · light and 02-grid · light. Stop and wait for "continue".
- Turn 2 (after "continue"): 03, 04 and 05 as named above. Then add the FirstWeekRow section to 00c · Notes and update its board section. Stop and wait for the next component message.

DONE WHEN
- The five FirstWeekRow artboards exist, named exactly, each with its visible label.
- 01 shows callouts ①–⑦, both dashed targets and the five panels.
- 02 and 05 hold exactly the 7 listed cells, each captioned "FirstWeekRow · <variant key> · <state key>".
- No fraction, step count or percentage is drawn on any specimen, callout, annotation or crop (INSTEAD OF names "3 of 6" only as the pattern to avoid).
- If V1b wraps, its row grows and its dismiss button is top-aligned.
- Both 04 crops show Place B's pickup day as known ("Thursday · City of Camas", hollow mark), each with the legend line; the only missing Place B pickup item is "Pickup frequency · Not set · Add".
- Every string is in this message or listed on Notes.

name: BillRow
job: A household bill with payer attribution, so two people don't pay the same bill.
text:
Component 00c-04: BillRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: BillRow. This message is the complete BillRow specification.

PURPOSE (top of 01). A household bill with payer attribution, so two people don't pay the same bill.

USED IN (panel): f3-bills-list · f3-member-home-dashboard · f3-bill-detail-web · f10-mail-piece-photo.

FIXTURE ROWS (Home A, viewer Maya unless stated; strings given only here)
- Clark Public Utilities · Upcoming · $142.18 · "Due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct".
- City of Vancouver water · Upcoming · $84.00 · "Due in 9 days · Wed 28 Oct".
- HOA dues · Upcoming · $285.00 · "Due in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov".
- Comcast · Upcoming · $79.99 · "Due in 14 days · Mon 2 Nov".
- Paid (invented): Comcast · Paid · $79.99 · "Due Fri 2 Oct" · "Paid by Sam · Thu 1 Oct".
- Overdue (invented): Waste Connections · Overdue (error glyph in chip) · $38.75 · "Due Thu 15 Oct".
- Due today (invented; shown on Fri 23 Oct): Clark Public Utilities · Due today · $142.18 · line 2 left "Due today". The repetition is intended: the chip is the status and line 2 keeps the due-date column filled. Today stands alone; the date is only spoken.
- Header ⑧: Maya sees "4 upcoming · $591.17 through Mon 2 Nov · You and Sam can see these"; Sam sees "… · You and Maya can see these".

ANATOMY (01, at 2x): Maya's header over the Clark upcoming and paid Comcast rows.
① Row: 12 + 24 + 20 + 12 = 68pt at default sizes (min 68pt), padding 12pt vertical, 16pt horizontal, surface.base. The whole row opens bill detail (dashed target).
② Line 1 left: provider, bodyMedium 16/24 text.primary. The ONLY field that truncates (default sizes only).
③ Line 1: one StatusChip after the provider.
④ Line 1 right: amount, bodyMedium tabular, one right-aligned column.
⑤ Line 2 left: due date, bodySmall 14/20 text.secondary.
⑥ Line 2 right: attribution, bodySmall text.secondary, never truncated.
⑦ Overflow (dashed target): 20pt ellipsis, 44pt / 48dp, 8dp from the row target: Mark paid · I paid this · Paid a different amount · Skip this month.
⑧ Header, bodySmall text.strong. Finance access differs, so it names people.
⑨ Not on 01; it sits on the V1 · S3 cell: "the household notification is held until the user leaves the screen without undoing".
⑩ Web menu: "the ⑦ overflow is the web row menu button; no second menu".

VARIANTS (rows; "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · manage (Maya): the Clark upcoming row.
- V2a · member-overflow (Sam): same row; overflow holds "I paid this" only.
- V2b · member-no-overflow (Sam): same row, no overflow; "Maya can mark this paid" (invented) replaces line 2 right. Its S4 cell has no bill row; it keeps the R7 label and caption, with a separate annotation beside the cell: "viewer: Sam, before Maya shared bills".
- V3 · only-me: same row, lines 1–2 unchanged. Line 3, leading-aligned: 12pt person glyph + "Only you will see this." in bodySmall text.secondary.
- V4 · former-member (later state, after Sam left): the paid Comcast row with "Paid by Sam (no longer here) · Thu 1 Oct".
- C1 · chip-upcoming, C2 · chip-due-today, C3 · chip-overdue (hue on glyph only), C4 · chip-paid: the Clark upcoming, due-today, overdue and paid fixtures.

STATES (columns: S1, S2a, SF, S2b, S3, S4, S5)
- S1 · default. V1 · S1 draws its menu open with all four items.
- S2a · highlighted-arrival (R8; dark D1), focus moved here: infoBg wash, 4pt leading bar, ring 2px outside.
- SF · focused: the R8 ring on the whole row. It sits between S2a and S2b so the ring can be compared with both.
- S2b · highlighted-decayed: wash and bar gone; ring remains.
- S3 · marked-paid: InlineUndo "Clark Public Utilities marked paid · Undo" (invented), role=status. Beside it, the row after the user left: line 1 "Clark Public Utilities · Upcoming · $142.18"; line 2 left "Next due in 35 days · Mon 23 Nov" (invented).
- S4 · permission-denied (Sam before Maya shared bills): header is just "Bills"; the body is one locked row: 16pt text.secondary lock glyph, "Maya can give you access to bills" (invented), bodySmall text.secondary, no link, min 44pt, border.subtle hairline above.
- S5 · offline: FreshnessLine "You're offline · as of 5:52 PM" (invented) above the rows; rows still open cached detail. V1 · S5 draws the menu open, all four items disabled, with one shared reason under the item group: "You're offline. You can mark bills paid when you're back." (invented). (Overrides R8 for menus: one shared reason under the group, not one per item.)

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 15): V1: S1, S2a, SF, S2b, S3, S5 · V2a: S1 · V2b: S1, S4 · V3: S1 · V4: S1 · C1–C4: S1.

DARK (05): D1 highlight; D4 chip fills; D7 overdue glyph, caption "error on dark raised 3.03:1"; D8 keyline on open menus, caption "5.71:1"; Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): C1 and C4 in both columns. Provider wraps (no truncation); chip drops below it, then amount; due date and attribution stack, attribution last; overflow stays top-trailing (overrides R9: an overflow control stays top-trailing).

GREYSCALE (03): status = chip words · overdue = glyph + "Overdue" · payer = "Paid by Sam" · highlighted = leading bar · marked paid = "marked paid · Undo".

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Merged label: "Clark Public Utilities, 142 dollars 18 cents, due Friday 23 October, upcoming." Due today: "…, due today, Friday 23 October." Paid: "Comcast, 79 dollars 99 cents, paid by Sam, Thursday 1 October."
- S3 is a live region ("Clark Public Utilities marked paid. Undo."); Undo is focusable.
- Overflow items are also custom actions; offline-disabled ones keep the shared reason as a hint.

COPY RULES (panel): notifications say "marked paid", not "paid" · "Paid by <first name> · <weekday day month>" · future dates beyond tomorrow add the relative count; past dates show the date only ("Due Thu 15 Oct", "Paid by Sam · Thu 1 Oct") · former member "Sam (no longer here)" · the header names who can see · never monitoring language ("still hasn't paid").

PLATFORMS (panel; added by this board): the overflow is native: iOS pull-down menu, Android M3 DropdownMenu, web menu button with keyboard support.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- One-tap "Mark paid" on the row or dashboard → in the overflow; a mis-tap must not notify the household.
- Avatar without a name → "Paid by Sam"; the name is the point.
- Budget meter → the header total.
- Truncated attribution → truncate the provider.

IN CONTEXT (04; R13)
1. f3-bills-list · ios, Maya: her header, the four upcoming rows.
2. f3-member-home-dashboard · android, Sam: a Bills card (radius lg), his header, two V2b rows (Clark, City of Vancouver water).
3. f3-bill-detail-web · web-1440: V1 in S2a as the header summary, overflow as the web menu.
Platform strip: the V1 menu in the three PLATFORMS forms; web shows keyboard focus on item one.

NOTES (add a "BillRow" section to 00c · Notes)
- Invented strings: all marked (invented) above.
- Fixture deltas: C2 on Fri 23 Oct · S4 is Sam before sharing · V4 shows a later state after Sam left · HOA dues is also a self-added monthly date (DateRow V6).
- Contract conflicts: header names people, not "… Everyone at Maple St can see these" (ScopeChip doNot) · V3 uses ScopeChip's sentence · native menus added here · V2a drawn per contract, but the brief did not adopt member-recorded payments (finance.view decision), so crops use V2b.
- Board-rule overrides: a menu gets one shared offline reason under its item group (overrides R8's per-action caption) · at AX5 / 200% the overflow stays top-trailing (overrides R9).
- Copy decisions: C2 repeats "Due today" in the chip and on line 2 on purpose · past dates show the date only, with no relative count.

ARTBOARDS (exact names)

- 00c · BillRow · 02-grid · light
- 00c · BillRow · 03-ax5-200-greyscale · light
- 00c · BillRow · 04-in-context · light
- 00c · BillRow · 05-grid · dark

BATCH PLAN
- Turn 1 (now): 01-anatomy · light and 02-grid · light. Stop and wait for "continue".
- Turn 2 (after "continue"): 03, 04 and 05 as named above, then add the BillRow section to 00c · Notes and update its board section. Stop and wait for the next component message.

DONE WHEN

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw a MEMBERS group at 2x: the ⑥ heading, the V3 row and the ⑦ disclosure. Beside it, draw V1 at 2x to show ⑧.
① Row: 56pt minimum, padding 16pt horizontal and 8pt vertical (8 + 40 + 8 = 56; text block 24 + 16 = 40), on surface.base. V1, with the ⑧ caption, grows to 72pt. The row is one element: draw its dashed target.
② A 40pt initials avatar: a surface.sunken circle (dark: D4) with initials in label 13/18 text.strong. Neutral, with no identity hue.
③ Name: body 16/24, text.primary.
④ Caption: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "joined Tue 22 Sep 2026" (invented) or "access until Sun 1 Nov 2026" (invented).
⑤ Overflow button (44pt / 48dp) holding Change role · Confirm lives here · Remove. On the viewer's own row, the only item is "Leave Larkspur Loop". Draw its dashed target.
⑥ Group heading in overline 11/16, text.secondary: OWNER · ADMINS · MEMBERS · GUESTS.
⑦ Group disclosure: a 44pt / 48dp row under its heading, with a chevron. MEMBERS "What can members do?", ADMINS "What can admins do?" (invented), GUESTS "What can guests do?" (invented). OWNER has no disclosure.
⑧ Optional second caption naming method and date: "Address confirmed by postcard · Thu 15 Oct 2026" (date invented), caption text.secondary, no badge shape. Only on the viewer's own row, so members never look different from one another.
⑨ Web menu callout: "the ⑤ overflow is the web row menu button; no second menu".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>"). Home A, viewer Maya. Role variants reuse Sam Ortega, so no new people are invented. Draw V1–V5 with their group heading above the row inside the cell.
- V1 · owner: OWNER · "Maya Chen (you)" ("(you)" invented) · "joined Mon 21 Sep 2026" (invented) · ⑧ · overflow (closed). This is the owner's own row. The owner as seen by another member (e.g. Sam on f3-member-home-dashboard) is the V2 layout under an OWNER heading: "Maya Chen", join caption, no ⑧, and no overflow.
- V2 · admin: ADMINS · "Sam Ortega" · "joined Tue 22 Sep 2026" · overflow.
- V3 · member: MEMBERS · the same content as V2.
- V4 · guest: GUESTS · "Sam Ortega" · "access until Sun 1 Nov 2026" · overflow.
- V5 · you: V1's content (OWNER heading, "Maya Chen (you)", join caption, ⑧) with the overflow open, showing only "Leave Larkspur Loop".
- V6a · roster-line: a 44pt / 48dp row "Maya and Sam live here · View". "View" is a text button in primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus).
- V6b · roster-count (Priya's view before she accepts; count only): a 44pt / 48dp row "Maya Chen and 1 other live here", no action.
- V7 · empty (fixture delta: Home A before Sam joined): a 44pt / 48dp row "Just you at Larkspur Loop · Invite someone". "Invite someone" is a text button in primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus).

- S1 · default.
- SF · focused: the ring on the whole row.
- S2 · loading: a WarmingSkeleton in the row's final geometry, no text, announced once as "Loading". Per row type:
  - V3: 56pt high, a 40pt circle and two bars.
  - V6a: 44pt / 48dp high, one text bar and one short trailing bar, no circle.
- S3 · offline: the overflow opens and its items are disabled. A menu gets one shared reason under its item group (overrides R8 for menus). The V3 menu (Change role · Confirm lives here · Remove) carries "You're offline. You can manage people when you're back." (invented). On V5, "Leave Larkspur Loop" carries "You're offline. You can leave when you're back." (invented).

text:
Component 00c-06: InviteRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: InviteRow. This message is the complete InviteRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). A pending invitation or invite link, with its expiry and a one-tap fix.
