ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x under its "PENDING" overline.
① Row: minimum 56pt, in a "PENDING" group (overline 11/16 text.secondary) that only managers see. Quieter than people rows: no avatar on any variant.
② Leading mail glyph, 16pt, text.secondary.
③ Line 1, the recipient: bodySmall 14/20 text.primary, "priya@example.com" or a username such as "@priya".
④ Line 2, the caption: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "Member · sent Mon 12 Oct · Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". It runs the full text width under ⑤ and ⑥ and wraps at a middot when it has to.
⑤ "Resend" text button, bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), trailing and aligned to line 1, with a 44pt target. Draw its dashed target.
⑥ Overflow button (44pt / 48dp) holding Cancel · Extend, trailing, 8dp after Resend. Draw its dashed target.
⑦ Web menu callout: "the ⑥ overflow is the web row menu button; rows without an overflow use their visible buttons; no second menu".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · pending-email: as in the anatomy.
- V1u · pending-username: V1 with the recipient "@priya".
- V2 · expiring (fixture delta: shown on Sun 25 Oct): V1 with the caption "Member · sent Mon 12 Oct · Expires tomorrow · Mon 26 Oct". The expiry is words in text.secondary, not tinted.
- V3 · needs-reissue: a 16pt warning glyph replaces the mail glyph (hue on the glyph only; dark: D7). Line 1: the recipient, with ⑥ trailing. Line 2: "Needs reissue — your household's invite rules changed" in bodySmall text.primary, wrapping within the text width. Line 3: the caption "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct" leading, and the "Reissue" text button trailing with a 44pt target.
- V4 · declined (fixture delta: Priya declined): the 16pt mail glyph; line 1 the recipient; line 2 a StatusChip "Declined · Thu 15 Oct". ⑥ holds only "Remove". No Resend.
- V5 · link-active: a 16pt link glyph; line 1 "Invite link" in bodySmall text.primary; line 2 the caption "Works once · Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". "Turn off link" is a trailing text button with a 44pt target. No overflow.
- V6 · awaiting-approval (Priya joined by link, so the link is used and no expiry applies): the 16pt mail glyph; line 1 "priya@example.com"; line 2 the caption "Waiting for your OK". "Approve" and "Remove" are equal-weight text buttons, trailing, 8dp apart, each with its own 44pt target. No overflow.

- S1 · default.
- SF · focused: the ring on the Resend button only.
- S2 · sending: "Resend" becomes "Sending…" and "Reissue" becomes "Reissuing…", each with a 12pt spinner before it (dark: D6; static text under Reduce Motion). Not re-tappable.
  - Follow-on (V1 only): inside the V1·S2 cell, under the sending row, draw a second stacked frame sub-labelled "then": the caption gains " · Sent" at the end and the button returns to "Resend". "Sent" is a role=status region whose accessible text is "Invitation resent". It stays one cell.

The ⑥ overflow stays enabled and opens; Cancel and Extend inside it are disabled with "You're offline. You can change this invite when you're back." On V4, Remove inside it uses the remove reason.

- SF: V1 (1).
- S2: V1 with its "then" frame, and V3 (2). V4 in S2: "n/a — declined invites cannot be resent" (1).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V6 in both columns. The recipient wraps at the "@". Captions wrap at middots. Resend drops below the caption and keeps its target. The overflow stays top-trailing (an icon button, not a text action). Approve and Remove stack below the caption, each full width with its own target.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Pattern: "Invitation to priya@example.com, member, expires in 7 days, Monday 26 October. Resend. Button."
- A successful resend is announced as "Invitation resent" (the visible word is "Sent").
- Expiry is always in words. Targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px with 8dp gaps.

- Instead of a real email domain, draw @example.com.

text:
Component 00c-08: TextActionRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: TextActionRow. This message is the complete TextActionRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Tertiary actions that spread the product: share, compare and outbound links. They never outrank the primary action.

USED IN (panel): f8-native-share-compare · f8-compare-sheet · f8-seasonal-aha · f6-place-section-details · f8-compare-reveal.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x, and V2b at 2x below it.
① Two text buttons side by side: "Share this address" and "Compare with a friend". Each is bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), with a 44pt / 48dp / 44px target, 8dp apart, no fill and no border. Draw both dashed targets and the 8dp gap.
② Caption under the buttons: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "The card shows your city and your readings — never your address, and no name."
③ Outbound variant: a bordered row, 48pt minimum, radius md 8, padding 12pt vertical and 16pt horizontal, with a 1px text.secondary edge (4.83:1 on base; a border token would fail as the only edge). It holds the destination text in bodySmall text.primary and a trailing 16pt external-link glyph "↗" in text.secondary. The whole row is the target. The "↗" at the end of each variant string below is this glyph: draw it once, as a vector, not as a text character.
④ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · share-compare: ① plus ②.
- V2a · outbound-test-kits: "Free test kits · Washington Dept of Health ↗".
- V2b · outbound-votewa: "Check or update at VoteWA ↗".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, SF)
- S1 · idle.
- S2 · minting: on "Compare with a friend", a 12pt spinner (dark: D6) replaces the start of the label, which reads "Making a link…". Not re-tappable. Under Reduce Motion the spinner is removed and the words stay.
- S3 · copied: the caption "Link copied" (role=status) sits between the buttons and the ② caption, and stays until the user leaves the screen.
- S4 · cancelled: nothing changes. Draw the idle row again with the annotation "share sheet dismissed: neutral, no message".
- S5 · offline: "Compare with a friend" is disabled per R8, with the reason "You're offline. Compare needs a connection." "Share this address" stays enabled (the system share sheet works offline). Outbound rows are disabled: the destination text turns text.secondary (glyph unchanged), the edge stays, and "You're offline. You can open this when you're back." sits under the row.
- SF · focused: the ring 2px outside the V2b row.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 16 cells)
- V1: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 (5).
- V2a and V2b: S1 and S5 (4).
- V2a and V2b in S2, S3 and S4: "n/a — outbound links open the browser" (6).
- V2b: SF (1).

DARK (05): rows on dark surface.base. Buttons use dark border.focus. The outbound edge is a 1px dark text.secondary keyline (6.96:1 on dark base). Spinners use D6. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V2b in both columns. The two buttons stack, each full width with its own target. The caption wraps. The outbound row wraps its destination text; the glyph stays trailing, top-aligned.

GREYSCALE (03 captions): actions = verbs and position, not colour · outbound = text.secondary edge + destination name + ↗ glyph · minting = "Making a link…" words · copied = "Link copied" words · offline = reason captions.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Links name their destination: "Check or update at VoteWA, opens in browser".
- "Link copied" is a status message.
- Targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px, with 8dp between the two buttons.
- The minting button is announced as "Making a link" and cannot be re-activated.
- Disabled offline controls stay in the tree with their reason as a hint.

COPY RULES (panel)
- The V1 buttons start with a verb. Outbound rows name the destination as the contract gives it.
- The caption states what the card reveals.
- Use "Compare with a friend", never "challenge" or "vs".
- Offline reasons open with "You're offline".

PLATFORMS (panel)
- Only the system share sheet is used. iOS supplies LPLinkMetadata; Android supplies EXTRA_TITLE to the system chooser; web uses the browser's share, falling back to copying the link (S3).
- System UI is never redrawn by us: in 04 it is a surface.sunken frame with a 1px text.secondary keyline, labelled "system UI" in caption text.secondary.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of placing these actions inside the sticky WallBar, draw them on the page surface under the content card. The wall's single primary action must stay single.
- Instead of an app-drawn Android chooser, draw the system chooser frame.
- Instead of filled or bordered buttons for share and compare, draw text buttons, so they never outrank the primary.

text:
Component 00c-09: LockedActionRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: LockedActionRow. This message is the complete LockedActionRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Replaces or accompanies an unavailable control. It states the reason and the path forward.

USED IN (panel): f3b-locked-action-row · f3-members-roster · f3-member-home-dashboard · f3b-invitation-decision · f3-bills-list · f3-bill-detail-web · f3-household-calendar · f10-bill-provenance · f10-extraction-confirm · x-place-file · x-date-sheet · f6-home-basics-rows · f9-block-founders-panel · f11-keeper-strip.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x: the disabled button with the row under it.
① One row, minimum 44pt, padding 12pt vertical and 16pt horizontal.
② Leading glyph, 16pt, text.secondary: a lock on every row except V4, which uses a clock.
③ Reason in bodySmall 14/20: text.strong on surface.sunken, or text.secondary on surface.base.
④ Trailing link "Verify address" in bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), with a 44pt target. Draw its dashed target.
⑤ A 1px border.subtle hairline above the row (decoration only).
⑥ The reason wraps to 2 lines before anything truncates.
⑦ When the row sits under a disabled button, tapping the disabled button opens the same reason. Draw a callout arrow from the button to the row.
⑧ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · under-cta: a disabled filled button "Message your neighbors", 44pt / 48dp / 44px high, radius md, full content width (per R8: surface.sunken fill, text.strong label, kept focusable; dark: D4), with the row directly below it on surface.base: "Address verification needed to message your neighbors · Verify address".
- V2 list row (group heading only, not a grid row): "Address verification needed to get a residency letter · Verify address", drawn as two rows:
  - V2s · list-row-sunken: on surface.sunken, reason in text.strong.
  - V2b · list-row-base: on surface.base, reason in text.secondary.
- V3 · card-header: a card (radius lg, shadow sm; dark: D8 edge) titled "Residency Pass", with the row inside the header on surface.base: "Address verification needed to show your Residency Pass · Verify address".
- V4 · pending (viewer Sam, whose postcard is still in transit; Maya's address is already confirmed): a 16pt clock glyph in text.secondary instead of the lock, then "We're checking your postcard code — expected in 3–10 days · Thu 22–Thu 29 Oct", with no link.
- V5 · server-refused, shown after a tap the server refused: "Address verification needed to get a residency letter. We checked again. · Verify address".
- V6 · names-who-can-act (viewer Sam, who can see bills but not add them): "Maya can add bills here", with no link.
- V7 · not-at-tier (Place B): the lock glyph, then "Claim this address first" in text.secondary, with no link and no button.
All rows sit on surface.base unless stated.

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2, S3; each ends with its 03 greyscale caption)
- S1 · locked. Greyscale: "locked = lock glyph + the words; nothing is coloured except the link, which reads through its position and its verb".
- SF · focused: the ring on the "Verify address" link only (R8). Greyscale: "focused = ring".
- S2 · pending: V4's form. Greyscale: "pending = clock glyph + 'We're checking' words".
- S3 · offline: the link is disabled per R8 (text.secondary, focusable). The row grows: the caption "You're offline. You can verify when you're back." sits under the reason text, at the leading edge, full width. On V1 the button stays as in S1; its reason is still the row itself, and the button gets no offline caption. Greyscale: "offline = the dimmed link + the offline caption under the reason".

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 17 cells)
- S1: V1, V2s, V2b, V3, V5, V6 and V7 (7 cells). V4 in S1: "n/a — pending is its own variant" (1 cell).
- SF: V2b (1 cell).
- S2: V4 (1 cell).
- S3: V1, V2b, V3 and V5 (4 cells). V4, V6 and V7 in S3: "n/a — this variant has no link to disable" (3 cells).

DARK (05)
- V2s uses D3 (dark raised, dark text.strong). The V1 disabled button uses D4. The V3 card uses D8: caption "keyline 5.71:1" beside it. Other rows sit on dark base with dark text.secondary reasons (6.96:1).
- The lock and clock glyphs use dark text.secondary. Links use dark border.focus.
- Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

- The reason wraps fully.
- "Verify address" drops to its own line below the reason, left-aligned, keeping its target.
- The glyph scales to 24pt and stays top-aligned.
- The V1 button grows in height and its label wraps.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The reason is at 4.5:1 or better (text.strong on sunken 9.37:1; text.secondary on base 4.83:1).
- The link names its destination: "Verify address, opens Verify this address".
- The disabled button is exposed with its reason as a hint: "Message your neighbors, dimmed. Address verification needed to message your neighbors."
- The offline link is exposed as dimmed, with its reason as a hint.
- Row and link targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px.

COPY RULES (panel)
- The pattern is "Address verification needed to <specific action>". Any extra context (V5) follows as a second sentence.
- Never write a generic "Verification required".
- When someone else can act, name them ("Maya can add bills here").
- Dates beyond tomorrow carry the relative count (V4).

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of red or amber colouring, draw the neutral lock glyph in text.secondary. Nothing is wrong; something is not yet available.
- Instead of text.muted for the reason or the disabled link, draw text.strong on sunken or text.secondary on base, because both must be read.
- Instead of a present but inert control with no explanation, draw the control with this row under it.
- Instead of an "Address verification needed…" reason for a saved-place user on a home-only feature, draw V7 "Claim this address first". Verification means nothing before a claim.

The 4 upcoming bills are Clark Public Utilities, City of Vancouver water, Comcast and HOA dues.

You can verify when you're back." · "Address verification needed to earn a Block Founder rank" · "4 upcoming · $591.17 through Mon 2 Nov · You and Maya can see these" · the other reasons, built from the contract pattern and the grant/limit string set.

We checked again." instead of a generic server-refusal notice, to keep the contract pattern.

text:
Component 00c-10: GrantLimitList. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: GrantLimitList. This message is the complete GrantLimitList specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Two scannable lists: what you get now (ticked) and what needs address verification (locked). One component serves invite, attestation and verify.

USED IN (panel): f3b-invitation-decision · f3-invite-composer · f3b-owner-attestation · f3b-verify-address-sheet · f9-verification-promise-copy · f3-members-roster.

EXTRA STAND-IN FOR THIS COMPONENT (label it "stand-in", per R11)
- ChoiceChip: pill, 32pt visual height inside a 44pt / 48dp target, label 13/18. Selected: primary.50 fill, primary.700 label and a leading check glyph (dark: D5). Unselected: a 1px text.secondary edge and a text.strong label. The focus ring is distinct from selection. At AX sizes the chips become radio rows. Platform notes: an iOS segmented control where native; M3 filter chips on Android.

STRING SET (exact; every variant draws from it)
- Grants: "Sees and edits the calendar" · "Sees bills and who paid" · "Sees who lives here".
- Limits: "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" · "Show your Residency Pass" · "Share what you pay in rent (Real Rent)" · "Earn a Block Founder rank".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw the specimen twice: the stacked iOS form of V1 at 2x, and the two-column web-1440 form of V1 beside or below it at 1x (never shrunk; R2).
① Grant list heading "What you get now": label 13/18 text.strong. The grant list always comes first.
② Grant rows, 44pt each: a 16pt bare stroke check in success hue (a stroke, not a disc, so it cannot be mistaken for the YOU ADDED mark; dark: D7), a 12pt gap, and the verb phrase in body 16/24 text.primary.
③ Limit list heading "What needs address verification": label 13/18 text.strong.
④ Limit rows, 44pt each: a 16pt lock glyph in text.secondary, a 12pt gap, and the verb phrase in body 16/24 text.primary.
⑤ Callout: "both lists use identical type and row height".
⑥ Callout: "two columns 24pt apart on web 1440; stacked on mobile (iOS, Android, web 390)".
⑦ Callout: "one shared string set; every variant draws from it".
⑧ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · invitation-decision: both headings, all 3 grants and all 5 limits. The grid cell draws the stacked iOS form.
- V2 · role-offered: under a 44pt disclosure row "Role offered: Member" (expanded), the heading "What you get now" and the 3 grants only.
- V3 · attestation (viewer Maya, the owner, confirming that Sam lives here): the heading "What Sam gets once you confirm", then 3 rows with stroke checks: "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" · "Show your Residency Pass". V3 uses the grant row style because these become Sam's grants once Maya confirms; the heading carries the condition.
- V4 · verify-unlock: the heading "What needs address verification", then "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" with lock glyphs, then a 44pt row "Show 3 more" with a chevron that expands the remaining three limits.
- V5 · role-caption-member: a ChoiceChip pair, "Member" (selected) and "Guest". Under them, a caption in caption 12/16 text.secondary: "Sees and edits the calendar · Sees bills and who paid · Sees who lives here". It has no visible heading and is exposed as a list with the accessible name "What members can do".
- V5g · role-caption-guest: the same chips with "Guest" selected. The caption reads "Sees and edits the calendar", exposed as a list named "What guests can do".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2)
- S1 · default.
- SF · focused: on V4, the ring on the "Show 3 more" row only. On V5, the focus ring on the unselected "Guest" chip, with "Member" still selected (fill and check). On V5g, the focus ring on the unselected "Member" chip, with "Guest" still selected. So V5·S1 sits beside V5·SF, and V5g·S1 beside V5g·SF, in the same row.
- S2 · accepted: the limit list gains the caption "Verify your address to unlock these", in caption text.secondary, directly under its heading.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 15 cells)
- S1: V1, V2, V3, V4, V5 and V5g (6 cells).
- SF: V4, V5 and V5g (3 cells).
- S2: V1 (1 cell). V2, V3, V4, V5 and V5g in S2: "n/a — accepted applies after an invitation is accepted" (5 cells).

DARK (05)
- Lists sit on dark surface.base. The success check keeps its hue (D7): caption "success on dark base 4.74:1" beside the first one. Lock glyphs use dark text.secondary.
- Selected chips use D5. Unselected chip edges use dark text.secondary (6.96:1).
- Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V5 in both columns.
- The two lists stack, grants first.
- Phrases wrap; glyphs stay top-aligned and scale to 24pt.
- In V5, the chips become radio rows, each with a 44pt / 48dp target, and the caption wraps under them.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- grant vs limit = stroke check vs lock (shape) + the headings.
- selected chip = its check glyph.
- focused = ring.
- accepted = the "Verify your address to unlock these" caption.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Each list has a heading, exposed as a heading. Where there is no visible heading (V5, V5g), the list has an accessible name.
- The check and lock glyphs are decorative; the heading carries the meaning.
- Rows are read as list items: "What you get now, list, 3 items. Sees and edits the calendar."
- "Show 3 more" is a 44pt / 48dp / 44px button, spoken "Show 3 more" (the spoken name matches the visible label).
- Chips are spoken with their selected state: "Member, selected".

COPY RULES (panel)
- Every row is a verb phrase.
- Use the string set exactly.
- Never write a bare product name.

PLATFORMS (panel): stacked on mobile (iOS, Android, web 390) and two columns on web 1440. The V5 chips follow the ChoiceChip platform notes (an iOS segmented control where native; M3 filter chips on Android).

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of a warning box around the limits, draw the plain lock rows. Limits are information, not danger.
- Instead of bare product names ("Real Rent", "Residency Pass"), draw verb phrases ("Share what you pay in rent (Real Rent)"). People decide on what they can do.
- Instead of text.muted on sunken for locked rows, draw body text.primary with a text.secondary lock, because these rows must be read.

name: Board setup
job: Board rules for every component on this board. Send first; draws nothing.
text:
Foundations board 00d: States, feedback and asks. BOARD SETUP.

Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is one Foundations board. This message sets the board rules and draws nothing. Eight component prompts follow, one per turn: 1 QuietDayReceipt, 2 WarmingSkeleton, 3 InlineUndo, 4 DestructiveConfirm, 5 LandingBannerSlot, 6 NotificationAsk, 7 PushCopy, 8 ReminderLeadControl. Each opens with "Component 00d-NN: <Name>. Follow the board rules from the setup message." and carries that component's complete specification.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
A NEW component specimen board with no screens. These components cover the moments when the product must be honest about time and consent: nothing is wrong, something is loading, something can or can't be taken back, something is waiting, and the product wants to interrupt now or on dates you chose. Each has a quiet default; none nags. Later, 59 surfaces are designed in separate projects with no memory of this one, using these components by exact name from the published Pantopus design system. So every size, token, string and state in a component prompt is literal: draw each component once, precisely, with every variant and state listed.

HOW THIS PROJECT RUNS
1. Each component prompt has an ARTBOARDS list and a BATCH PLAN of at most 6 artboards per turn. Draw batch 1 and stop; the founder types "continue" before each later batch. After a component's last batch, wait for the next component prompt.
2. Before every batch, re-read R1–R19 and the whole current component prompt. Don't carry details between components unless a prompt says so.
3. Component order replaces the house-style priority order: finish each component, dark twin included, before the next. A named attachment arrives with its component prompt.
4. Ask a question only if two readings would give materially different specimens. Otherwise decide, and record it on Notes (R19).

PUBLISH (a founder step)
The founder adds each accepted component to the Pantopus design system under its exact name, with each specimen under the name printed beneath it (R7). Notes F lists every name.
- Every drawn specimen except the review aids below is published in light. Every specimen on a dark artboard is published in dark; every variant × state cell has a dark twin there.
- Light-only frames (platform strips, large-text frames, web-1440 crops, anything a prompt marks light only) are published in light only and listed on Notes E. A later dark surface takes their geometry from the light frame and their colours from R9.
- Review aids, never published: greyscale copies, "Not applicable" cells, "Not this" thumbnails, IN CONTEXT crops, and anything a prompt calls a review aid.

BOARD RULES

R1. Artboard names. "00d · <Component> · <NN-what> · <light|dark>", exactly as the ARTBOARDS list gives it. This replaces the house-style name format on this board, because one artboard can hold several platforms; the platform goes in each specimen name (R7). The Notes artboard is "00d · Notes", with no suffix. Print the name above the frame in label 13/18/600 text.strong.

R2. Artboard format. 1600px wide, as tall as needed, on surface.app (dark: dark app). Top left: the component name in h2 24/32/600 text.primary, then the artboard's subject in body text.secondary. Each 01 artboard also prints PURPOSE (body text.secondary) and "Used in:" (caption 12/16 text.secondary). Section headings are overline 11/16/600 caps text.strong.

R3. Platforms. Specimens are 1x at real width: iOS 393pt, Android 412dp, web-390 390px, web-1440 1440px (cropped to the relevant column, labelled "web-1440 crop"). Content width inside 16 margins: 361pt iOS, 380dp Android, 358px web-390.

R4. Units and type. pt, dp and px have equal values, except targets (R11). Spacing uses only the 4px scale. Type uses only the house-style scale, plus bodyMedium 16/24/500, bodySmallMedium 14/20/500 and the R17 large-text sizes. Other dimensions appear only where a prompt states them.

R5. Callouts. A numbered SQUARE marker (20×20, radius xs 4, surface.sunken fill, 1px text.strong outline, numeral in label 13/18/600 text.strong, centred), joined to its part by a 1px text.secondary leader. The key sits beside the specimen in caption 12/16 text.strong as number · size · token ("1 · 16pt tick glyph · text.secondary"). Markers are never circles (circles mean provenance). Dimension rulers are 1px text.secondary with 4px end ticks and the number in caption text.secondary.

R6. Grids. A "variants-by-states" artboard is a table: rows are variants, columns are states, in the order given. Headers are label 13/18/600 text.strong in sentence case ("V1 · Removed row"). Each cell holds one specimen unless the prompt lists more. Draw every cell. A combination that doesn't apply is a surface.sunken cell with "Not applicable: <the prompt's reason>" in caption text.strong, never blank.

R7. Keys and names. Each grid row and column prints "key: <key>" under its label in caption 12/16 text.secondary: lowercase, hyphenated, no "/", never a fixture string, name, amount or date. Use each prompt's keys exactly. Under every specimen, print its published name in caption 12/16 text.strong:
  <Component> / <variant-key> / <state-key> / <platform> / <light|dark>
for example "InlineUndo / removed-row / pending-undo / ios / light". Platform keys: ios, android, web-390, web-1440; large text: ios-ax5, ios-ax2, ios-ax-widget, android-200, android-150; "any" where a prompt calls a specimen platform-neutral. An anatomy specimen that repeats a grid cell carries that cell's name.

R8. Tokens. Label every colour by token name; hex appears only in R9 and R10. The house-style TOKEN USAGE rules apply: semantic hues on glyphs and borders only; text.muted for disabled labels only; readable secondary text is text.secondary on base, raised or app, and text.strong on sunken; borders are decoration, never the only edge of a control, segment or card.

R9. Dark mapping. Each dark artboard redraws its light twin:
  surface.base → #0F172A (dark base) · surface.raised → #1E293B (dark raised) · surface.app → #020617 (dark app) · surface.sunken → dark base (same colour, separates nothing)
  text.primary → #E5E7EB · text.strong → #F1F5F9 · text.secondary → #94A3B8 · text.muted → #64748B · text.inverse → #111827
  border.default → #1F2937 · border.strong → #374151 · border.focus and primary.700 → #38BDF8 · primary.50 (selected fill) → primary.900 #0c4a6e with #E5E7EB text
  semantic.error #DC2626 and semantic.warning #D97706 keep their hue.
  A dark card's edge is the fill step (raised on app), never a border, with no shadow. Dialogs and sheets are dark base. Print the container surface each prompt names in the dark frame's subject line.

R10. Contrast figures. The only figures on the board; prompts cite them as "(R10)". Print the figure beside the part; never compute a new one.
  Light on base: text.secondary 4.83:1 · primary.700 5.93:1 · text.inverse on primary.700 5.93:1 · semantic.error 4.83:1 · semantic.warning 3.19:1 · text.muted 2.54:1.
  Light on sunken: text.strong 9.37:1 · primary.700 5.39:1 (text.secondary is only 4.39:1 here).
  Light selection: primary.700 border on primary.50 5.57:1.
  Dark on raised: #94A3B8 5.71:1 · #38BDF8 6.83:1 · #D97706 4.59:1 · #DC2626 3.03:1 (glyphs only) · #64748B 3.07:1 · #1F2937 1.00:1 (never an edge).
  Dark on base: #94A3B8 6.96:1 · #38BDF8 8.33:1 · #F1F5F9 16.30:1 · #DC2626 3.70:1 · #64748B 3.75:1 · #111827 on #38BDF8 8.28:1.
  Dark selection: #E5E7EB on primary.900 7.64:1 · #38BDF8 on primary.900 4.42:1 (checks and borders only) · primary.900 on dark base 1.89:1 (a fill; the #38BDF8 border is the edge).

R11. Targets. Minimum hit areas: 44×44pt iOS, 48×48dp Android with 8dp gaps, 44×44px web, each drawn as a dashed 1px text.secondary rectangle labelled with its size. A glyph is never a target on its own.

R12. Focus and selection. Focus: a 2px border.focus ring with a 2px gap. Selection: primary.50 fill, 1.5px primary.700 border, 16pt primary.700 check, 600-weight text.primary label (dark per R9). They never look alike. A prompt may define one further treatment, in full.

R13. Glyphs and circles. Pantopus icon set only, 16pt unless stated, 1.5px stroke. Filled vs hollow circles mean provenance only, so no glyph, tick, bullet, marker or control is a plain disc or ring; the one exception is an avatar circle (MemberRow or its skeleton), which is never a mark. A tick is a bare check stroke. No control uses a radio circle, on any platform or text size: at large sizes, the brief's "radio rows" are list rows with the R12 selection check.

R14. Strings. Use the house-style FIXTURES exactly (TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific). Every string comes from the house style or the current prompt; any string you add goes on Notes D. Never draw a fallback where the published component exists.

R16. Disabled controls. A disabled control stays focusable and reads "<label>, unavailable, <reason>". Its label is text.muted, and the reason is also written nearby in readable text. No button is silently dead.

R17. Standard artboards.

  - "ax5-200-greyscale" (light), three required columns. (a) iOS AX5: caption 12 → 43pt, label 13 → 44pt, bodySmall 14 → about 46pt, body 16 → 51pt (Callout), h3 20 → 55pt. ACCESSIBILITY. COPY. PLATFORMS. INSTEAD OF: "Instead of X, draw Y — because Z", with a struck-through thumbnail of X labelled "Not this" beside one of Y.

R18. Motion. Transitions have a purpose and last 300ms or less; idle loops stop within 5 s. Wherever something moves, draw its Reduce Motion form (cross-fade or static). Nothing is gesture-only or hover-only.

R19. Notes. "00d · Notes" is shared by all eight components: create it in QuietDayReceipt's last batch, extend it in each later last batch, never drop entries. Body 16/24 text.primary on surface.base, overline headings, grouped by component:

Board chrome, once: "host illustrative, not a spec" · "Not this" · each "Not applicable: <reason>" · "key: <key>" · "Reads without colour: <cue>" · "web-1440 crop" · "Also consumed by:" · callout key texts. Row labels and component callouts go in each component's list.

Component 00d-02: WarmingSkeleton. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print on 01): Content-shaped placeholders that sit in their final slots during cold loads of 1–10 s, so nothing jumps when the data arrives.
Used in (print on 01): f1-today-tab, x-place-file, f5-today-calendar-strip, f1-your-places, f3-members-roster, f3-household-block, f3-member-home-dashboard, f8-compare-reveal, f8-compare-arrival-header, f9-privacy-mirror, f9-nearby-cells-map, f10-bill-trend, f11-keeper-strip, f7-widget-tap-landing

ARTBOARDS (5, then extend Notes)

00d · WarmingSkeleton · 02-variants-by-states · light

KEYS (R7)
Variants: V1 Section skeleton = section-skeleton · V2 Row skeleton = row-skeleton · V3 Instrument skeleton, four sub-specimens with their own keys: a = instrument-skeleton-strip · b = instrument-skeleton-year-band · c = instrument-skeleton-scale-strip · d = instrument-skeleton-bill-trend · V4 Panel skeleton = panel-skeleton.
States: S1 Shimmer = shimmer · S2 Static = static · S3 Replaced progressively = replaced-progressively.
Examples: "WarmingSkeleton / section-skeleton / shimmer / ios / light" · "WarmingSkeleton / instrument-skeleton-bill-trend / static / ios / dark".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy: V1 at S1 on iOS 393 with callouts, plus V3d at S1 beside it, named "WarmingSkeleton / instrument-skeleton-bill-trend / shimmer / ios / light")
1. Shapes are surface.sunken fills on surface.base cards, matching the final geometry: strip cells, track shapes, row bars, avatar circles. A count of facts is a number bar plus pill chip bars (the count is an integer plus chips, so there is no ring skeleton). Each shape takes the radius of the part it stands in for. Shapes are filled, never outlined, because an outline-only skeleton reads as an empty state. The avatar circle is placeholder geometry and carries no meaning (R13).
2. The skeleton reserves the exact final height. Beside it, draw a height ruler; beside a loaded version, a second ruler; caption both "same height". The loaded version is a review aid, not published: AqiBand (AQI 42 Good), PickupCard for HOME A (recycling and garbage, Tue 20 Oct) and the V3a loaded strip below, as R15 components or fallback boxes.
3. No text, no glyphs and no "checking…" inside a skeleton.
4. Shimmer: a soft band 30% of the shape's width, surface.base at 60% opacity, sweeping left to right. 1.2 s per pass; it stops after 4 passes (4.8 s) and holds static. This is an idle loop under the 5 s rule, not a 300ms transition (Notes 2.4). Draw the band mid-sweep with the callout "1.2 s per pass · stops after 4 passes".
5. Container: one accessibility element labelled "Loading" (callout).
6. Print on the board: "Skeleton shapes are decorative and have no contrast requirement."

VARIANTS (grid rows), all iOS 393. Strip geometry everywhere: 14 cells, each (361 − 52) / 14 ≈ 22.07pt wide, 4pt gaps, 361pt overall, radius xs.
V1 Section skeleton (f1-today-tab), three blocks in one column:

  - Pickup card: a card with a 42×42pt square (radius md) in the KindGlyph slot, two bars (200×20pt and 240×14pt, radius xs) and two 44pt button shapes of equal width (radius md).
  - Fourteen-day strip: the strip geometry, 40pt tall.
V2 Row skeleton (lists): three rows, each as tall as the final row it stands in for, drawn at 56pt (the MemberRow height) with the caption "height = the consuming row's final height". 16pt horizontal padding; a 40pt avatar circle and two bars (60% width × 14pt, 40% width × 12pt, 4pt apart), all vertically centred in the 56pt row.
V3 Instrument skeleton, four labelled sub-specimens stacked in the cell:
  a. 14-day strip: the strip geometry at 40pt tall (the R15 fallback height; if the published FourteenDayStrip is taller, match it and note it on Notes B).
  b. Year band: 361×120pt, 12 month columns × 4 lanes of 24pt, with lane-label bars.
  c. Scale strip: 4 rows of 48pt, each a 12pt filled track shape with a 72×14pt reading bar beside it.
  d. Bill trend: a 160×14pt summary bar above 12 columns, 16pt wide, 8pt gaps, radius xs, bottom-aligned, heights 40, 56, 48, 64, 52, 44, 60, 72, 56, 48, 64, 52pt.
V4 Panel skeleton (f9-nearby-cells-map): on a surface.base card, a 361×240pt surface.sunken panel, radius lg, with a 6×4 grid of 1px border.default lines (decoration), and a 120×14pt caption bar below it.

STATES (grid columns)
S1 Shimmer (default): the band mid-sweep.
S2 Static (Reduce Motion): the same shapes, no band. Loaded content replaces it with a 200 ms cross-fade.
S3 Replaced progressively: each replacement is a 200 ms cross-fade in place; the height ruler shows no change. Loaded content:
  - V1: the air band is AqiBand (R15): AQI 42 Good, AirNow, observed 7:00 AM. Pickup card and strip stay skeletons.
  - V2: row 1 is MemberRow (R15, owner variant) "Maya Chen" with caption "Owner". Rows 2–3 stay skeletons.
  - V3: a is FourteenDayStrip (R15) for HOME A from Mon 19 Oct 2026, with marks exactly as the published HOME A strip specimen: Tue 20 Oct recycling and garbage, hollow (city schedule, not confirmed) · Fri 23 Oct Clark Public Utilities bill, tick (you added) · Mon 26 Oct voter registration must arrive by, full-height state bar · Tue 27 Oct garbage only, hollow · Wed 28 Oct City of Vancouver water bill, tick · Sun 1 Nov HOA dues, tick, weekend cell. b, c, d stay skeletons, each with its own name.
  - V4: "Not applicable: the panel lands as one piece".

GRIDS
02 light: 4 rows × 3 columns, iOS; the V3 cells hold sub-specimens a–d, each named.
03 dark: the same grid per R9. Container: V1–V3 cards are dark raised on dark app, with shapes in #374151 (border.strong) and a shimmer band of dark raised at 60%. V4: the panel is dark raised on a dark base card, grid lines #374151, band of dark base at 60%. (Dark sunken equals dark base, so it would vanish.) Loaded content uses its own dark tokens.

04-ax5-200-greyscale-reduce-motion (light, per R17)
- (a) iOS AX5, V1 and V2 at S1: bar heights follow the R17 AX5 line heights of the text they stand in for, so V1 grows to its AX5 final height and the two pickup button shapes stack; V2 rows grow to their AX5 heights. Names use ios-ax5.

- Row "Reduce Motion": V1 and V3 static, captioned "no shimmer; replacements cross-fade". They repeat the S2 cells and are not published again.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Spoken "Loading", once, on the container (VoiceOver container label; Android contentDescription; web aria-busy="true" plus visually hidden "Loading"). Shapes are hidden from assistive tech.
- Skeletons carry no data, so need no non-colour encoding. They are not interactive; controls can't be tapped until content lands. Reduce Motion: no shimmer.

COPY. The only string is the spoken "Loading".

PLATFORMS
- All platforms skip skeletons for loads under about 1 s. Callout: "under 1 s: show nothing new; keep the old content".
- Warm screens (the widget path, f7-widget-tap-landing) never show a skeleton; they refresh in place with no hairline.
- Android uses its existing shimmer component with these shapes and ANATOMY 4; iOS and web match it.
- Fail-closed components never get a skeleton: the founding meter (f9-founding-meter-preview), the Earn row (f9-earn-removal) and LandingBannerSlot render nothing until their data is confirmed. Print this list here.

IN CONTEXT (05, per R17)

- f3-members-roster: V2 with three rows.
- f10-bill-trend: V3d inside the bill trend card.

- Instead of an empty card frame, draw filled shapes — because a frame-only skeleton looks empty.
- Instead of "Checking air…", draw text-free shapes — because a skeleton must not claim a check is running.

- Instead of a skeleton for the founding meter, the Earn row or LandingBannerSlot, draw nothing — because they fail closed.

NOTES (extend 00d · Notes)
A. 2.1 Dark shapes: dark sunken equals dark base, so shapes are dark raised on dark base and #374151 on dark raised cards.
   2.2 Shapes: the contract says "track outlines" and "ring outline". This board draws filled shapes (per the contract's "no frame-only skeletons") and drops the ring, because brief section 4 replaced the count ring with an integer plus chips. Confirm.
   2.3 Threshold: the contract says 1–10 s; brief P11 says about 2–10 s. This board follows the contract. Question: skeleton or nothing between 1 and 2 s?

Component 00d-04: DestructiveConfirm. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print on 01): The confirm for real losses. It names what goes and what stays.
Used in (print on 01): f10-mail-piece-photo, f10-mail-snap-privacy, f10-bill-provenance, f11-keeper-naming, f3-members-roster
ATTACH: none.

ARTBOARDS (6, then extend Notes)
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 01-anatomy · light
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 02-variants-by-states · light
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 03-platforms · light
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 04-variants-by-states · dark
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 05-ax5-200-greyscale · light
00d · DestructiveConfirm · 06-in-context-and-rules · light
00d · Notes (extend it)

KEYS (R7)
Variants: V1 One photo = one-photo · V2 All photos = all-photos · V3 Keeper = keeper · V4 Leave home sheet = leave-home-sheet.
States: S1 Open = open · S2 Deleting = deleting · S3 Done = done.
Specimens outside the grid, named in full:
"DestructiveConfirm / one-photo / open-keep-focused / ios / light" (the focus specimen on 01)
"DestructiveConfirm / one-photo / open / android / light"
"DestructiveConfirm / one-photo / open / web-390 / light"
"DestructiveConfirm / one-photo / open / web-1440 / light" (the 01 web-1440 crop repeats this specimen and carries its name)
"DestructiveConfirm / leave-home-sheet / open / android / light"

ANATOMY (01-anatomy: V1 S1 on iOS 393, plus the web-1440 crop of the same dialog, with callouts)
1. Container.
   - Dialogs (V1–V3): surface.base, radius xl 16 on all corners, padding 24, shadow lg. Width: 320pt on iOS; 364dp on Android (a Material 3 basic dialog, 24 from each screen edge; Notes 4.8); 400px on web-1440; 358px on web-390 (16px each side). Dialogs have no Close.
   - Sheet (V4): surface.base, radius xl 16 on the top corners, large detent, a visible "Close" text button in the top bar above the title.
   - Scrim, both kinds: text.primary #111827 at 40%, in both themes (board assumption, Notes B). In S1, tapping the scrim cancels.
2. Title: h3 20/28/600 text.primary, a question that names the object ("Delete this photo?").
3. Body: one sentence in body 16/24 text.primary, naming what survives.
4. Buttons: two buttons of equal size and type, 44pt tall (48dp on Android), radius md 8, horizontal padding 12, labels that describe outcomes. Both labels are bodyMedium 16/24/500 text.primary.
   - Destructive: surface.base fill, 1.5px semantic.error border (R10: 4.83:1), a leading 16pt trash glyph in semantic.error, glyph-to-label gap 8. Red only on the border and glyph. Callouts: "no red fill" and "no red text".
   - Keep: surface.base fill, 1px text.secondary border (R10: 4.83:1), no glyph.
   - Side by side: equal-width pair filling the content width, Keep leads, Delete trails, gap 8. Widths: 154dp on Android, 151px on web-390, 172px on web-1440. Stacked (iOS at every size, every platform at AX5 and 200%): Delete on top, Keep below, gap 8.
   - If a label doesn't fit on one line at its side-by-side width, stack the pair instead of wrapping or truncating, and log it on Notes A.
5. Initial focus: screen readers start on the title. Keyboard focus lands on Keep, never on the destructive button. Draw the R12 focus ring on "Keep it" in a second iOS specimen beside the first ("…/open-keep-focused/…").

VARIANTS (grid rows; viewer Maya Chen for V1–V3, Sam Ortega for V4)
V1 One photo (f10-mail-piece-photo, f10-bill-provenance). Title "Delete this photo?" Body "The bill and its amount stay; only the photo is removed." Buttons "Delete photo" / "Keep it".
V2 All photos (f10-mail-snap-privacy). Title "Delete all 17 photos?" Body "The bills and their amounts stay; only the photos are removed." Buttons "Delete 17 photos" / "Keep them".
V3 Keeper (f11-keeper-naming). Title "Remove Ollie?" Body "Today goes back to no keeper. You can add one again any time." Buttons "Remove Ollie" / "Keep Ollie".
V4 Leave home sheet (f3-members-roster). Title "Leave Larkspur Loop?" Two labelled lists, each heading in label 13/18/600 text.primary; each item is a 16pt glyph in text.secondary plus words in bodySmall text.primary:
  "What goes" (minus-stroke glyph): "The household calendar and bills" · "Household activity notifications" · "Your access to this home's place file".
  "What stays" (check-stroke glyph): "Dates you added that are Only you" · "Your saved places" · "Bills you marked paid still show 'Sam (no longer here)'".
  Buttons "Leave this home" / "Stay in this home". The destructive button uses the icon set's door-exit glyph (an arrow leaving a doorway) in semantic.error instead of the trash. If the set has none, use the trash glyph and log it on Notes C.

STATES (grid columns)
S1 Open: as above.
S2 Deleting: the title stays. The body becomes a progress line in body 16/24 text.primary with a 4pt determinate bar under it (primary.700 on surface.sunken, R10: 5.39:1; Reduce Motion: the bar steps with no easing). V1 "Deleting the photo…", bar 50% · V2 "Deleting 5 of 17…", bar 5/17 · V3 "Removing Ollie…", bar 50% · V4 "Leaving Larkspur Loop…", bar 50%. Only these lines end in an ellipsis. Both buttons are hidden until the action finishes. Escape, Back, the scrim and swipe-to-dismiss do nothing.
  V4 only: the top-bar "Close" stays visible but disabled per R16 (text.muted label, focusable, read as "Close, unavailable, Close is available when this finishes."), and "Close is available when this finishes." is written under the bar in caption 12/16 text.secondary (R10: 4.83:1).
S3 Done: the dialog or sheet has closed. Draw the host status line that replaces it, in bodySmall 14/20 text.primary with a 16pt check glyph in text.secondary: V1 "Photo deleted. The bill stays." · V2 "17 photos deleted. The bills and their amounts stay." · V3 "Ollie removed." · V4 Sam's Place tab: "You left Larkspur Loop." at the top, above a surface.sunken 361×200pt box labelled "Place tab (host)" in caption text.strong. No Undo, because the loss is real.

GRIDS
02-variants-by-states · light: 4 rows × 3 columns, iOS. Every cell applies.
04-variants-by-states · dark: the same full grid in dark tokens (R9). Every dialog and sheet is dark base over the scrim, never dark raised; S3 lines sit on a dark raised host card. Destructive border and glyph stay #DC2626 (R10: 3.70:1 on dark base; non-text only). Labels are dark text primary. Keep border #94A3B8 (R10: 6.96:1). S2 bar #38BDF8 on a dark raised track (dark sunken would vanish on dark base). Disabled Close #64748B (R10: 3.75:1); its written reason #94A3B8 (R10: 6.96:1).

PLATFORMS (03-platforms · light only). V1 S1 four ways, per anatomy 1 and 4:
- iOS 393: the grid cell repeated (a custom in-app dialog, not the system alert, so the outlined treatment shows).
- Android 412: a Material 3 basic dialog, buttons side by side. Back cancels in S1.
- web-390: a dialog, not a sheet: anchored 16px above the tab bar, no Close; Escape and the scrim cancel in S1.
- web-1440 crop: a centred modal, buttons side by side. Escape cancels in S1. Focus is trapped inside and returns to the opening control on close.
Also V4 S1 on Android: a bottom sheet with a drag handle and a visible "Close" (48dp). V4 on iOS is the grid cell.

AX5 / 200% / GREYSCALE (05-ax5-200-greyscale · light, per R17)
- (a) AX5 iOS, V1 and V4 at S1: both become scrollable sheets with the top-bar "Close" (it cancels like Keep), so V1 gains a Close. Buttons stack full width, pinned at the bottom, with scroll padding reserved so the last body line is never hidden. Names use ios-ax5.
- (b) 200% Android, V1 at S1: the dialog content scrolls and the buttons stack. Name uses android-200.
- (c) Greyscale of V1 S1 and V4 S1. Caption: "Reads without colour: the destructive button has its outcome label, its glyph and its heavier 1.5px border; the V4 lists differ by glyph shape and heading word."

ACCESSIBILITY
- Spoken: "Delete this photo?, dialog. The bill and its amount stay; only the photo is removed. Delete photo, button. Keep it, button." While deleting, a polite live region reads progress at most every 5 items: "Deleting 5 of 17", "Deleting 10 of 17", "Deleting 15 of 17", then "17 photos deleted. The bills and their amounts stay."
- Each title is unique. Cancel and S2 behaviour follow S1 and S2 above.
- Non-colour: the destructive action is named by its label and marked by its glyph and heavier border, never by red alone. The glyph is decorative for screen readers.
- Targets: buttons 44pt / 48dp / 44px with 8 gaps. Close 44pt / 48dp / 44px.

COPY. Titles are questions naming the object, bodies name what survives, buttons name outcomes. Never just "Are you sure?" or "This can't be undone". Use only the strings under VARIANTS, STATES and ACCESSIBILITY, plus "Close".

IN CONTEXT (06-in-context-and-rules · light, per R17)
- f10-mail-piece-photo: the photo viewer with V1 open over it.
- f10-mail-snap-privacy: the "Mail snaps" card with V2 open.
- f3-members-roster: Sam's member view with the V4 sheet.
Also consumed by: f10-bill-provenance, f11-keeper-naming

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of "Are you sure?" / "OK" / "Cancel", draw "Delete this photo?" / "Delete photo" / "Keep it" — because people decide faster when the buttons say what happens.
- Instead of "This can't be undone", draw the sentence naming what stays — because people fear losing more than they will.
- Instead of a filled red button, a red slab above the content, or red label text, draw the outlined button with a semantic.error border, the glyph and a text.primary label — because a red fill shouts, semantic hues go on glyphs and borders only, and red text drops below readable contrast in dark mode.
- Instead of default focus on the destructive button, put keyboard focus on Keep — because Enter must never destroy something.
- Instead of this dialog for a cheap removal, use InlineUndo — because dialogs are only for losses that can't be undone.

NOTES (extend 00d · Notes)
A. 4.1 Label: the contract asks for a red label ("text.error", not a token); the house style puts semantic hues on glyphs and borders only. This board follows the house style: both labels share bodyMedium 16/24/500 text.primary (no R4 exception), and the destructive button carries the border and glyph. The alternative (a semantic.error label, 4.83:1 on base) would need a dark error text token, since #DC2626 is 3.70:1 on dark base. Question for the founder.
   4.2 Dark: no dark error token and no accent token. #DC2626 stays on border and glyph only. Dialogs and sheets stay on dark base, where it measures 3.70:1 (3.03:1 on dark raised).
   4.3 S2 ignores Escape, Back, the scrim and swipe-to-dismiss, and the V4 Close stays visible, disabled and focusable with its written reason. The contract only says "Escape / Back cancels". Confirm.
   4.4 S2 progress is announced every 5 items, so V2 is drawn at "Deleting 5 of 17…". V1, V3 and V4 are single actions, drawn at a 50% mid-action pose.
   4.5 V4 uses the door-exit glyph because nothing is deleted. Confirm.
   4.6 At AX5, V1 becomes a sheet and gains "Close", because every sheet needs one. Confirm.
   4.7 The S2 count and bar are operation progress for a real loss, not a completion score (house invariant 6); kept because the contract asks for "deleting (progress count)". Confirm.
   4.8 The Android dialog is 364dp wide instead of 312dp so the side-by-side buttons (154dp) fit "Delete photo" with its glyph and padding. Confirm.
B. Sam Ortega is the member who leaves in V4. Ollie is HOME A's keeper. HOME A has 17 mail photos. The scrim (text.primary at 40%, both themes) is a board assumption.

Grid states: S1 Never asked = never-asked · S2 Granted = granted · S3 Declined = declined · S4 OS blocked = os-blocked · S5 Save status = save-status. The S5 cell holds three specimens, stacked, with the state keys saving, saved and save-failed.
Specimen outside the grid (in its own row below the grid on 02 and 04, labelled "Settings row · OS blocked" (new)): "NotificationAsk / settings-row / os-blocked / ios / <theme>".

  "NotificationAsk / primer-ios / never-asked / ios / <theme>"

ANATOMY (01-anatomy: the card row and the pickup primer on iOS 393, with callouts)
A. Card row form (on f4-briefing-optin-card). The briefing card is surface.base (radius lg 12, shadow sm) on surface.app, so the R10 "on surface.base" figures apply.

Component 00d-07: PushCopy. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print on 01): The canonical push strings and tray-preview artwork, so every surface draws the same notification.
Used in (print on 01): f4-notification-primer, f4-today-pickup-card, f1-today-air-band, f3-household-notifications, f4-notification-settings
ATTACH: none.

ARTBOARDS (7, then extend Notes)
00d · PushCopy · 01-anatomy-and-levels · light

00d · Notes (extend it)

KEYS (R7)
Variants: V1 Unconfirmed pickup = unconfirmed-pickup · V2 Confirmed pickup = confirmed-pickup · V3 Air, Time Sensitive = air-time-sensitive · V4 Air, below 151 = air-below-threshold · V5 Bill marked paid = bill-marked-paid · V6 Household roll-up = household-roll-up · V7 Date reminder = date-reminder · V8 Hidden-preview placeholders = hidden-preview.
States: S1 Collapsed = collapsed · S2 Expanded = expanded · S3 Lock screen public = lock-screen-public.
V8 cells hold four specimens each, one per placeholder group, with these state keys: collapsed-pickup, collapsed-air, collapsed-household, collapsed-date (S1) and lock-screen-public-pickup, lock-screen-public-air, lock-screen-public-household, lock-screen-public-date (S3).
Levels table rows (platform-neutral, light only): "PushCopy / levels / pickup-briefings-dates-bills / any / light" · "PushCopy / levels / household / any / light" · "PushCopy / levels / air-151-and-above-and-noaa / any / light" · "PushCopy / levels / air-below-151 / any / light".
Example: "PushCopy / air-time-sensitive / expanded / android / dark".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy-and-levels: V1 S2 on iOS 393 with callouts, then the levels table)
1. The tray preview is an in-app illustration: a surface.raised inset card (radius lg 12, padding 12) on a surface.sunken panel (radius lg, padding 16). It is never drawn as a system alert, over a wallpaper, or with system chrome. In the grids, the panel spans the full device width (393pt on iOS, 412dp on Android), so the inset is the real notification width: 361pt on iOS (337pt of text) and 380dp on Android. Inside a host sheet (IN CONTEXT, and the NotificationAsk primers) the panel fits the sheet's content width and the inset shrinks with it.
2. Inside the inset, the top row: the Pantopus app icon from the design system at 20pt (R15; if it isn't published, use the R15 fallback box and log it on Notes C), then "Pantopus" in caption 12/16 text.strong, then "now" in caption text.strong, right-aligned. (Secondary words on the raised inset inside a sunken frame use text.strong.) R10 has no light-raised row, so print no contrast figure for these words. On Android, the row uses the Android small-icon form of the same app icon, in the same illustrated style.
3. Title: bodySmallMedium 14/20/500 text.primary, 30 characters or fewer, caveat first. Under the string, draw a ruler marked in characters: one small tick per 5 characters, a labelled tick at 30, and the part after the last character shaded as the remaining room.
4. Body: bodySmall 14/20 text.primary, 40 characters or fewer on its first line. Draw the same character ruler, with the labelled tick at 40.
5. Place label: the street name only ("Larkspur Loop"), and only when the person has more than one place. Callout: "drop ' · Larkspur Loop' for someone with one place".
6. Caption under the panel: "This is the whole thing." in caption text.strong (it sits on the sunken panel, R10: 9.37:1).
7. Actions (expanded only): title-case text buttons inside the inset in bodySmallMedium primary.700, separated from the body by a 1px border.default rule (decoration). Print no contrast figure for them (no light-raised row in R10). They are drawn for illustration; real tray actions belong to the system.
8. Levels table, on the same artboard: four rows, each printed with its name from KEYS.
   - pickup, briefings, dates, bills: iOS Active / Android DEFAULT.
   - household: iOS Passive / Android LOW, one thread per home.
   - air at AQI 151 or above, and NOAA warnings: iOS Time Sensitive / Android HIGH.
   - air below AQI 151: iOS Active / Android DEFAULT.
   Under the table, print: "Never Time Sensitive for pickup." and "Android: the air group holds two channels, one HIGH (AQI 151 or above, and NOAA warnings) and one DEFAULT (below 151). Every other group has one channel."

VARIANTS (grid rows; the viewer is Maya, HOME A, who also has a saved place, so street labels show). Print each string's character count beside it, and each row's level in words under the row label.
V1 Unconfirmed pickup. Title "Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow" (28). Body "Recycling + garbage · city schedule" (35). Action "That's My Day". iOS Active / Android DEFAULT.
V2 Confirmed pickup. Title "Recycling + garbage tomorrow" (28). Body "Bins out tonight · Larkspur Loop" (32). No action. iOS Active / Android DEFAULT.
V3 Air, Time Sensitive. Title "Unhealthy air: AQI 176" (22). Body "AirNow, 4:00 PM · Larkspur Loop" (31). iOS Time Sensitive / Android HIGH (176 is 151 or above). In V3 S1 and S2 only (not S3), draw the words "Time Sensitive" as a caption word inside the inset beside "now" (caption text.strong), not as copied system chrome.
V4 Air, below 151 (the fixture alert; a variant this board adds, Notes 7.5). Title "Sensitive groups: AQI 118" (25). Body "AirNow, 4:00 PM · Larkspur Loop" (31). iOS Active / Android DEFAULT (the air group's below-151 channel).
V5 Bill marked paid (the actor is Sam). Title "Sam marked Clark PUD paid" (25). Body "Due Fri 23 Oct · Larkspur Loop" (30). No amount. iOS Passive / Android LOW.
V6 Household roll-up. Title "Sam marked 3 bills paid" (23). Body "Larkspur Loop" (13). One notification that updates in place. iOS Passive / Android LOW.
V7 Date reminder. Title "Lease notice due in 14 days" (27). Body "Tell your landlord by Mon 1 Mar" (31). Action "Done". iOS Active / Android DEFAULT.
V8 Hidden-preview placeholders: "Pickup reminder" (15) · "Air quality alert" (17) · "Household update" (16) · "Date reminder" (13). Android public versions: "Pantopus · Pickup reminder" (26) · "Pantopus · Air quality alert" (28) · "Pantopus · Household update" (27) · "Pantopus · Date reminder" (24).

STATES (grid columns)
S1 Collapsed tray at true truncation. On iOS, drawn at 393pt device width (inset 361pt); on Android, at 412dp (inset 380dp). Title on one line, body on one line. None of these strings truncates at real width: draw them whole, and show the shaded remaining room on the ruler. An ellipsis is allowed only where a string actually overflows. V8 S1: four collapsed trays, unlocked with previews hidden: the top row as in item 2, and one text line holding the placeholder. Under each V8 S1 specimen, print the board caption "Unlocked, previews hidden".
S2 Expanded: the full body. V1 and V7 add their action row ("That's My Day", "Done"). V2–V6 are drawn with the board caption "No action" under the inset. V8 S2: "Not applicable: a hidden preview does not expand until the device is unlocked".
S3 Lock screen public version, still the inset illustration, never on a wallpaper. The placeholder follows the variant's group (V1, V2 → "Pickup reminder"; V3, V4 → "Air quality alert"; V5, V6 → "Household update"; V7 → "Date reminder").
  - iOS S3: the top row keeps the icon, "Pantopus" and "now"; the single text line is the placeholder.
  - Android S3: the top row keeps the icon and "now" only; the single text line reads "Pantopus · <placeholder>", so the name appears once.
  - V8 S3: the four public forms for that grid's platform. Under each V8 S3 specimen, print the board caption "Locked, public version".
  Addresses, names, amounts and "Time Sensitive" never appear in S3.

GRIDS

03-android-variants-by-states · light: the same 8 × 3 grid on Android.
04-ios-variants-by-states · dark: the full 02 grid in dark tokens (R9).

Action buttons are #38BDF8 (R10: 6.83:1). The caption "This is the whole thing." is #F1F5F9 on the dark base panel (R10: 16.30:1). Rulers, counts and the V8 captions stay board chrome in dark text.secondary.

AX5 / 200% / GREYSCALE (06-ax5-200-greyscale · light, per R17)
- (a) AX5 iOS, V1 S2 and V3 S2: in the in-app illustration, the title and body wrap fully and never truncate; the caption "This is the whole thing." wraps; the illustration grows taller and never scales down. Names use ios-ax5.

- (c) Greyscale of V1 S2 (the light default) and V3 S2 (the most state-heavy cell). Caption: "Reads without colour: the Time Sensitive marker on V3 reads by its words; levels are labelled in words, never by colour."

ACCESSIBILITY
- The in-app illustration is read as one element: "Example notification. Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow. Recycling + garbage · city schedule. This is the whole thing." (each variant reads its own title and body).
- No house numbers and no full addresses in any string. Actions are title case.

- Targets: the illustration is not interactive. Real tray actions belong to the system.

COPY: all strings are given in ANATOMY, VARIANTS and STATES; use them exactly. Never "Open Pantopus to…". No keeper name or voice. No marketing, Founding or referral pushes. No pickup reminder alongside the briefing for the same pickup.

PLATFORMS

- Android: DEFAULT / LOW / HIGH channels, one per group, except the air group's two (levels table). The public version is "Pantopus · <placeholder>".
- Web: no push on this board.

IN CONTEXT (07-in-context-and-rules · light, per R17)

NOTES (extend 00d · Notes)

"Open Settings" (6.1) is also title case. This board follows the contract for both. Question: keep title case, or switch to sentence case ("That's my day", "Open settings")?
   7.5 V4 is a variant this board adds: the contract lists one air variant. It comes from the contract's "Time Sensitive only at 151 or above" and research brief section 3 (air: HIGH / DEFAULT), and covers the fixture's AQI 118 alert, which is below the threshold. Its title "Sensitive groups: AQI 118" is invented. Confirm the added variant and its title.

Component 00d-08: ReminderLeadControl. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print on 01): Shows every reminder that will actually fire, on a small timeline running back from the date the person must act.
Used in (print on 01): x-date-sheet, f10-extraction-confirm

ARTBOARDS (5, then finish Notes)
00d · ReminderLeadControl · 01-anatomy · light
00d · ReminderLeadControl · 02-variants-by-states · light
00d · ReminderLeadControl · 03-variants-by-states · dark
00d · ReminderLeadControl · 04-ax5-200-greyscale · light
00d · ReminderLeadControl · 05-in-context-and-rules · light
00d · Notes (extend and finish it)

KEYS (R7)
Variants: V1 Date sheet = date-sheet · V2 Extraction confirm = extraction-confirm · V3 Lease = lease-notice.
States: S1 Default = default · S2 Lead already passed = lead-passed · S3 Disabled = disabled.
Specimens outside the grid, named exactly:
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default-one-day / ios / <theme>" (light on 02, dark on 03)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default-focused / ios / light" (01)
  "ReminderLeadControl / segment / chosen-then-passed / ios / light" (the inset on 01)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default / ios-ax5 / light" (04)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default / android-200 / light" (04)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default / ios-ax2 / light" (04)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default / android-150 / light" (04)
  "ReminderLeadControl / date-sheet / default / web-1440 / light" (04)

PASSED-LEAD RULE (stated once here; everything below refers to it)
TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026. A lead whose date is before TODAY has passed. A passed lead gets exactly one of two treatments:
- Passed (never chosen): disabled per R16. Label in text.muted (disabled only), no check, still focusable, read as "<N> days, unavailable, <N> days before was <date>, which has passed." Its reason is also written in readable text: the passed-lead line, 8pt below the control and above the timeline, in bodySmall 14/20 text.secondary (R10: 4.83:1; dark #94A3B8, R10: 6.96:1). It names only never-chosen passed leads: "60 days has passed for this date." (V1) or "60 and 30 days have passed for this date." (V2). With no such lead, there is no line. Activating a passed segment shows the explanation line and suggestion instead of selecting it.
- Chosen-then-passed (the lead was selected, then the date was edited so it has now passed): a primary.50 fill, a 1.5px primary.700 border, NO check, the label in bodySmall 14/20 at weight 400 in text.primary, and the word "passed" under the label in caption 12/16 text.primary; both lines fit inside the 44pt segment. Dark: a primary.900 fill, a 1.5px #38BDF8 border, no check, label and word in dark text primary. Read as "<N> days, selected, passed. <N> days before was <date>, which has passed." It keeps this treatment, with the explanation line and suggestion under the control, until the person picks another lead. This is the one extra treatment R12 allows.
The suggestion is always the longest lead still ahead. Nothing is saved until the person taps the suggestion or picks a live segment. The timeline never draws a tick for a passed lead.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy: V1 S1 on iOS 393 with callouts; the example date is the water-heater warranty ending Sat 12 Dec 2026)
Lead dates: 60 days = Tue 13 Oct 2026 (passed) · 30 days = Thu 12 Nov 2026 · 7 days = Sat 5 Dec 2026 · 1 day = Fri 11 Dec 2026.
1. Label above the control: label 13/18/600 text.primary, "Remind me".
2. Segmented control, 361pt × 44pt (Android 380 × 48dp), four equal segments: "60 days", "30 days", "7 days", "1 day". Container: 1px text.secondary outline (R10: 4.83:1), radius md 8, 1px text.secondary dividers. Unselected segment: surface.base, label in bodySmall text.primary. Selected: the R12 selection treatment (fill + check + 600 weight).
   - "60 days" is passed (rule). Callout: "passed: Tue 13 Oct; focusable, reason read out and written below".
   - The passed-lead line, 8pt below the control: "60 days has passed for this date."
   - Chosen-then-passed: drawn once as a small inset beside the control (rule). Callout: "chosen before a date edit; no check; 'passed' written".
   - Focus: the R12 ring on the unselected live segment "7 days", in a second full specimen beside the first ("default-focused").
3. Mini timeline, 361pt wide, not to scale. It starts below the passed-lead line (or below the control when there is no line). Vertical order, top to bottom:
   a. Event line (16pt), right-aligned to the 361pt edge: KindGlyph (16pt, R15), 4pt, then the event label in caption text.primary ("Water-heater warranty ends"). On the same line, left-aligned, the caption "not to scale" in caption text.secondary.
   b. 4pt, then the timeline: a 2px text.secondary horizontal line from x 0 to 361, with three ticks (12pt tall, 2px wide) centred at x 54, 180 and 307. A two-slash break mark sits on the line at x 117. A 1px text.secondary leader line drops from under the event label to the top of the tick at 307.
   c. 4pt, then under each tick, centred on it: the date in bodySmall 14/20 text.primary ("Thu 12 Nov 2026" · "Fri 11 Dec 2026" · "Sat 12 Dec 2026"), and under that the role in caption 12/16 text.secondary ("30 days before" · "Day before" · "Day of"). Tick dates use the contract's absolute form, with no relative count (Notes 8.6).
4. Caption, 8pt below the role labels: "We'll also remind you the day before and on the day." in caption text.secondary.
5. When "1 day" is selected, the lead and the day before are the same day, so only two ticks are drawn, at x 54 and 307 ("Fri 11 Dec 2026 · Day before", "Sat 12 Dec 2026 · Day of"), with no break mark (the ticks are one day apart), and the caption reads "We'll also remind you on the day." Use the full names from KEYS.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Spoken: "Remind me, 30 days before, selected, 2 of 4." The segment's accessibility label intentionally expands "30 days" to "30 days before". Passed and chosen-then-passed segments read as the rule says; the passed-lead line is plain text read in order after the control. The timeline is one element with a summary: V1 "Reminders on Thu 12 Nov, Fri 11 Dec and Sat 12 Dec." · V1 one day "Reminders on Fri 11 Dec and Sat 12 Dec." · V2 "Reminders on Wed 21 Oct, Tue 27 Oct and Wed 28 Oct." · V3 "Reminders on Sat 30 Jan, Sun 28 Feb and Mon 1 Mar." The same facts appear as a list at AX sizes. The S2 explanation line is announced politely when it appears.
- Non-colour encoding: selection is a text label plus a fill change plus a check, never colour alone.
- Targets: segments (disabled ones included) are 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android and 44px on web. The suggestion button is 44pt. Ticks are not targets.

COPY: all strings are given in the rule, ANATOMY, VARIANTS, STATES and AX rows; use them exactly. Dates always show the weekday.

PLATFORMS: the same on all platforms apart from target sizes and the large-text layouts above. On web-1440, the control sits in the date sheet's 480px side panel (04 extra row).

IN CONTEXT (05-in-context-and-rules · light, per R17)
- x-date-sheet: the Date sheet for "Water-heater warranty", with V1 below the date field.
- x-date-sheet (lease): the Date sheet for the lease, with V3.

Also consumed by: none beyond these two surfaces.

INSTEAD OF
- Instead of a single "Remind me 30 days before" row, draw all three reminders with their real dates — because three will fire, and the person should see each one.
- Instead of anchoring the lease reminder to Wed 31 Mar 2027, anchor it to the notice deadline Mon 1 Mar 2027 — because the notice is what the person must act on.
- Instead of silently accepting, hiding or greying a passed lead, apply the PASSED-LEAD RULE, with its written passed-lead line — because a reminder dated in the past never fires, and silent dead controls leave people guessing.
- Instead of keeping the check on a lead that passed after a date edit, draw the chosen-then-passed segment — because a check says a reminder will fire.
- Instead of radio circles at large text, draw selectable rows with a check — because filled vs hollow circles mean provenance.
- Instead of showing selection by colour alone, draw fill + check + weight — because colour alone fails in greyscale and for colour-blind people.
- Instead of a timeline drawn to scale, draw fixed tick positions with a "not to scale" break — because a to-scale 60-day line squashes the last two ticks together.

NOTES (extend 00d · Notes, then finish it)
A. 8.1 V3: the fixture's lease reminder is Sat 30 Jan 2027 (14 days before the notice deadline; PushCopy V7 says "due in 14 days"), but the contract's leads are 60 / 30 / 7 / 1. This board draws 30 days (Sat 30 Jan 2027). Question: add a 14-day option, or change the fixture?
   8.2 Passed leads: the contract gives no rule. The PASSED-LEAD RULE, including the written passed-lead line, is this board's invention (following OfflineNotice's "Disabled controls stay focusable" and R16). Confirm.

DONE WHEN
