text:
Use the Pantopus house style pasted above and the Foundations components (boards 00a–00d), by exact name.

SCREEN: Your places (and which one Today uses) · f1-your-places

TYPE: EXTENSION of the existing designed screen "Saved places". This screen already exists in the Pantopus design system. The attached screenshot is exact. Keep everything and change only what is listed.

ATTACH: (1) the current "Saved places" screen on iOS and on Android; (2) a web capture of the current web saved-places page (today it is a bare 760px page with no sidebar and no tab bar); (3) the web Place tab shell at 1440 (left sidebar) and 390 (four-tab bar), which this list moves into; (4) Today's location row showing the "Saved place · Only you" chip; (5) the Foundations board.

PLATFORMS & VIEWPORTS: iOS 393x852 · Android 412x915 · web 1440x900 with the left sidebar, Place selected · web 390x844 with the four-tab bar, Place selected. On every web frame, draw the list inside the normal Place shell at /app/place/saved.

WHERE IT LIVES & HOW PEOPLE ARRIVE: Place tab. Entry points: (1) the place file's Address row: the place file is the Place tab's first screen for everyone with a place (only with no saved place at all is this list's empty state the tab's first screen); (2) tapping the "Saved place · Only you" chip in Today's location row; (3) the Place tab itself when no place is saved (the empty state); (4) "See your places" on the save confirmation; (5) on iOS, the existing saved-places route from the feed context bar; (6) Today's one-time notice after a claim (owned by the Today tab), which opens this list with the arrival line described below; (7) proposed: the Notifications settings caption that names the place briefings follow; (8) the Add a place sheet, when opened from here, returns here after saving. When the person arrives from the Today chip, scroll the row Today uses into view once, fade its highlight, and move accessibility focus to that row. Where actions lead: Open goes to that place's place file. Claim this address opens the existing claim flow, which ends on the claim receipt. + Add a place opens the Add a place sheet. After Remove, Today never shows that address again, even if Today is already open: a removed address still showing on Today reads as a privacy failure on an "Only you" surface.

WHO AND WHEN: Jordan Lee, 36, moved from Portland to PLACE B, 1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas, on Fri 9 Oct and saved it when he signed up on Sat 10 Oct (the save and email projects). It was his only place through his first week. On Sun 18 Oct he saved four more, his mom's house last, and each save moved Today to the newest place, so on Mon 19 Oct morning he chose Birchfield again with Use for Today. At 6:10 PM Today shows Birchfield. He taps the chip to check that Today isn't using Mom's house.

THE ONE JOB: See every place you saved, see which one Today uses and why, and switch, claim or remove it.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: The eye lands first on the top row, which carries the only "Used for Today" badge, then on the sentence directly under it that says why, then on the other rows, which carry no badge. The one primary action is "+ Add a place" at the foot of the list. Row actions live in each row's menu.

CONTENT (Jordan, except where marked):
Title "Your places". Directly under the title, the ScopeChip saved-place variant "Saved place · Only you". It replaces the retired line "Only you can see these."
Each row: label · city, state and ZIP · saved date. The row Today uses comes first, then the rest, newest first:
- 1107 NE Birchfield Ct · Camas, WA 98607 · Saved Sat 10 Oct · badge "Used for Today". Under it: "Today uses this place because you chose it."
- Mom's house · Camas, WA 98607 · Saved Sun 18 Oct
- The Blairmont rental · Vancouver, WA 98683 · Saved Sun 18 Oct
- Sister's apartment · Portland, OR 97214 · Saved Sun 18 Oct
- Worst case: Grandma and Grandpa's lake house on Lacamas Shores Drive · Camas, WA 98607 · Saved Sun 18 Oct
With only one place (frames 5 and 6), Birchfield's sentence is "Today uses the address you saved most recently." After Birchfield is removed (frame 12), Mom's house, the newest save, takes the badge with that same sentence.
Foot row: "+ Add a place".
Saved-row menu, in this order: Open · Use for Today · Claim this address · Remove. The badged row never offers Use for Today.
Chosen place: after Use for Today on Mom's house, the badge moves to that row, the row moves to the top, and the sentence reads "Today uses this place because you chose it." The status line reads "Today now uses Mom's house."
Today using a location not in the list: no row is badged. A single line sits above the list: "Today is using a location you looked at recently, not one of these. Choose Use for Today on a place to switch." (For a pin set elsewhere: "Today is using a location you pinned, not one of these. Choose Use for Today on a place to switch.") Every saved row, including Birchfield, offers Use for Today.
Maya (HOME A): the list splits into two groups with plain labels. Group "Your home": 2418 NE Larkspur Loop · Vancouver, WA 98684 · Claimed Tue 1 Sep, with the home glyph, the ScopeChip "Your household" and the caption "Today uses your home". Group "Saved places", with the "Saved place · Only you" chip in its group header: Mom's house · Camas, WA 98607 · Saved Fri 4 Sep, then Sam's old apartment · Vancouver, WA 98661 · Saved Sat 15 Aug.
Maya just claimed (frame 9): the home row reads "Claimed Mon 19 Oct"; she had saved 2418 NE Larkspur Loop before, and that saved row is gone.
Maya arriving from Today's notice (frame 10): the LandingBannerSlot line "Today now uses 2418 NE Larkspur Loop. Mom's house is still saved." with a trailing "Close", above the groups; home row "Claimed Mon 19 Oct".

LAYOUT & VISUALIZATION: Top bar. The place file is the Place tab's first screen, so for everyone with a place, Jordan and Maya alike, this list is a pushed screen with a back control labelled "Place" (iOS back chevron with the large title; Android navigation arrow; web breadcrumb "Place / Your places"). Only when no place is saved is this list the tab's first screen: then its empty state has a tab-root title and no back control.
List. A plain vertical list. In Jordan's frames exactly one row carries the StatusChip "Used for Today" variant: surface.sunken fill, text.strong label, a leading 12pt sun-outline glyph in text.strong (not a check, not a circle), not tappable. Every other saved row carries nothing: one badge slot, one menu button, no chips, no radio column. Only the home row carries a chip (ScopeChip "Your household"). Put the precedence sentence (bodySmall, text.secondary) directly under the badged row, never in the page header. Show "Today uses the address you saved most recently." only when Today's source is a saved place and nothing is chosen; show "because you chose it" only when the person picked it; show the above-list line only when Today uses a location that is not a row.
With a home: split into "Your home" and "Saved places" groups; the saved-place chip moves into the Saved places group header. The home row carries no StatusChip; its caption "Today uses your home" is the Today marker and its reason, and no saved row is badged. A claimed home always drives Today: a pinned or recently viewed location never replaces it. Draw the home row as a home, not a disabled saved place: home glyph (home pillar token, icon only), "Your household" chip, the caption. The home row's menu has only Open, which goes to the place file: no Use for Today, Claim or Remove. Leaving a home stays in home settings behind DestructiveConfirm and is not drawn here.
This list is the answer to "where does Today get this address"; there is no second sheet. Row menu form: iOS pull-down menu from the More button; Android Material 3 dropdown menu; web-1440 popover; web-390 bottom sheet with Close. Menus never stack on another sheet. When the service cannot say which place Today uses, draw no badge and show an InlineErrorRow in the sentence slot.

INTERACTION, MOTION & HAPTICS: Tapping a row opens it. Tapping the menu button (44pt / 48dp / 44px) opens the menu. Use for Today: the menu closes, the badge stays where it is until the save succeeds, and the sentence slot shows "Switching Today to Mom's house…" only if the save takes 1s or longer; on success the badge and row move; on failure the InlineErrorRow appears. Remove collapses the row in place to an InlineUndo (height change 300ms or less), and the badge cross-fades to the next row in the same frame. Undo stays until the person leaves the screen; no timer and no confirm dialog. This replaces Android's 4-second snackbar. If the removal fails on the server, the row comes back in place, the badge returns to its original row, and an InlineErrorRow sits under that row. Tapping the header ScopeChip expands one explanation in place: "Saved places are only for you. To share one with the people you live with, claim it." plus a text button "Claim this address" for the place Today uses. Every LandingBannerSlot line on this screen has a trailing 44pt action: the sync line uses "Review"; the account-switch and claim-notice arrival lines use "Close". One banner at a time. A successful Use for Today gives one light haptic tick; nothing else has a haptic. With Reduce Motion on, every change is a cross-fade. No swipe-only actions: every row action is also a menu item.

FOUNDATIONS COMPONENTS USED: ScopeChip (saved-place variant, expandable, under the title or in the Saved places group header; "Your household" variant on the home row) · StatusChip (new "Used for Today" variant, sun-outline glyph, saved rows only) · InlineUndo (removed-row variant, consequence in the same line) · WarmingSkeleton (row skeleton with the badge slot reserved) · OfflineNotice with FreshnessLine (offline variant) · InlineErrorRow (load failed; Use for Today failed; remove failed) · LandingBannerSlot (sync merge V6 with Review; new account-switched and claim-notice arrival variants with Close; one at a time).

ACCESSIBILITY: Reading order: title, scope chip (or group label and chip), the Today row, the precedence sentence, other rows, + Add a place. Each row is one element, for example: "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas, Washington 98607. Saved Saturday 10 October. Used for Today." Its custom actions are Open, Claim this address and Remove; the visible menu button reads "More for 1107 NE Birchfield Ct". Arriving from the Today chip moves accessibility focus to the row Today uses; arriving from Today's claim notice moves focus to the arrival line. The badge is a word, never only a colour; the sun-outline and home glyphs are decorative, and the home row's caption carries its meaning. A disabled Use for Today stays focusable and gives its reason. Removed rows, the remove-failed row, the switching line, the sync line and arrival lines are role=status. Targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px. At AX5 the label, city and saved date stack, the badge moves under the label, and labels wrap and never ellipsise.

COPY: "Your places" · "Place" (back label) · "Saved place · Only you" · "Your household" · "Your home" · "Saved places" · "Used for Today" · "Today uses the address you saved most recently." · "Today uses this place because you chose it." · "Today is using a location you looked at recently, not one of these. Choose Use for Today on a place to switch." · "Today is using a location you pinned, not one of these. Choose Use for Today on a place to switch." · "Today uses your home" · "Your claimed home comes first." (reason under a disabled Use for Today) · "Claimed Tue 1 Sep" · "Claimed Mon 19 Oct" · "Joined Tue 1 Sep" · "Saved Sat 10 Oct" · "Open" · "Use for Today" · "Claim this address" · "Remove" · "More for 1107 NE Birchfield Ct" · "+ Add a place" · "Switching Today to Mom's house…" · "Removed \"The Blairmont rental\" · Undo" · "Removed \"1107 NE Birchfield Ct\" · Today now uses Mom's house · Undo" · "Removed \"1107 NE Birchfield Ct\" · Today will ask for a place · Undo" · "We couldn't remove \"The Blairmont rental\" · Retry" · "We couldn't remove \"1107 NE Birchfield Ct\" · Retry" · "Today now uses Mom's house." · "Saved places are only for you. To share one with the people you live with, claim it." · Empty: "No places yet" / "Save an address and Today will show its weather, air, alerts and dates." / "+ Add a place" · "You switched accounts. These are the places saved to this account." · "Synced 3 items from your other device · Review" · "You're offline · as of 6:04 PM" · "You're offline. You can open your places. Changes need a connection." · "We couldn't load your places · Retry" · "We couldn't change the place Today uses · Retry" · "Today now uses 2418 NE Larkspur Loop. Mom's house is still saved." · Today's own line after the last removal (owned by the Today tab): "Today starts with a place" · "Close".

EDGE CASES: The longest label wraps to three lines. With 12 places the list scrolls with no pagination, and the Today row stays first. Zero places shows the empty state. On a slow network, skeletons appear only after 1s, with the badge slot reserved. If Jordan removes his last place, the undo row says Today will ask for a place. A household member such as Sam Ortega sees 2418 NE Larkspur Loop under "Your home" with "Your household" and "Joined Tue 1 Sep" in place of "Claimed". A saved place outside Clark County looks like any other row, with no warning. Claiming a different address first shows a one-time notice on Today; tapping it lands here with the arrival line. Claiming the saved address shows it once, as a home, and the old saved row is gone. A home user's Today never moves to a viewed or pinned location, so Maya's frames never show the other-location line. Offline, Open works from cache; Use for Today, Claim and Remove are disabled with the reason, and + Add a place is disabled with "Adding a place needs a connection."

INSTEAD OF:
- Instead of a chip or status on every row, draw one StatusChip on one saved row — because one mark reads instantly.
- Instead of a check glyph or a toggled-looking selected chip for "Used for Today", draw the neutral StatusChip with a sun-outline glyph — because it is a status, not a control, and the check belongs to Paid and selected choices.
- Instead of a radio group or settings picker, draw a list with a row menu — because this is a list of places, not a preference.
- Instead of a greyed-out saved row for a claimed home, draw a home row in its own "Your home" group with Open as its only action — because it is a fact, and leaving a home belongs in home settings.
- Instead of one "Only you" chip over a list that holds a home, split the groups and chip each — because scope must be true for every row.
- Instead of a separate "Where Today gets this" sheet, put the reason beside the badged row or on the home row, or above the list when Today uses something else — because this list already answers that.
- Instead of a "Remove this place?" dialog or a timed snackbar, collapse the row to Removed · Undo — because lasting undo is safer.
- Instead of "home" or "household" on saved rows, use "Saved place" — because a saved place is shared with nobody.

DONE WHEN: A web person who saved a place reaches this list from the Place tab and from the Today chip. Anyone can say which place Today uses and why within five seconds, including when it is not a row and when they have a home. No caption on screen contradicts another. Removing the Today place moves the badge in the same frame, a removed place never lingers on Today, and a failed removal visibly puts it back. A claimed address appears once, as a home, with no Remove. Every frame reads correctly in greyscale and at AX5.

name: Add a place (signed-in address search + save)
job: Type one address, save it privately, and see truthfully which place Today now runs on.
attach: (1) Today's no-place card and (2) the Your places list and its empty state, as backdrops; (3) Today's location row with the "Saved place · Only you" chip; (4) the existing iOS save-place sheet, as a reference for sheet chrome only; (5) the Foundations board;…
text:
Use the Pantopus house style pasted above and the Foundations components (boards 00a–00d), by exact name.

SCREEN: Add a place · f1-add-place-sheet

TYPE: NEW. It is a sheet; nothing like it exists for a signed-in person on web or Android.

ATTACH: (1) Today's no-place card and (2) the Your places list and its empty state, as backdrops; (3) Today's location row with the "Saved place · Only you" chip; (4) the existing iOS save-place sheet, as a reference for sheet chrome only; (5) the Foundations board; (6) Today in its warming state for a saved place (iOS and web-1440), as the backdrop for frames 12 and 13; (7) Maya's Your places on Android from the f1-your-places project, if drawn, as the backdrop for frame 17.

PLATFORMS & VIEWPORTS: iOS 393x852: the sheet opens at the large detent while the field has focus, with a grabber and a visible Close. Android 412x915: a full-height Material 3 modal bottom sheet that resizes above the keyboard, with a visible Close. Web 1440x900: a centred 560-wide modal with Close. Web 390x844: a bottom sheet with Close. On iOS and Android, Save and the "Only you will see this." caption stay pinned above the keyboard. Host behind the sheet: on web-1440 the sidebar stays visible and dimmed behind the modal; on web-390 the host stays dimmed above the sheet; on iOS and Android only the top of the dimmed host shows above the sheet.

WHERE IT LIVES & HOW PEOPLE ARRIVE: The sheet opens over Today and over the Place tab. Entry points: (1) Today's no-place card, whose button is now "Add a place" (it was "Preview an address"); (2) "+ Add a place" on Your places, in the empty state and at the list foot; (3) a widget tap when there is no place (the widget reads "Save an address to see today here"), which opens Today with this sheet on top; (4) the widget how-to's "Save an address first" button, which lands in the same place as (3); (5) the place file's Address row when it is empty; (6) proposed: "Save this address" on the signed-in compare arrival header. "Preview an address" stays only on buttons that really go to the /start preview. The sheet receives nothing, except from the compare arrival header, where it opens in the selected state (03) with the address the person just typed already confirmed.
Where it leads: on success the sheet returns to where it opened. From Today, the widget, the place file's empty Address row or the compare header, it dismisses onto Today: Today's location row reads "408 NE Juniper St · Saved place · Only you" (when Today switched), Today opens in its warming state, and a one-line role=status row sits directly under the location row until the person leaves Today (not a toast). From Your places, it dismisses onto Your places: the new row appears at the top (with the "Used for Today" StatusChip if Today switched), and a role=status line under the title reads "Saved privately. Today now uses 408 NE Juniper St." with a text button "See Today". For a home user, a chosen-place user or a viewed/pinned-location user, that line uses the matching "Today still uses…" string below, and they stay on Your places.

WHO AND WHEN: Jordan Lee, 36, moved from Portland to PLACE B on Fri 9 Oct and saved 1107 NE Birchfield Ct when he signed up on Sat 10 Oct (the save and email projects). On Sun 18 Oct, after his first week, he saved three more places, and Today now runs on the newest, The Blairmont rental. At 6:10 PM he opens Your places on his iPhone, taps "+ Add a place" and types his mom's address from memory, misspelled: "408 NE Junpier". These frames are dated Sun 18 Oct, not TODAY. Frame 5 shows the unnamed signed-in first-place case over Today's no-place card; the sheet shows no name.

THE ONE JOB: Type one address, save it privately, and see truthfully which place Today now runs on.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: The eye lands first on the focused "Street address" field (caret in it, keyboard up on iOS and Android), then on the suggestion list beneath, then on the Save button with "Only you will see this." under it. Save is the single primary action.

CONTENT:
Title "Add a place". Field label "Street address". Caption under the field: "We use the address you type — no location access."
Typed value: "408 NE Junpier". Five plain-text suggestions, ranked by distance from Camas and Vancouver, forgiving the typo:
- 408 NE Juniper St, Camas, WA 98607
- 408 NE Juniper Ct, Camas, WA 98607
- 480 NE Juniper St, Camas, WA 98607
- 408 NW Juniper Ave, Vancouver, WA 98685
- 408 SE Juniper Dr, Portland, OR 97202
Selected: the address appears as one confirmed line (AddressChip, selected) above the button. Button "Save". Directly under the button: "Only you will see this." When the person already has a saved place and nothing else is in charge of Today, add a caption under Save: "Today will switch to this address. You can change it in Your places." (not shown on the first-place frame).
Not found: "We couldn't find that address." plus the text button "Can't find it? Enter it line by line". It opens five fields in the same sheet: "Street address" (keeps the typed text), "Apt, suite or unit" (optional), "City", "State" (a picker, default "WA") and "ZIP code".
Lookup service down: the manual fields open with "Address search isn't working right now. Enter it line by line instead."
Outside Clark County: "1402 NE 33rd Ave, Portland, OR 97232". Save stays enabled, and one line appears under the address: "Flood, wildfire, air and radon readings work here. Pickup days and local deadlines are on file only in Clark County, WA for now."
Duplicate: typing "1107 NE Birchfield" matches his first place, which has no name of its own. That suggestion row reads "Already saved · Sat 10 Oct". Selecting it shows the AddressChip duplicate variant with the dated message "You already saved this on Sat 10 Oct." The primary becomes "Use for Today", with a text button "Open it".
Saved status (Today's status row, or the line on Your places): "Saved privately. Today now uses 408 NE Juniper St."
Chosen-place variant (if Jordan had already chosen Birchfield with Use for Today): "Saved privately. Today still uses 1107 NE Birchfield Ct, the place you chose."
Viewed-location variant (Today runs on a location he looked at recently that is not a saved row): "Saved privately. Today still uses the location you looked at recently." Pinned twin: "Saved privately. Today still uses the location you pinned."
Claimed-home variant (Maya, HOME A): "Saved privately. Today still uses your home."

LAYOUT & VISUALIZATION: A deliberately compact sheet: one field, a plain list, one button and one scope sentence. No map, pin, thumbnail, reading, grade, "what you'll get" list, progress dots or second page, because the reading appears on Today a second later. Suggestion rows are text only (48pt / 48dp / 44px), with the untyped part at medium weight in the same size as the row text. The not-found message, manual fields, outside-area line and duplicate chip replace the suggestion list in place; the sheet never opens a second page, and it keeps its height when a state replaces the list so nothing resizes under the thumb. In the duplicate state, the AddressChip duplicate variant shows its message only; its inline "Use for Today" action is hidden because the primary button carries it. At AX5 the sheet scrolls. On Today after saving, the status row is one line directly under the location row (bodySmall, text.primary). On Your places after saving, the status line sits under the title and above the list.

INTERACTION, MOTION & HAPTICS: Suggestions update as the person types. No indicator for lookups under 1s; after that, "Looking up addresses…" in the list slot. Tapping a suggestion selects it and enables Save. Save shows its loading state and locks the field. On success the sheet dismisses with the platform transition onto the screen it opened from, and iOS and Android give one light haptic tick. "See Today" on the Your places status line opens Today. Close, Android Back and web Escape discard the sheet and return focus to the button that opened it. After a successful save, focus goes to the status row or line. With Reduce Motion on, list changes and dismissal are cross-fades.

FOUNDATIONS COMPONENTS USED: AddressChip (selected state; duplicate variant with a dated message and its inline action hidden) · ScopeChip (sentence form "Only you will see this."; the saved-place chip on Today) · StatusChip ("Used for Today" on the new row on Your places, as drawn in that project) · OfflineNotice (form-offline variant) · InlineErrorRow (save-failed variant, value kept).

ACCESSIBILITY: Title "Add a place" is unique, and focus is trapped in the sheet. The field uses street-address autofill; ZIP code uses a number keyboard; State is a labelled picker. "5 addresses found" and each error are announced politely and tied to the field. Each suggestion row is one element that reads the full address. Save's disabled state explains itself: "Pick an address first". Focus stays visible above the keyboard. The status row on Today and the status line on Your places are role=status. At AX5, the manual fields are one column and addresses wrap. Nothing depends on colour.

PLATFORMS & VIEWPORTS: iOS 393x852 · Android 412x915 · web 1440x900 (Place shell with the sidebar, content column 560 wide) · web 390x844 (four-tab bar).

WHERE IT LIVES & HOW PEOPLE ARRIVE: Place tab, the save moment just before Today. Entry points:
(1) /start → "Keep this address handy" → register: lands on 03-saved, because the address was saved at registration. /start → "Keep this address handy" → sign in: the save runs on arrival, showing 02-saving only if it takes 1s or longer, then 03-saved. The person never taps Save twice. The native launch funnel works the same way.
(2) The email confirmation page, whose code or link opens 03-saved directly with "Email confirmed." as a status line at the top, never the pre-save Save button, because the person already asked to keep the address.
(3) Recovery arrivals: when the /start draft is lost or expired on arrival, or the person confirms their email after the hold has expired (held mode), this screen opens in recovery: 04a when the server or this device still has the address, otherwise 04b. The email page does not draw its own recovery; it routes here.
The Add a place sheet does not open this screen: it reuses this screen's saved sentence as a status line. The previous step hands over the address the server holds (the device's own copy is only a backup, not the normal cross-device path) and the account it was started under. Where actions lead: See Today goes to Today in its warming state, location row "1107 NE Birchfield Ct · Saved place · Only you". Claim this address opens the existing claim flow. See your places opens Your places. This screen never asks for notification permission.

WHO AND WHEN: Jordan Lee looked up 1107 NE Birchfield Ct on his work laptop at lunch on Sat 10 Oct, the day after moving from Portland, and registered. At 6:10 PM that day he confirms his email on his iPhone and arrives here. These frames are dated Sat 10 Oct, the fixture save day.

THE ONE JOB: Say in one sentence what the save changed, then hand the person to Today.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: The eye lands first on the title "Saved privately" with its tick, then on the one sentence naming what changed, then on the filled "See Today" button, the single primary action.

CONTENT:
Pre-save (01): title "Keep this address handy"; address line "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas, WA 98607"; body "Today and a night-before pickup reminder run on it."; primary "Save"; caption "Only you will see this."
Saving (02): actions disabled, address intact, and the inline line "Saving…" only if the save takes 1s or longer.
Saved (03): title "Saved privately" with a tick; the same address line; body "Today now uses this address, and so will any reminders you turn on."; primary "See Today"; secondary "Claim this address" with caption "A separate step, only if you live here."; tertiary "See your places"; caption under the stack "Only you will see this." When arriving from the email page, a status line "Email confirmed." sits above the title. This is the exact page the email project draws as its confirmed landing; there is no separate "Saved … to your account." line (flow-01 step 8's line is folded into the title plus the address line).
Announced on save: "Saved privately. Today now uses 1107 NE Birchfield Ct."
Recovery, address still held on the server or on this device (04a): keep the pre-save title. Body "Save the address you looked up?" Then the AddressChip selectable recovery row "1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas — Save it", a text button "Different address", and the caption "Only you will see this."
Recovery, nothing held anywhere (04b): keep the pre-save title. Body "We stopped holding that address. Type it again to save it." Then a blank, focused "Street address" field, the button "Save it" and the caption.
Storage error (05, web only): "We couldn't save that. Your browser blocked the storage we use to hold it." with "Try again"; the address stays shown.
Save failed (05b, all platforms): an InlineErrorRow under the address: "We couldn't save that. Try again." with "Try again"; the address stays shown.
Account switched (06): "This preview was started on a different account, so we didn't save it." Primary "Preview it on this account"; text button "Switch account". Saved-at-registration version of 06: "1107 NE Birchfield Ct is saved to the account that registered. We didn't save anything to this account." with primary "Switch account" and no "Preview it on this account".
Offline (07): the saved state from cache, with "You're offline · as of 6:04 PM". See Today and See your places stay enabled (your places open from cache). Claim this address is disabled with the reason "You're offline. Claiming needs a connection."
Home variant (Maya, HOME A, saves 1107 NE Birchfield Ct): body "Today keeps using your home, 2418 NE Larkspur Loop." Primary "See your places"; tertiary "See Today"; no Claim button.
Chosen-place variant (Jordan had picked Mom's house with Use for Today): body "Today still uses Mom's house, the place you chose."
Viewed-location variant (Today runs on a location he looked at recently that is not a saved place): body "Today still uses the location you looked at recently." Pinned twin: "Today still uses the location you pinned."
Duplicate: the AddressChip duplicate variant showing only its message "You already saved this as “Mom’s house”" (its inline action hidden); primary "Use for Today"; if it is already Today's place, primary "See Today".

LAYOUT & VISUALIZATION: A title that switches between two states, with one small tick glyph in primary.700 at body size beside the saved title, and nothing more. Show the address once, as a single line under the title: not a card, and not repeated in the body. Stack the three actions full width in strict weight order: filled primary, outlined secondary, plain-text tertiary. "Only you will see this." is a caption under the stack, never a second paragraph. 01-pre-save is the host's existing before state; it appears only when the person arrives without having already asked to keep the address, for example in the native launch funnel before its Keep tap. The recovery frames keep the pre-save title and swap only the body, so a lost address reads as "pick it or type it", not an error page: no error red, no warning glyph, no illustration. The held row always wins; the blank field appears only when nothing is held anywhere. When data is missing, the address line never goes blank; it falls back to a recovery frame.

INTERACTION, MOTION & HAPTICS: Save swaps the title with a cross-fade of 200ms or less; the tick appears still, with no animated check. iOS and Android give one light haptic tick on the saved state. Saving disables the actions and shows "Saving…" only if the save takes 1s or longer. "Save it" on the held row saves in one tap and lands on 03-saved. "Different address" swaps the row for the field in place. See Today with no session (for example a mail app's in-app browser) opens Today after sign-in and keeps the saved address. With Reduce Motion on, every swap is instant.

FOUNDATIONS COMPONENTS USED: AddressChip (selectable recovery row; duplicate variant with its inline action hidden; always paired with the ScopeChip sentence) · ScopeChip (sentence form "Only you will see this.") · InlineErrorRow (save-failed variant, value kept) · OfflineNotice with FreshnessLine (offline variant).

ACCESSIBILITY: The saved confirmation, "Saving…" and "Email confirmed." are role=status, announced without moving focus. On arrival from an email link, focus starts on the title. Reading order: status line, title, address, sentence, See Today, Claim this address, its caption, See your places, scope caption. The tick is decorative; the title carries the meaning. The held row is one element with a 44pt / 48dp / 44px target that reads "Save 1107 NE Birchfield Ct, Camas". Buttons are 44pt / 48dp / 44px. A disabled Claim stays focusable and reads its reason. At AX5 the address and sentence wrap, and nothing truncates.

EDGE CASES: The longest address, "12808 NE Lacamas Shores Rd, Unit 204, Camas, WA 98607", wraps to two lines. An address outside Clark County adds the layer line under the address. An already-saved address shows the duplicate variant. A mail app's in-app browser with no cookies still lands on 03-saved, never on a sign-in page; See Today there goes through sign-in and keeps the address. A confirm after the hold expired lands on 04a or 04b, never on 03-saved. A slow save never shows a full-page spinner. A save failure keeps the address and offers Try again. A claimed-home user gets the home variant. A person with a chosen place, or whose Today runs on a viewed or pinned location, gets the matching "still uses" body. A different signed-in account gets 06, which must visibly refuse to save; in saved-at-registration mode its only primary is Switch account.

INSTEAD OF:
- Instead of confetti, an animated check, a full-bleed illustration or "Congratulations", draw one still tick and one factual sentence — because a quiet acknowledgement is what people trust.
- Instead of "Set up a Home" as primary, keep See Today primary and Claim this address secondary — because Today is where the value is, and claiming is optional.
- Instead of a field when the server or this device holds the address, draw the one-tap held row — because nobody should retype what we hold.
- Instead of landing on the pre-save Save button after sign-in or registration, land on the saved state — because the person already asked to keep the address.
- Instead of a notification ask or "Turn on reminders" here, say only what changed — because permission is asked later, after a pickup day is confirmed.
- Instead of dead-end error pages for recovery or account switch, keep the title and give one clear next action — because the person is one tap from done.
- Instead of wording that implies a home was created or anyone was told, say "Saved privately" and "Only you" — because a saved place grants nothing and nobody else sees it.
- Instead of "Today now uses this address" when a chosen place, a home, or a viewed or pinned location stays in charge, name what Today still uses — because the sentence must be true.

DONE WHEN: Someone who registered on a laptop and confirmed on a phone sees "Saved privately" with the address and taps See Today, with nothing to retype and no second Save tap. The one sentence names what changed, truthfully. There is no celebration and no permission ask. The recovery frames look like the happy path, not like errors, and the email project's confirmed landing matches 03-saved exactly.

THE ONE JOB: Keep the looked-up address safe across the confirm-your-email gap, and let the person finish on whichever device they are using.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: The eye lands first on the headline "Check your email", then on the sentence saying the address is already saved, with the address chip beneath it, then on the code field. The single primary action is "Confirm email".

CONTENT:
The headline stays "Check your email".
Saved at registration (default wherever the sign-in provider allows it): under the headline, "Saved privately. Confirm your email to keep your account." Chip: the AddressChip default state, "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with "Camas, WA 98607", with no hold message, followed by "Only you will see this."

text:
Use the Pantopus house style pasted above and the Foundations components (boards 00a–00d), by exact name.

SCREEN: Today · f1-today-tab

TYPE: EXTENSION of the existing designed screen "Today". This screen already exists in the Pantopus design system. The attached screenshot is exact. Keep everything and change only what is listed. What changes: three screens are called Today today (the Today tab, Place › Today, and a briefing screen that only a push can open). Merge them into ONE composition per platform. Reuse the existing cards as drawn. Change only their order, when they show, and their states.

ATTACH: (1) the current Today tab on web /app/today at 1440 and 390, on iOS and on Android; (2) web Place › Today (/app/place/today): its "Next 14 days at this address" card and its "Good day to…" tiles move into this tab; (3) the iOS briefing screen opened from a push; (4) exports of the Foundations boards 00a–00d.

PLATFORMS & VIEWPORTS: iOS 393×852 (primary; large title "Today"). Android 412×915 (Material 3 top app bar). Web 1440×900: left sidebar and one centred content column 720 wide, so the reading order stays the same. Web 390×844 with the bottom tab bar. Draw artboards 01, 02, 04, 13, 14, 19, 20, 21 and 22 as full-length scrolls at their platform width (as tall as the content), with a dashed line at the fold. Draw all other artboards at their platform viewport: iOS 393×852, Android 412×915, web 1440×900 and 390×844. The web and Android dense frames (16–18) may also be drawn full-length with a dashed fold line.

WHERE IT LIVES & HOW PEOPLE ARRIVE: the Today tab, second of Place · Today · Nearby · Mail. Entry points:
- The tab itself: bottom bar (phones, web 390) or left sidebar (web 1440). Web URL /app/today. /app/place/today (including ?rule=…) redirects here with its query intact.
- A briefing push: pantopus://hub-today?deliveryId=…&kind=morning|evening. The evening briefing (6:00 PM) carries pickup and next-day items; the morning briefing (7:00 AM) carries date items. Either one opens this tab, hands over the delivered items, fills the pinned slot by rule (b) below, and highlights the matching section.
- An air or NOAA alert push: pantopus://today?section=air&src=alert. It fills the pinned slot for Today's place. An alert for a different saved place lands on the air band screen (f1-today-air-band) for that place, not on this tab.
- A widget tap: pantopus://today?src=widget&section=pickup|strip|air. Content already on screen stays; Today scrolls to that section and highlights it once.
- A date reminder push: pantopus://today?rule=… or /app/today?rule=…. Today scrolls to that row in the 14-day card (f5 draws the row), then the DateSheet opens in view mode. If the date is outside the 14 days, the link opens the place file's Dates row instead (x-place-file); Today is not the landing. A removed date shows "That date was removed." as a status line under the 14-day card's summary.
- "See Today" on the save confirmation. Today arrives warming, and the location row already shows the new saved place.
- The first open after claiming an address or joining a household shows a one-time notice.
- Removing the last saved place returns here in the no-place state. A briefing push tapped after its place was removed also lands in the no-place state.
Out of Today: the location-row chip opens Your places. FirstWeekRow scrolls to and highlights the control that holds its step. Strip rows and "+ Add a date" open the DateSheet. "Add a place" opens the add-place sheet. The one-time claim notice opens the claim receipt.

WHO AND WHEN: At 6:10 PM Mon 19 Oct, Maya Chen opens Today at HOME A before she wheels the carts out. Jordan Lee opens Today at PLACE B out of habit with notifications never turned on; nothing is due tomorrow there. (Delta) For this project Jordan saved PLACE B on Sat 17 Oct, 2 days before TODAY, so he is inside the 7-day first-week window; artboard 03 replays his first open seconds after saving.

THE ONE JOB: In one scroll, read everything happening at this address today, and see that a quiet day really was checked.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: first the location row (address, ScopeChip, FreshnessLine). Second, the pinned slot if it is filled; at a new saved place, FirstWeekRow "Next: set your pickup day →", the one next step. Third, the PickupCard (or QuietDayReceipt), then the 14-day card. Today is for reading, so it has no page-level primary button. The only action is the one inside the top card, or FirstWeekRow during the first week.

CONTENT (fixtures plus these deltas):
- HOME A location row: "2418 NE Larkspur Loop" · ScopeChip "Your household" · "Updated 4m ago". PLACE B: "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" · "Saved place · Only you".
- PickupCard at HOME A, as f4-today-pickup-card draws its confirmed variant: "Recycling and garbage tomorrow" · "Bins out tonight — curbside by 6:30 AM" · "You · Tuesday · Waste Connections" with the you-added mark.
- 14-day card, as f5 draws it: "Next 14 days: 4 items" (Tue 20 pickup, Mon 26 statewide voter bar, Tue 27 garbage only, Sun 1 Nov HOA dues added by Sam). Artboards 04 and 05 use f5's 6-item strip (f5 artboard 02: "Next 14 days: 6 items", which adds the Tue 20 bulk pickup and Maya's renters-insurance row).
- Weather (delta): "54°F · Dry tonight · Rain from Wed morning" · "National Weather Service · Portland forecast office · updated 5:45 PM".
- Air, as f1-today-air-band draws it: section title "Air quality index (AQI)", AqiBand detail "AQI 42 · Good · PM2.5", the EPA Good statement, "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM".
- Alerts: none, so the section takes no space.
- Ranked signal (delta): KindGlyph property-tax · "Pay property tax, 2nd half" · "in 14 days · due Mon 2 Nov" · detail "For property owners in Clark County · moved from Sat 31 Oct" · "Clark County Treasurer · county-wide". The mark follows the seeded rule's confidence: draw it official only because this project assumes the seed was checked against the Treasurer; an unchecked seed shows the hollow mark.
- Tile (delta): "Good day to clear the gutters — dry until Wednesday".
- Briefing opt-in card at HOME A: the morning row reads "7:00 AM · Change" and the night-before row reads "6:00 PM · Change". At PLACE B it has never asked (artboard 02) or was declined (artboard 06).
- PLACE B only: FirstWeekRow "Next: set your pickup day →" and QuietDayReceipt, each CheckItem with its source time: "weather 5:45 PM · air 7:00 AM · alerts 6:00 PM · your calendar 6:00 PM". The gutters tile shows, and the property-tax signal shows below the receipt: it is a heads-up 14 days out, below the push threshold, so it does not cancel the all-clear.
- Alert variant: AQI 118, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, crossed at 4:00 PM, Maya's threshold 101.
- Worst case (artboard 04): the full label "2418 NE Larkspur Loop, Vancouver, WA 98684" wraps to two lines beside the chip and "Updated 2h ago", with the pinned alert, the PickupCard and f5's 6-item strip below.

LAYOUT & VISUALIZATION: Draw this vertical order, the same at every tier and on every platform:
1 location row · 2 pinned slot · 2b FirstWeekRow (first 7 days only; zero height when complete or hidden) · 3 PickupCard (on a quiet day, QuietDayReceipt takes this slot) · 4 14-day card · 4b keeper slot (phase 2; zero height in this project, and hidden whenever an alert is pinned) · 5 weather · 6 AqiBand · 7 alerts · 8 ranked signals · 9 "Good day to…" tiles · 10 briefing opt-in card.
Each section title is an accessibility heading. A section appears or vanishes with its data, and the sections that stay never move. Claiming an address must read as "the chip changed, and any household sections appeared". Whenever a place exists, the 14-day card never disappears.
The pinned slot holds at most one card, in this precedence for every arrival type:
(a) An active air or NOAA crossing at Today's place: the AqiBand widget-micro variant (name and number beside the track, no text on fills) with "Air quality index (AQI) 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups", "Crossed 101 at 4:00 PM · AirNow" and "See air quality ↓". A NOAA crossing uses the same form: "Wind advisory until 10:00 PM Tue" · "National Weather Service · Portland forecast office" · "See alerts ↓".
(b) On a briefing-push arrival, list only the delivered items that are NOT in the first viewport, headed "From your 6:00 PM briefing · Also:" (morning: "From your 7:00 AM briefing · Also:") with one "↓" line each, each scrolling to and highlighting its row. Highlight any delivered item that is already in the first viewport in place; never repeat it in the slot. If every item is in the first viewport, the slot takes no space.
(c) The one-time claim or join notice, drawn with LandingBannerSlot geometry.
(d) Otherwise it takes no space.
Quiet day: draw a finished screen, not an empty state. Show the heading only when all four CheckItems are ticked.
Warming: for cold loads over 1s only, draw WarmingSkeleton section shapes at final height in slots 3–6. Each fills in as its provider returns. While warming, the FreshnessLine under the address reads "Setting up Today for Birchfield Ct"; it becomes "Updated just now" once every provider has returned or timed out. After 10s, a provider that still hasn't returned becomes its InlineErrorRow ("We couldn't reach AirNow just now · Retry"); the others stay as they landed. FirstWeekRow shows during warming. Warm refresh: never skeleton or dim anything. The FreshnessLine reads "Updating…" then "Updated just now", with the hairline only if the refresh takes 1s or longer.
Hidden details (the address resolves but weather, air, alerts, signals and tiles are withheld): show the hidden-details line directly above slot 3, full width, in bodySmall text.strong on surface.sunken; the PickupCard (when pickup is tomorrow) and the 14-day card follow in their usual slots.
When data is missing: a failed provider gets an InlineErrorRow in its own slot. A refresh failure keeps the content. With no cache, show the error state. Offline, show cached content with OfflineNotice, and each disabled control carries its reason caption.
Signals never repeat a section's fact. Pickup appears once, as the PickupCard with its KindGlyph, never with a sparkle icon.

INTERACTION, MOTION & HAPTICS: On an arrival from a push, widget or reminder, scroll once to the target and highlight it with the DateRow highlighted wash (fades in under 300ms, then decays); accessibility focus moves there. If a push arrives while Today is open, show no banner; highlight the PickupCard, and the notification bell badge increments; nothing else changes.
FirstWeekRow: the step order is Save ✓ → Pickup day → Reminder or widget → One date or person. The row names only the next unfinished step, with no fraction. It is a whole-row link that scrolls to and highlights the control for that step: (1) pickup day: the PickupCard when it is on screen; otherwise the first "Pickup day" row's "Set your pickup day" button in the 14-day card (f5 draws it); (2) reminder: "Next: get a reminder the night before →" scrolls to and highlights the briefing opt-in card in slot 10, whose widget line covers the widget half; (3) date or person: "Next: add one date that matters →" highlights the 14-day card's "+ Add a date" row; at a claimed home the person half, "Next: add someone to your household →", opens the household block in the place file. At a saved place the person half is not offered and not counted; only steps reachable at the current tier count. The row shows for 7 days from the save and disappears when the reachable set is done or when hidden. Its separate 44pt text button "Hide this" collapses the row to InlineUndo "Hidden · Undo", stored on the server, kept until the person leaves Today; later sections move up once. A member who joined a household never sees FirstWeekRow.
Pull to refresh on native; its alternatives are Retry in the FreshnessLine and a "Refresh" accessibility action, and web refreshes on focus. Sections fill in with a 200ms cross-fade. Under Reduce Motion: jump-scroll without animation, a static highlight that clears on the next interaction, no shimmer. Today fires no haptics of its own (the PickupCard confirm has its own).

FOUNDATIONS COMPONENTS USED: ScopeChip (saved place; claimed home; person glyph + "Only you" on a private row), FreshnessLine (fresh, refreshing, warming, stale, failed, offline), OfflineNotice, WarmingSkeleton (section skeleton), QuietDayReceipt (Today full: all ticked, one pending, one failed; CheckItems with source times), InlineErrorRow (provider unreachable), PickupCard (confirmed incl. the named-person form, highlighted on arrival), FourteenDayStrip with DateRow (Today card), AqiBand (detail, alert, widget micro in the pinned slot), ProvenanceMark, SourceCaption, KindGlyph, FirstWeekRow (no-fraction variant; dismissed with InlineUndo), InlineUndo, NotificationAsk (card row: never asked, granted, declined), KeeperStrip (slot only, suppressed under an alert), LandingBannerSlot (one-time claim receipt banner variant, used in Today's pinned slot for both notices; the join notice wraps to two lines with "See your places" as the trailing 44pt action and a 44pt Close glyph labelled "Dismiss").

ACCESSIBILITY: Reading order follows the visual order. Each section title is an accessibility heading (web h2), so the VoiceOver rotor, TalkBack headings and web heading navigation jump between sections. The location row is one element, "2418 NE Larkspur Loop, visible to your household, updated 4 minutes ago", with custom actions "Open your places" and, when refresh failed, "Retry". On web, the chip and Retry stay separate 44px buttons after the address text. The receipt is read as "Checked: weather, air, alerts, your calendar". The pinned-slot card has role=status on appearance. On iOS the tab bar uses Large Content Viewer. All rows are whole-row targets of at least 44pt / 48dp / 44px, and "Hide this" is its own 44pt target. Retry reads "Retry air quality". The strip and the air band carry their own summary sentences. At AX5 the location row stacks (address, then chip, then freshness), text wraps, nothing truncates, and the 14-day card shows its summary sentence in place of the cells (the same proposal as f5's AX5 frame). In greyscale, marks read by shape and the AQI by its printed name and separators.

DONE WHEN: A new account that saved PLACE B sees weather, air, alerts, the seasonal tile and its calendar in the same order as HOME A, with its one next step above the fold. Artboard 13 differs from artboard 02 only by the chip, the notice, the missing FirstWeekRow step it finished, and any household sections. name: Next 14 days at this address (strip + rows)
job: See the next two weeks at this address as a shape, with every item's source and certainty visible without tapping.
attach: (1) the accepted f1-today-tab frames (ios 01-dense-home, web-1440, android) as the host; (2) the existing "Next 14 days at this address" card from web Place › Today and its iOS and Android calendar blocks; (3) exports of the Foundations boards 00a–00d.
text:
Use the Pantopus house style pasted above and the Foundations components (boards 00a–00d), by exact name.

SCREEN: Next 14 days at this address · f5-today-calendar-strip

TYPE: EXTENSION of the existing designed screen "Today" (a new card inside it). This screen already exists in the Pantopus design system. The attached screenshot is exact. Keep everything and change only what is listed. What changes: the address-calendar list card becomes a FourteenDayStrip card with DateRows beneath it. It sits directly below the PickupCard and above weather.

ATTACH: (1) the accepted f1-today-tab frames (ios 01-dense-home, web-1440, android) as the host; (2) the existing "Next 14 days at this address" card from web Place › Today and its iOS and Android calendar blocks; (3) exports of the Foundations boards 00a–00d.

PLATFORMS & VIEWPORTS: iOS 393 wide (primary), Android 412 wide, web 1440 (inside Today's 720 column), web 390. Draw each artboard full-length at its platform width: the location row, then the PickupCard collapsed to its top 64pt with a torn-edge marker (or omitted on days without one), then the whole card down to the scope sentence, then 24pt of weather. Put a dashed line at the platform fold (iOS 852, Android 915, web 900 and 844). Never shorten rows to fit.

WHERE IT LIVES & HOW PEOPLE ARRIVE: Today tab → slot 4 of Today. It is always present when a place exists. Entry points:
- Scrolling Today.
- A widget tap: pantopus://today?src=widget&section=strip. The card is scrolled into view and highlighted once.
- A reminder push for a date (pantopus://today?rule=… or /app/today?rule=…; /app/place/today?rule=… redirects here with its query). The row is highlighted and focused, then the DateSheet opens in view mode. If the date is outside the 14 days, the place file's Dates row is the landing instead (drawn in x-place-file). A removed date shows a status line (artboard 13).
- The place file year band's "this fortnight" link.
- FirstWeekRow on Today: "Next: add one date that matters →" scrolls here and highlights the "+ Add a date" row. "Next: set your pickup day →" (when no PickupCard is on screen) scrolls here and highlights the first "Pickup day" row's "Set your pickup day" button.
Out of this card: a row tap opens the DateSheet (view-mine or view-seeded). The row action "Where this comes from" swaps the sheet to the ProvenanceSheet content. "+ Add a date" opens the DateSheet in create mode. "Set your pickup day" opens the DateSheet in create mode with the Pickup day kind. Saving a date inside the window returns here with the new row highlighted; a date outside it returns here with the place-file status line under the summary.

WHO AND WHEN: At 6:10 PM Mon 19 Oct, Maya Chen checks what is coming at HOME A this fortnight: bins tomorrow, the voter deadline, garbage only next week, and the HOA dues Sam entered. Jordan Lee at PLACE B sees two hollow Thursday marks and the renters-insurance date he added, then taps "+ Add a date" to add his lease, which ends months away.

THE ONE JOB: See the next two weeks at this address as a shape, with every item's source and certainty visible without tapping.

FIRST FIVE SECONDS: first the strip's rhythm (Tuesday marks, the Mon 26 bar). Second, the first row, "Recycling and garbage · Tomorrow". Third, the legend. The only primary action is the "+ Add a date" row at the foot; at PLACE B, "Set your pickup day" is a secondary text button inside its row.

CONTENT (fixtures plus these deltas). Phase-1 kinds only in every artboard except 15. HOME A window Mon 19 Oct → Sun 1 Nov. Summary "Next 14 days: 4 items".
- Tue 20 Oct: "Recycling and garbage" · "Tomorrow" · "You · Tuesday · Waste Connections" · you-added. Two marks in the cell (garbage, recycling).
- Mon 26 Oct: "Register or update to vote: online or mail" · "in 7 days · must arrive by Mon 26 Oct" · "In person: until 8:00 PM Tue 3 Nov" · region chip "Statewide — WA" · "Washington Secretary of State · statewide · 2026 general election" · official. A bar fills the cell.
- Tue 27 Oct: "Garbage only" · "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct" · you-added. One mark.
- Sun 1 Nov: "HOA dues · $285" · "in 13 days · Sun 1 Nov" · "Repeats monthly" · (delta) entered by Sam: the you-added mark shape with the caption "Sam added this · 3 Oct".
- Many-items deltas (artboard 02, HOME A): Tue 20 Oct also holds "Bulk pickup — curbside by 6:30 AM" (official, "Waste Connections · Vancouver service area · 2026 calendar") and Maya's "Renters insurance renews — check the new premium" (you-added, "Repeats yearly"; its title wraps to two lines). The cell shows 3 marks and "+1". Summary "Next 14 days: 6 items".
- PLACE B window: Thu 22 Oct and Thu 29 Oct, title "Pickup day" · detail "Which bins go out isn't set yet" · "in 3 days · Thu 22 Oct" / "in 10 days · Thu 29 Oct" · "City of Camas · weekday only · 2026 calendar" · on record, not confirmed. The Thu 22 row carries the "Set your pickup day" button. Also the Mon 26 Oct bar, and (delta) Jordan's "Renters insurance renews" · "in 11 days · Fri 30 Oct" · "Repeats yearly" · you-added (a tick in the cell). "Next 14 days: 4 items".
- Saved-outside-window delta (artboard 14, PLACE B): Jordan saves "Lease ends" on Wed 31 Mar 2027. The card shows, under the summary, the status line "Saved · Lease ends Wed 31 Mar 2027 is in your place file · See it"; "See it" opens the place file's Dates row. No row is added to the card.
- Holiday specimen (delta, PLACE B viewed Mon 23 Nov 2026, window Mon 23 Nov → Sun 6 Dec): "Thanksgiving — moved to Fri 27 Nov · City of Camas 2026 calendar". The Thu 3 Dec pickup row shows the reported state: "You reported this · checking".
- County specimen (delta, HOME A viewed Tue 20 Oct 2026 at 6:10 PM, window Tue 20 Oct → Mon 2 Nov, summary "Next 14 days: 5 items"): "Pay property tax, 2nd half" · "in 13 days · due Mon 2 Nov" · detail "For property owners in Clark County · moved from Sat 31 Oct" · region chip "Clark County" · "Clark County Treasurer · county-wide · 2026 tax year" · official. The Tue 20 pickup row reads "Recycling and garbage · Today" in the done style (text.secondary), and cell 1 has no tonight outline. The week-two label above cell 8 reads "Tue 27".
- Seeded civic rows take their mark from the rule's confidence. The voter and tax rows are drawn official only because this project assumes each seed was checked against its authority. An unchecked seed shows the hollow mark and the caption "… · not yet checked against the source".
- Empty specimen (delta): a new account whose only saved place is "Mom's place · Washougal, WA", with no seeded pickup rule, viewed Mon 9 Nov 2026 (window Mon 9 Nov → Sun 22 Nov); chip "Saved place · Only you"; footer "Only you will see this."
- Phase-2 specimen (artboard 15 only, labelled "Phase 2 (F10)"), viewed Tue 20 Oct 2026 at 6:10 PM (window Tue 20 Oct → Mon 2 Nov): "Clark Public Utilities · $142.18" · "in 3 days · Fri 23 Oct" · you-added (tick); "City of Vancouver water · $84.00" · "in 8 days · Wed 28 Oct" · you-added (tick); "Comcast · $79.99" · "in 13 days · Mon 2 Nov" beside the narrowed county bar. The Tue 20 pickup row reads as in the county specimen. Summary "Next 14 days: 8 items". Beside the frame, a state column: overdue, "Paid by Sam · 15 Oct", "A household bill is due" (redacted for a viewer without bill access), and the amount "$2,233.48" right-aligned in tabular figures.

LAYOUT & VISUALIZATION: The card is surface.base with radius lg and shadow sm. Top to bottom:
1. Header: "Next 14 days at this address" in overline style, with the summary caption in text.secondary under it. One status line at a time sits under the summary (removed date, or saved outside the window), as a polite status, never a modal.
2. Strip: 14 equal cells across the content width. On iOS that is about 23.5pt pitch, 2pt gaps and cells 56pt tall. "Today" sits above cell 1 and the week-two date ("Mon 26") above cell 8. A weekday initial sits beneath each cell. Each cell is surface.sunken with a 1.5px text.secondary baseline along its bottom edge; weekend cells use the same fill at 50% opacity, with the baseline and marks at full ink; the S S initials carry the meaning. The instrument skeleton has no baselines and no initials, so ready or empty cells never read as loading.
3. Marks: each cell stacks up to 3 XS ProvenanceMarks (12pt) top-down in one ink, text.secondary. A cell draws one mark per pickup stream and one per other row, in row order, pickup streams first. "+N" in text.strong counts the marks not drawn; the summary counts rows. Shape is the only per-mark code. Kind is carried by the KindGlyph on the rows. Each kind uses its own KindGlyph from Foundations (including lease ends, notice deadline, insurance renews, warranty ends, HOA dues, property-tax), never a generic calendar icon. A combined pickup day has two marks and a garbage-only day has one.
4. Region rule: a statewide or county rule is a full-height ink bar filling its cell (cell width minus 6pt, radius xs) with no mark inside. When that day also has address items, the bar narrows to 4pt at the cell's left edge and the marks sit to its right. Draw this narrowed form in context in artboard 15, and as a 4× cell callout beside artboard 05. The bar reads as "a whole region", never as a claim about this house.
5. Tonight's pickup: the cell for tomorrow's pickup (cell 2 on Mon 19) gets a 1.5px text.primary outline, an emphasis, never a banner.
6. Holiday move: the mark sits on the moved day. The usual day shows a struck ghost ring at 50% opacity. The row carries the caption.
7. Pickup marks after the last published city calendar (Dec 2026) use the projected style. Record this on Notes only; it is outside every drawn window.
8. Legend line under the strip, once, with S marks: "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this".
9. DateRows in date order, each at least 56pt. Annual or self-entered rows (HOA dues, renters insurance, a pickup schedule the person set) get a 2px identity.home left rule plus their recurrence caption; seeded city pickup rows never get the rule. At a claimed home, a date the viewer kept private shows the ScopeChip person glyph plus "Only you" at the end of its SourceCaption line. A seeded pickup row whose frequency is Not set carries a visible 44pt text button "Set your pickup day" under its caption (first such row only; later rows offer it in their actions). The button opens the DateSheet in create mode with the Pickup day kind selected and Thursday prefilled. The same action appears in that row's custom actions and in its view-seeded DateSheet. The region chip on civic rows uses the DateRow region-chip slot: ScopeChip pill geometry with a map-region glyph (never the person or house glyph), spoken "applies across Washington" / "applies across Clark County", never "Visible to …". It is not a visibility chip.
10. Foot row: "+ Add a date" (at least 44pt, primary.700), with the scope sentence under it.
When data is missing: empty after a successful check shows drawn empty cells with their baselines, then "Checked — nothing in the next 14 days", then "+ Add a date". A failure draws no strip; an InlineErrorRow sits in the card. The card shows its own FreshnessLine only when the calendar is older than the rest of Today ("Calendar updated 2h ago · Retry calendar"). Otherwise the location row covers freshness.

INTERACTION, MOTION & HAPTICS: On native, cells are not targets. The whole strip is one adjustable element. iOS: swipe up or down to move a day, then double-tap to scroll to that day's first row and highlight it. Android TalkBack: the strip is one focusable node with a state description and the custom actions "Next day" / "Previous day". A plain tap on the strip scrolls to the rows. Web 1440: cells share the content width (about 47px each with 2px gaps, never under 44px), and only cells that hold items are buttons; each moves focus to its first row. The focus ring is a 2px border.focus ring with a 2px offset, distinct from the 1.5px tonight outline and from the highlight wash. Web 390: the strip is decorative and the rows carry everything. A row tap opens the DateSheet. Every row action is reachable without gestures: inside the DateSheet (Remind me, Mark done, Edit, and a "Where this comes from" row that swaps the sheet's content with a Back control, never stacking a second sheet). Screen readers also get them as custom actions: Edit, Remind me, Where this comes from, Mark done; seeded rows drop Edit, and an unset seeded pickup row adds "Set your pickup day". On web 1440 each row also has a 44px overflow button with the same actions. On a push or widget arrival, scroll once, fade in the DateRow highlighted wash in under 300ms, let it decay, and move focus to the row. Cells fill with a 150ms cross-fade when data lands. Under Reduce Motion: static highlight, no shimmer. Haptics: none here; the DateSheet save carries the one light tick.

FOUNDATIONS COMPONENTS USED: FourteenDayStrip (Today card; ready, empty, loading, stale, permission-denied, saved place, error, highlighted row), DateRow (pickup, deadline, holiday moved, money row in artboard 15 only; states default, highlighted, done, permission-hidden, unchecked seed, reported · checking, private at a home), KindGlyph (row 24pt), ProvenanceMark (XS in cells, S in rows and legend; reported variant), SourceCaption (short form), ScopeChip (footer sentence form; person glyph + "Only you" on a private row; the civic region chip is the DateRow slot above), QuietDayReceipt (strip empty, with the string below), WarmingSkeleton (instrument skeleton), InlineErrorRow, FreshnessLine (stale, offline), OfflineNotice, LockedActionRow (names who can act), DateSheet (create, view-mine, view-seeded), ProvenanceSheet.

ACCESSIBILITY: Reading order: header, summary, status line, strip, legend, rows, add row. Strip label: "Next 14 days: 4 items. Next: Recycling and garbage, tomorrow." Days are spoken as "Tuesday 20 October: Recycling and garbage, your household's schedule, you added this", "Thursday 22 October: Pickup day, City of Camas schedule, on record, not confirmed" or "Friday 23 October: nothing". Initials are never spoken. Each row is one element, e.g. "Register or update to vote, online or mail, must arrive by Monday 26 October, in 7 days, applies across Washington, Washington Secretary of State, official", "Pay property tax, 2nd half, due Monday 2 November, in 13 days, applies across Clark County, Clark County Treasurer, official" and "HOA dues, 285 dollars, Sunday 1 November, in 13 days, added by Sam". The "Set your pickup day" button is its own 44pt target after its row. The status lines use role=status. Marks are at least 12pt with a 1.5px stroke and 3:1 contrast in light and dark; the cell baseline is at least 3:1 against base. Rows wrap and never truncate. AX proposal: at AX3 and above, the cells give way to the summary sentence and the rows become the table; f1's AX5 frame uses the same fallback. Greyscale: every distinction is shape, count, bar, baseline or outline.

COPY: "Next 14 days at this address" · "Next 14 days: 4 items" · "Today" · "Tomorrow" · "Tonight" · "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct" · "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this" · "+ Add a date" · "Set your pickup day" (delta) · "Only you will see this." (saved place) · "Everyone in this household will see this." (home) · "Only you" (private row at a home) · "Statewide — WA" · "Clark County" · "Register or update to vote: online or mail" · "must arrive by Mon 26 Oct" · "In person: until 8:00 PM Tue 3 Nov" · "Pay property tax, 2nd half" · "For property owners in Clark County · moved from Sat 31 Oct" · "Thanksgiving — moved to Fri 27 Nov · City of Camas 2026 calendar" · "You reported this · checking" · "not yet checked against the source" · "Sam added this · 3 Oct" · "You marked this done" · "Checked — nothing in the next 14 days" (use this here even if the Foundations board shows "two weeks"; the research brief uses 14 days) · "Saved · Lease ends Wed 31 Mar 2027 is in your place file · See it" (delta) · "That date was removed." · "We couldn't load your calendar just now" (delta) · "Retry calendar" · "Calendar updated 2h ago · Retry calendar" (delta) · "You're offline · as of 4:10 PM" · "Adding a date needs a connection." (delta) · "Maya can add dates here." (delta) · "Pickup day" · "Which bins go out isn't set yet" (delta) · "City of Camas · weekday only · 2026 calendar" (delta) · "Repeats monthly" (delta) · "Repeats yearly" (delta).

EDGE CASES: Long titles wrap to two lines beside the glyph. Many items: more than 3 marks on one day show "+N" in the cell, and every item still gets a row. Zero items: the empty specimen. A date saved beyond the window: the place-file status line, never a silent toast. Slow network: the instrument skeleton reserves the final height and holds no text. Offline: the cached strip, the location row's "You're offline · as of 4:10 PM", and "+ Add a date" and "Set your pickup day" disabled with their reason. Permissions: by default a member such as Sam can add dates. A member whose calendar editing the owner turned off (or a Guest) sees rows but no add row, and a LockedActionRow names who can act. A viewer without bill access sees phase-2 money rows redacted. A saved place shows "Only you will see this." and never uses household words. At a home, the add-row sentence states the DateSheet's default ("Everyone in this household will see this."); the DateSheet lets the person keep a date to "Only you", and such rows show the private caption (f1 artboard 13 draws it). The voter row never states or implies registration status. Its "Mark done" is person-scoped ("You marked this done", Only you), and the household never sees it. The tax appeal never shows as a single seeded date; it is a conditional rule in the DateSheet and the place file. Camas has no Saturday bulk pickup.

INSTEAD OF:
- Instead of four class-coloured dots, draw one-ink marks told apart by shape — because hue alone fails greyscale and 3:1.
- Instead of 14 tappable cells on phones, make the strip one element and the rows the targets — because 23pt cells are below 44pt and 48dp.
- Instead of a dot, or a ScopeChip with a house glyph, for the voter deadline, draw a full-height bar and a region chip with a map glyph — because either would read as a claim about this house.
- Instead of "in 11 days" alone, write "in 11 days · Fri 30 Oct" — because people act on deadlines by the date.
- Instead of an even Thursday rhythm through Thanksgiving week, draw the moved mark and a struck ghost — because the usual day is wrong that week.
- Instead of an empty strip when loading fails, draw no strip and a named Retry — because drawn empty cells with baselines mean "checked, nothing found".
- Instead of a toast that vanishes after saving a far-off date, show the "is in your place file · See it" status line — because a saved date must never disappear from view.
- Instead of a seeded pickup row that only opens a locked sheet, draw the "Set your pickup day" button in the row — because the first-week step needs a visible path.
- Instead of a "+ Date" header toggle, keep "+ Add a date" as the last row — because a list gets a list row, not a mode switch.

DONE WHEN: The hollow and tick marks are told apart in the cells at 1x in greyscale and dark (artboards 20 and 22), and the filled and tick marks in artboard 02. All three shapes are told apart in the rows and the legend. The Mon 26 bar cannot be read as a household fact. Empty, loading and error look clearly different; artboards 07 and 08 differ by baselines, initials and the receipt line even with the text covered. Every row beyond tomorrow shows its relative count, weekday and date, and every relative count matches its artboard's viewing date. Maya's confirmed Tuesdays show ticks, and combined days differ from garbage-only days. The PLACE B frame shows the hollow city weekday, the "Set your pickup day" button and an "Only you" footer. A reminder arrival lands on the exact row with focus. A date saved outside the window is still visibly findable. No phase-1 artboard shows a bill. No row is compressed below 56pt.

ARTBOARDS:
